dervis-irab:4-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْجَوارِحِ): the beasts of prey among animals and birds that catch game, such as the dog and the eagle.
(مُكَلِّبِينَ): «المكلّب» is a passive participle of «كلّب», i.e. one of these hunting animals that has been set upon game and trained to seize prey. Because training is most often done with the dog (كلب), the word was derived from its name, since it predominantly applies to it.

* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ ماذا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ): a resumptive clause introduced to answer their question: what has been made lawful for them? (يسألونك) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). As for (ماذا), it has already been stated that we have two ways of parsing it: either we take «ماذا» as a whole as an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the clause (أحل لهم) as its khabar (predicate); or we take «ما» as an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and «ذا» as a relative noun, its khabar, with the clause (أحل لهم) as the ṣila (relative clause). The interrogative clause is in the position of the second object of (يسألونك). They have stated explicitly that the verb of asking is suspended from governing (taʿlīq), even though it is not one of the verbs of the heart, because it is a cause of knowledge; just as knowing is suspended, so is its cause.
(قُلْ: أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّباتُ): the clause (قل) is resumptive; the clause (أحل لكم الطيبات) is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); (لكم) is attached to (أحل), and (الطيبات) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(وَما عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is a relative noun conjoined to (الطيبات); the clause (علمتم) is the ṣila; (من الجوارح) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). Concerning the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) there are two views: first, the relative noun «ما»; second, the omitted pronoun referring back to the relative noun, i.e. «علمتموه».
(مكلبين) is a ḥāl from (علمتم). It conveys that teaching requires complete expertise and utmost ability, and that the learner must take knowledge from its competent masters.
Some have permitted the wāw to be resumptive and «ما» to be a conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) being (فكلوا); this is an acceptable parsing.
(تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ): the clause (تعلمونهن) is a second ḥāl, or resumptive; (مما) is attached to (تعلمونهن); the clause (علمكم الله) is the ṣila. The second objects of (علمتم) and (تعلمونهن) are omitted, the implied form being: «وما علمتموه طلب الصيد لكم لا لأنفسهن، تعلمونهن ذلك» (and what you have taught to seek game for you, not for themselves, teaching them that).
(فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ, implying an omitted condition), or it links the apodosis according to the second parsing; (مما) is attached to (كلوا); the clause (أمسكن) is the ṣila of «ما»; (عليكم) is attached to (أمسكن).
(وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the clause is conjoined to the clause (فكلوا). The clause (فكلوا) has no grammatical position, or it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ): conjoined to what precedes; (إن) with its noun and its predicate.

dervis-irab:5-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حِلٌّ): a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "lawful" (حلال); hence it is not put in the dual or plural.
(مُحْصِنِينَ): chaste; those who have guarded themselves through marriage and have not aspired to fornication, neither in deed nor in intent.
(أَخْدانٍ): plural of «خِدْن» (with kasra on the khāʾ), a secret companion; it applies to both masculine and feminine.

* I'rab:
(الْيَوْمَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّباتُ): resumptive speech introduced to repeat the mention of the good things made lawful for you on the day you asked about them, or on the day in which your religion was perfected for you. It has also been said: it is not a specific day. (اليوم) is an adverb of time attached to (أحل); (أحل) is a past verb in the passive; (لكم) is attached to (أحل); and (الطيبات) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(وَطَعامُ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ حِلٌّ لَكُمْ وَطَعامُكُمْ حِلٌّ لَهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; (طعام) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذين) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أوتوا) is a passive past verb with its deputy agent; (الكتاب) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). (حل) is the khabar (predicate) of (طعام); (لكم) is attached to (حل); and (وطعامكم حل لهم) is conjoined to what precedes.
(وَالْمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِناتِ وَالْمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; (المحصنات) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. «حلّ لكم» (lawful for you). (من المؤمنات) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المحصنات). (والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم) is conjoined to what precedes, and (من قبلكم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(إِذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسافِحِينَ وَلا مُتَّخِذِي أَخْدانٍ): the adverb (إذا) is attached to the omitted «حل». (آتيتموهن) is a past verb, its agent and its first object; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. (أجورهن) is a second object; (محصنين) is a ḥāl, and (غير مسافحين) a second ḥāl; (ولا متخذي أخدان) is conjoined to (مسافحين).
(وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالْإِيمانِ فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; (يكفر) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (بالإيمان) is attached to (يكفر); the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (حبط عمله) is a verb and its agent; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis form the khabar of «من».
(وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (في الآخرة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (من الخاسرين) is attached to the omitted khabar of «هو».

dervis-irab:6-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَرافِقِ): plural of «مِرْفَق» (with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the fāʾ), or «مَرْفِق» (with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the fāʾ); it is the joint between the forearm and the upper arm (the elbow). He used the plural for it and the dual for «الكعبين» because a person has one elbow in each arm, so it was fitting to mention it in the plural in relation to all of them; the opposite is true of the two ankles, for the two «كعبين» are the two bones protruding from the two sides of the foot, so it was fitting to mention the two of each leg. Another reason is that the plural of «مرفق» is a familiar word in speech, whereas the plural of «كعب» is a word whose mention in speech is not free [of awkwardness] «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «لا يخلو ذكره في الكلام» (whose mention is not free); it may be a misprint for «لا يحلو» (is not pleasant)]», since it is pluralised as «كعاب», «كعوب» and «أكعب»; this is a matter whose reference is to taste alone.
(الْغائِطِ): low-lying, sunken ground; here it is meant as relieving oneself, as will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its parsing has already been given.
(إِذا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to set out the rulings of ablution (wuḍūʾ) for performing the obligatory prayer, which is the greatest act of obedience after faith. (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached to His saying (فاغسلوا); the clause (قمتم) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (إلى الصلاة) is attached to (قمتم); the fāʾ is linking; the clause (اغسلوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; and (وجوهكم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرافِقِ): (وأيديكم) is conjoined to (وجوهكم). (إلى) is a preposition indicating the meaning of limit and end in absolute terms; whether [the limit] is included in the ruling or excluded from it is a matter that turns on the evidence. Among cases where there is evidence of exclusion is the saying of the Exalted: «فنظرة إلى ميسرة» (then a deferral until ease), because hardship is the reason for the deferral, and with the arrival of ease the reason disappears; if ease were included in it, he would be waiting in both states, in hardship and in ease. Likewise «ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل» (then complete the fast until the night): if the night were included, continuous fasting (wiṣāl) would be obligatory. Among cases where there is evidence of inclusion is your saying: "I memorised the Quran from its beginning to its end," because the statement is made about memorising the whole Quran. From the Quran is: «سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى» (Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque), and it is known that he was not taken to Jerusalem without entering it. His saying, the Exalted:
«إلى المرافق» and «إلى الكعبين» contain no evidence for either of the two, so the scholars took the more cautious course and ruled that they are included in the washing. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَامْسَحُوا بِرُؤُسِكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes.
There has been much disagreement about this bāʾ. Some said it is redundant (zāʾida); others said it denotes the partitive (tabʿīḍ), as in the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فلثمت فاها آخذا بقرونها ... شرب النزيف ببرد ماء الحشرج
(I kissed her mouth, holding her locks, as the parched one drinks of the cool water of the pebbly hollow.)
Badr al-Dīn ibn Mālik said: in it there is support for the school of al-Shāfiʿī on wiping part of the head. Muḥibb al-Dīn Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī rejected that. Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn al-Qarāfī said: when you say "I wiped with the napkin," "I wrote with the pen," and "I circumambulated the House," it is known that you did not wipe with the whole napkin, nor write with the whole pen, nor circumambulate the whole House, top and bottom, outside and inside; rather you wiped with part of this, wrote with part of that, and circumambulated the outside of that. Ibn Hishām and al-Zamakhsharī chose that the bāʾ is for adhesion (ilṣāq): both the one who wipes part of it and the one who covers it entirely with wiping are attaching the wiping to his head. Mālik and Aḥmad took the cautious course and made covering [the whole head] obligatory; al-Shāfiʿī took what is certain and made obligatory the least to which the name "wiping" applies; and Abū Ḥanīfa took the explanation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, namely what is reported that he wiped over his forelock, and he estimated the forelock as a quarter of the head. We have lengthened this discussion only because of its novelty and the exercise it gives the mind. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (امسحوا); further discussion of it will come.
(وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ): Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, al-Kisāʾī and Yaʿqūb read:
«وأرجلَكم» with fatḥa, i.e. "and wash your feet up to the ankles," these being the two bones protruding at the joint of the shank on both sides. The rest — Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamza and Abū ʿAmr — read it with the genitive, and the apparent sense is that it is conjoined to «الرأس», i.e.:
"and wipe your feet up to the ankles." «[Translator's note: in the standard transmissions Shuʿba from ʿĀṣim also reads the genitive; the author lists only these three.]» From here the Muslims differed over washing or wiping the feet. The great majority of Ahl al-Sunna hold that what is obligatory is washing alone; the Shīʿa and the Imāmiyya hold that it is wiping. Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī and al-Nāṣir li-l-Ḥaqq of the Zaydiyya said: combining both is obligatory. Ibn Jarīr held combining the two views out of caution. They explained its being placed later in the accusative reading by saying that pouring water is a likely occasion for blameworthy, forbidden extravagance, so it was conjoined to the third, the wiped [limb], not so that it be wiped but to draw attention to the obligation of moderation in pouring water over them. They have gone to great lengths in derivation and interpretation, to a length for which this book has no room; it arises from a passion for verification and for reaching what is most beneficial and safest. For this reason Ibn Jarīr inclined to combining [them], and in that there is a great deal of good intention and soundness of heart.
(وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُباً فَاطَّهَّرُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is kāna with its noun, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (جنبا) is the khabar (predicate) of (كنتم); and the clause (اطهروا) is the apodosis.
(وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى أَوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ أَوْ جاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغائِطِ أَوْ لامَسْتُمُ النِّساءَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is the protasis, the tāʾ being its noun and (مرضى) its khabar; (أو) is a conjunction; (على سفر) is attached to an omitted second khabar of (كنتم); (جاء) is conjoined to (كنتم); (أحد) is the fāʿil (agent) of (جاء); (منكم) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (أحد); (من الغائط) is attached to (جاء); (أو) is a conjunction; and (لامستم النساء) is conjoined to what precedes.
(فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا ماءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيداً طَيِّباً): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (لم تجدوا) is likewise conjoined; (ماء) is the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause (فتيمموا صعيدا) is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; (طيبا) is an adjective.
(فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ مِنْهُ): conjoined to what precedes; (منه) is attached to (امسحوا).
(ما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ حَرَجٍ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to set out the wisdom behind the laws of the religion. (ما) is negative; (يريد الله) is a verb and its agent; the lām is causal (taʿlīl); (يجعل) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām; the implied «أن» and the imperfect verb form an interpreted maṣdar, the object of (يريد). The verb «الجعل» is either in the sense of bringing into being and creating, in which case it takes one direct object, (عليكم) being attached to it, (من) a redundant preposition, and (حرج) genitive in form and accusative in position as the object of (يجعل); or it is «الجعل» in the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr), in which case (عليكم) is the second object.
(وَلكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), here inoperative because it is lightened; (يريد) is an imperfect verb whose agent is «هو»; the lām is causal; (يطهركم) is accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يريد). (وليتم نعمته عليكم) is conjoined to it; (لعل) with its noun; the clause (تشكرون) is in the position of nominative as its khabar; and the clause of hope is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (kināya) in the saying of the Exalted: «أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط». Coming from the «غائط» — which is sunken or low-lying ground — is a metonymy for ritual impurity (ḥadath), following the custom of the Arabs: when one of them wished to relieve himself, he would go to a low-lying place and relieve himself there.

* Benefits:
The verse of ablution contains important benefits that must not be overlooked; we point to them in what follows:
1- With «وأرجلكم» the pattern of paucity (jamʿ qilla) suffices in place of the pattern of multitude (jamʿ kathra), because no pattern of multitude is used for it. Some patterns of paucity may suffice in place of the pattern of multitude, either by original coinage or by usage, relying on context. Al-Shāṭibī laid down a fine rule, which we summarise as follows: «The reality of [sufficing by] coinage is that the Arabs did not coin one of the two patterns, making do with the other; and [sufficing by] usage is that they coined both, but in some places made do with one instead of the other. The first:
is like «أرجل», plural of «رجل», «أعناق», plural of «عنق», and «أفئدة», plural of «فؤاد». The Exalted said:
«وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين», «فاضربوا فوق الأعناق» (so strike above the necks), «وأفئدتهم هواء» (and their hearts are void); here the pattern of paucity sufficed in place of the pattern of multitude, because no pattern of multitude was coined for them. The second: like «أقلام».
2- There is no doubt that whoever is commanded by another to wipe his head has complied by doing what can truly be called wiping. There is nothing in the language requiring that in such an act the whole head must be wiped. So it is with all transitive verbs, such as: "strike Zayd," or "stab him," or "stone him": the meaning is realised when the striking, stabbing or stoning falls on one of his limbs. No one among the people of the language, or anyone learned in it, would say that one is not a striker unless the striking falls on every part of Zayd; and so too stabbing, stoning and all other verbs.
3- The Exalted said: «إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة», and concerning major impurity (janāba): «وإن كنتم مرضى» «[Translator's note: so in the text; the clause about major impurity in the verse is «وإن كنتم جنبا»]», because «إذا» is used for what exists or is awaited without fail, while «إن» is used for a matter that may or may not happen. Standing for prayer is constant, while major impurity is not constant, for it may occur and may not. For this reason the exegetes have customarily explained «إذا قمتم» as "when you intend to stand," by putting the effect in place of the cause: standing is caused by the intention, and the intention is its cause.
4- Among the novel discussions is the scholars' disagreement about whether the elbow is included in the washing. One group said: the elbow is included in what is named "hand," because the hand extends from the fingertips to the armpit. This is refuted by your saying: "I slept last night until its middle," and it cannot be said that he slept the whole night. The majority held that the elbows are washed with the hands, while Mālik and Zufar said washing the elbows is not obligatory. «[Translator's note: so in the text; the view that the elbows are not included is usually attributed to Zufar, and to some Mālikīs, rather than to Mālik himself.]» This disagreement also concerns the ankles. The argument of Zufar is that «إلى» is for the end of the limit, and the end-point is other than the extremity, so washing the extremity is not specifically required. The reply is from two angles:
a- The first is the view of al-Zajjāj. He said: let us grant that the elbow need not be washed; but «المرفق» is a name for what lies beyond the tip of the bone, for it is the place on which one leans (yartafiqu), i.e. reclines. And there is no dispute that what lies beyond the tips of the bone need not be washed.
b- The second: the limit of a thing may be separate from what it delimits, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل», for the day is perceptibly separate from the night; and it may not be separate, as in your saying: "I sell you this cloth from here to here." This limit is not separate. There is no doubt that the distinction between the elbow and the forearm is not a definite separation; that being so, requiring washing up to one point is no more appropriate than requiring it up to another, so it is necessary to hold that the whole elbow is washed.
Some said: the end is other than what is ended, and washing the elbows was not understood from the noble verse but only from his action ﷺ. On this basis, if you said:
"I sell you [the land] from this tree to this tree," the limit is not included here.
And if you say: "I sell you from this wall to this wall," the two walls are included in the sale. The difference between them is that in the first the limit is of the same kind as what it enters, so it is excluded from it; and likewise the elbow is of the same kind as the hand, so it is excluded from the washing.
In the second, the limit is external, because the wall is not of the same kind as the orchard; for this reason the two walls are included in the sale. Do you not see that in the saying of the Exalted «ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل», since the night is of a different kind from the day, the entry of the beginning of the night was taken into account? He ﷺ said: «When the day withdraws from here and the night approaches from here, the fasting person has broken his fast.» So the entry of the night was taken into account because it is external to the day.
«[Translator's note: the reasoning in this last paragraph is reproduced as printed; the same-kind / different-kind criterion appears to be applied in the reverse of the usual way (normally a limit of the same kind is included and one of a different kind is excluded).]»

dervis-irab:42-42.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السحت), with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ or with it vowelless: the unlawful, and whatever earnings are foul and ugly so that disgrace attaches to them, such as bribery; the plural is أسحات. The Jews used to take bribes for their judgements. You will see a short account of it in the section on Benefits. Among the wonders of the sīn and the ḥāʾ, when they are the first and second radicals of a word, is that they denote dragging and far-reaching effect; سحب ذيله فانسحب ("he dragged his train and it trailed") is the mother of this group.
Among the figurative usages of speech: سحبت الريح أذيالها ("the wind trailed its skirts"), وانسحبت فيها ذلاذل الريح ("the hems of the wind trailed in it"), and اسحب ذيلك على ما كان مني ("draw your skirt over what came from me", i.e. overlook it). They say: "A man never preserves his companion's affection by anything like drawing the skirt over his faults." The root of السحت has preceded. One says: سحت الشحم من اللحم, he peeled the fat off the meat; and فلان مسحوت المعدة, "so-and-so is greedy", a colloquial expression that is also correct Arabic; سحجت الرياح الأرض, the winds stripped off what was on the surface of the earth; سحّ الماء, he poured the water; and سحّ المطر والدمع, the rain and the tears poured down. The meaning of dragging and sliding in all this is not hidden. سحره ("he bewitched him") is well known, and إنه لمسحّر, "he has been bewitched time after time until his mind is deranged". لقيته سحرا وسحرة, "I met him at dawn". جاء فلان بالسحر من القول, "so-and-so came with magic in speech", i.e. he captivated minds; from this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «إن من البيان لسحرا» ("Truly, some eloquence is magic"). In this way this root runs consistently and never departs from this meaning, and this is one of the wonders.

* I'rab:
(سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ): سماعون is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are سماعون"; the clause is resumptive, brought to reinforce what preceded it or to prepare for what follows. للكذب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سماعون», and likewise أكالون للسحت. (فَإِنْ جاؤُكَ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ أَوْ أَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to set out some of what follows from these rulings. إن is conditional; جاءوك is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is an imperative/request clause; احكم is an imperative verb, and بينهم is an adverb attached to «احكم»; أو is a conjunction of choice, and أعرض is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «احكم»; عنهم is attached to «أعرض»; and the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (وَإِنْ تُعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ فَلَنْ يَضُرُّوكَ شَيْئاً): the wāw is conjunctive, إن is conditional, and تعرض is the protasis, passive (mabnī lil-majhūl) [Translator's note: so in the source; تُعْرِضْ is in fact active, "you turn away"]; عنهم is attached to تعرض; the fāʾ links the apodosis; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and future; يضروك is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by لن, the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (وَإِنْ حَكَمْتَ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ): the wāw is conjunctive, إن is conditional, and حكمت is a past verb and its fāʿil, in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ links the apodosis; احكم is an imperative verb and بينهم an adverb attached to it; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; بالقسط is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being just". (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ): inna and its noun, and the clause يحب المقسطين is its khabar; the clause is resumptive, giving the reason.

* Benefits:
Al-Ḥasan narrated: When one of the Children of Israel brought a bribe to the judge among them, he would put it in his sleeve and show it to him; so he would listen to him and not look at his opponent; thus he would eat the bribe and listen to falsehood. It is related that a governor came back from his post, and his people came to him; he set before them the gifts he had brought back and began telling them what had happened to him. A Bedouin among the people said: "We are as Allah the Exalted said: «سمّاعون للكذب أكّالون للسحت»." And in the ḥadīth: «كل لحم أنبته السحت فالنار أولى به» ("Every flesh grown from unlawful earnings, the Fire is more fitting for it").

dervis-irab:43-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ): a relative adjective (nisba) formed from الرب ("the Lord"), contrary to the regular pattern. One also says ربّيّ with kasra on the rāʾ, and ربوبيّ with fatḥa on the rāʾ. We shall give the best-known nouns that come as relative adjectives contrary to the regular pattern in the section on Benefits. The رباني is the devout worshipper.
(الْأَحْبارُ): the jurists; its singular is حبر, with fatḥa or kasra. Al-Farrāʾ said: the kasra is more eloquent. It is taken from التحبير, embellishing and beautifying, for they embellish and adorn it. The الحبر الأعظم among the Christians is the successor of the Lord Christ on earth, and among the Jews the chief of the priests.

* I'rab:
(وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ): resumptive speech, brought to express wonder at their making someone they do not believe in, nor in his Book, their judge, even though it is the truth, as stated in their own Book in which they claim to believe. كيف is an interrogative of wonder in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); يحكمونك is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is circumstantial; عندهم is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), and التوراة is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the wāw in يحكمونك. (فِيها حُكْمُ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ وَما أُولئِكَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ): فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar, and حكم الله is the delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of التوراة. ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay, and يتولون is conjoined to يحكمونك. The benefit of conjoining with ثم, which denotes delay, is to indicate how deep-rooted their turning away and aversion are and their persistence in turning away from the ruling after long reflection and after the appearance of the signs proving the truth of the arbitration [Translator's note: the source has «عن الحكم الطويل، بعد التأمل الطويل»; the first الطويل appears to be a slip, and it is rendered as "the ruling"]. من بعد ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتولون, or a ḥāl. The wāw is conjunctive or resumptive; ما is the Ḥijāzī negative ما; the demonstrative is indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of a nominative as its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and المؤمنين is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of «ما». (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْراةَ): resumptive speech, brought to show the loftiness of the Torah, the height of its rank, and the obligation to observe its rulings. inna and its noun, and the clause أنزلنا is its khabar; التوراة is a mafʿūl bihi. (فِيها هُدىً وَنُورٌ يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا): the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of التوراة; فيها is attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; هدى is the delayed mubtadaʾ, and نور is conjoined to هدى. The clause يحكم بها النبيون is resumptive, showing the exalted status of the Torah, and you may make it a second ḥāl of التوراة. بها is attached to يحكم; النبيون is the fāʿil of يحكم; الذين is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause أسلموا is the ṣila (relative clause). (لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبارُ بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِنْ كِتابِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يحكم, and the clause هادوا is the ṣila; the meaning is: they judge by it among themselves. They may also be attached to أنزلنا, or to an omitted naʿt of هدى and نور. الربانيون and الأحبار are conjoined to «النبيون»; «بما استحفظوا» is attached to يحكم, and من كتاب الله is attached to استحفظوا; استحفظوا is a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ما may be maṣdariyya or a relative noun, and His saying «من كتاب الله» may be attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَكانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَداءَ): conjoined to «استحفظوا»; the wāw is the noun of كان, عليه is attached to شهداء, and شهداء is the khabar of كانوا. (فَلا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ وَاخْشَوْنِ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), i.e. "if you know this, then do not fear people"; لا is prohibitive; تخشوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the wāw is the fāʿil, and الناس is the mafʿūl bihi. In اخشون the wāw is conjunctive; اخشون is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ of the first person is the mafʿūl bihi. (وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِآياتِي ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا): conjoined to what preceded; لا is prohibitive; تشتروا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لا; بآياتي is attached to تشتروا, the bāʾ entering on what is given up, as has been established; ثمنا is a mafʿūl bihi and قليلا a naʿt. (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكافِرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, so that the ruling is general: everyone who takes a bribe and judges by other than the ruling of Allah has disbelieved. من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; لم is a particle of negation, of shifting (to the past) and of the jussive; يحكم is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لم, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بما is attached to يحكم, and the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila. In فأولئك the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, هم is a second mubtadaʾ, and الكافرون is the khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is one of the arts of rhetoric whose path is subtle; few notice it, because its import is deep, and none fathom it except the inspired, whose souls have been illumined by the light of certainty and inspiration. None of the scholars of rhetoric before has given it a chapter of its own, but it falls within the thread of iṭnāb (amplification) in the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿānī). It occurs in His saying in describing the prophets: «الذين أسلموا» ("who had submitted"). It is known that submission (islām) is among the elementary things whose existence is presupposed in the prophets, and in it they are equal to the least of their individual followers. But just as one may intend to magnify the one described by a great attribute, one may intend to magnify the attribute by its great bearer. If you say: "I read a poem by al-Mutanabbī the poet", you do not mean to praise al-Mutanabbī for being a poet, for this attribute, great as it is, does not distinguish him, since the least of poets is described by it; rather you praise poethood in that this great poet is counted among those who bear it. For this reason the one who said in praise of the Prophet ﷺ did supremely well:
فلئن مدحت محمدا بقصيدتي ... فلقد مدحت قصيدتي بمحمد
(If I have praised Muḥammad with my poem, I have in truth praised my poem through Muḥammad.)
Otherwise, if we restricted it to praise, as al-Zamakhsharī and others have stated, we would depart from the familiar law of rhetoric, which is ascending from the lower to the higher. How then would this agree with what came in the Qur'an if the purpose were not to praise the attribute by its bearer? Do you not see that Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī himself slipped from the highest station of eloquence in his saying:
شمس ضحاها هلال ليلتها ... درّ تقاصيرها زبرجدها
(The sun of its forenoon, the crescent of its night; the pearl of its short necklaces, its chrysolite.)
For he descended from the sun to the crescent and from the pearl to the chrysolite, and for this reason the early critics reproached him for this small flaw.

* Benefits:
The rules of the relative adjective (nisba) are set out at length in the books of grammar, but there are many frequently used nouns that go against the rules of nisba, so we wished to give the most commonly used of them for the man of letters to learn by heart. We have made a list of some of these nouns, arranged in alphabetical order:
أنافي: relating to a big nose (أنف).
أموي: relating to أمية (Umayya).
بهرانيّ: relating to بهراء, a tribe of Banū Quḍāʿa whose dwellings were in the plain of Ḥimṣ, and which professed Christianity like its neighbours Tanūkh and Taghlib.
بدوي: relating to بادية (the desert).
بحراني: relating to البحرين (Baḥrayn).
تهامي and تهام: relating to تهامة (Tihāma).
ثقفي: relating to ثقيف (Thaqīf).
جذميّ: relating to جذيمة (Jadhīma).
جلولي: relating to جلولاء (Jalūlāʾ), a town in Iraq on the road to Khurāsān, where the Arabs defeated the army of the Sasanian king.
حروري: relating to حروراء (Ḥarūrāʾ), a place in Iraq not far from Kūfa, where the first Khārijites gathered when they openly revolted against ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who fought them and wiped them out at the battle of al-Nahrawān.
حرميّ: with kasra on the ḥāʾ, relating to الحرمين, i.e. the two mosques of Makka and Madīna.
حضرميّ: relating to حضرموت (Ḥaḍramawt).
دهريّ, with ḍamma on the dāl: relating to دهر.
ديرانيّ: relating to دير (a monastery).
روحانيّ: relating to روح (spirit).
رباني: relating to رب (Lord).
رقباني: relating to one with a great neck (رقبة).
رديني: relating to ردينة; it is the spear, and Rudayna was a woman famed for straightening spears.
سليقي: relating to سليقة (natural disposition).
شآم: relating to الشام (Syria).
شعراني: relating to one with much hair (شعر).
صدراني: relating to one with a big chest (صدر).
صنعاني: relating to صنعاء (Ṣanʿāʾ).
طائيّ: relating to طيّء (Ṭayyiʾ).
عبديّ: relating to بني عبيدة (Banū ʿAbīda).
عبشمي: relating to عبد شمس (ʿAbd Shams).
عبدريّ: relating to عبد الدار (ʿAbd al-Dār).
يمان: relating to اليمن (Yemen).
عبدلي: relating to عبد الله (ʿAbd Allāh).
فرهوديّ: relating to فراهيد (Farāhīd).
قرشي: relating to قريش (Quraysh).
كنتي: relating to كنت.
لحياني: relating to one with a big beard (لحية).
مروزي: relating to مرو (Marw).
نباطي: relating to الأنباط (the Nabataeans).
ناصري: relating to الناصرة (Nazareth).

dervis-irab:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(وَكَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيها أَنَّ النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ وَالْعَيْنَ بِالْعَيْنِ وَالْأَنْفَ بِالْأَنْفِ وَالْأُذُنَ بِالْأُذُنِ وَالسِّنَّ بِالسِّنِّ): the wāw is conjunctive; كتبنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the verb is conjoined to «أنزلنا». عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كتبنا, and the pronoun in «عليهم» refers to those who are Jews (الذين هادوا). فيها is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the pronoun refers to the Torah. أنّ and its noun; بالنفس is attached to its omitted khabar (predicate); and أنّ with what follows it is to be interpreted as an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of كتبنا, because the writing falls upon it, i.e. "the killing of the soul for the soul", i.e. it is killed for the soul. والعين بالعين is conjoined, i.e. "the gouging out of the eye for the gouging out of the eye", "the cutting off of the nose for the cutting off of the nose", "the cutting off of the ear for the cutting off of the ear", and "the pulling out of the tooth for the pulling out of the tooth".
In one reading these four are in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. (وَالْجُرُوحَ قِصاصٌ): also conjoined. It has also been read in the nominative. What is meant by the wounds is that in which a decisive ruling cannot be made, and I hold that the nominative is preferable in الجروح, so that «قصاص» is its khabar; the details are in the long works. (فَمَنْ تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَهُ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; تصدق is a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); به is attached to تصدق; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); هو is a mubtadaʾ and كفارة the khabar; the nominal clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, a mubtadaʾ; لم is a particle of negation, of shifting (to the past) and of the jussive; يحكم is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لم, and it is the protasis; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحكم, and the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila (relative clause). In فأولئك the fāʾ links the apodosis; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, هم a second mubtadaʾ, and الظالمون its khabar; the nominal clause «هم الظالمون» is the khabar of أولئك; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

dervis-irab:46-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قَفَّيْنا): قفّى means "he came"; قفى فلان زيدا وبزيد means "he made him follow him". One says: قفّيت على أثره بفلان, i.e. "I made so-and-so follow him".

Between Abū Ḥayyān and al-Zamakhsharī:
A fine discussion arose between al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān, of which this is the summary. Abū Ḥayyān said that قفينا is made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of جئنا, i.e. "then We brought, upon their traces, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, following them". The doubling in «قفينا» is not for making the verb transitive, because «قفا» is transitive to one object; Allah the Exalted said: «ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم» ("And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge"). You say قفا فلان الأثر when he follows the trace. If the doubling were for transitivity, it would be transitive to two accusative objects, and the construction would be: ثم قفينا على آثارهم عيسى بن مريم, with عيسى the first object and آثارهم the second object. Rather it is made to include the meaning of «جاء» and made transitive with the bāʾ, and it reaches «آثارهم» with على. This is the summary of what Abū Ḥayyān said. He dwelt at length on this question in order to refute al-Zamakhsharī's analysis, for al-Zamakhsharī said, in his own words — what al-Zamakhsharī says:
«قفيته is like عقبته, when you make him follow. Then one says قفيته بفلان and عقبته به, making it transitive to the second object by adding the bāʾ. If you say: where then is the first object in the verse? I say: it is omitted, and the adverbial phrase, «على آثارهم», as it were stands in its place, because when He makes him follow upon his trace, He has made him follow him.»

Abū Ḥayyān's digression:
Abū Ḥayyān went further in refuting al-Zamakhsharī and said: His words need interpretation. That is because he made the doubled «قفيّته» mean «قفوته», so that «فعّل» would be in the sense of «فعل», as in قدّر الله and قدر الله, which is one of the meanings for which «فعّل» comes. Then he made it transitive with the bāʾ; and making a verb that is transitive to one object reach a second object by the bāʾ is rarely found, so that some even claimed that it does not occur and is not permissible: so for طعم زيد اللحم one does not say أطعمت زيدا باللحم. The correct view is that it has come, but rarely. You say دفع زيد عمرا ("Zayd pushed ʿAmr"), then make it transitive with the bāʾ and say دفعت زيدا بعمرو, i.e. "I made Zayd push ʿAmr". Likewise صكّ الحجر الحجر ("the stone struck the stone"), then you say صككت الحجر بالحجر, i.e. "I made it strike it". As for his saying that the first object is omitted and the adverbial phrase as it were stands in its place, this is not sound, because the object is an explicit mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and an adverbial phrase does not stand in its place.
Until he says: and al-Zamakhsharī's saying «فقد قفى به إياه» separates the pronoun, whereas it should properly be attached.

* I'rab:
(وَقَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ): resumptive speech, brought to begin setting out the rulings of the Gospel after setting out the ruling of the Torah. قفينا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); على آثارهم and بعيسى are attached to (mutaʿalliq) قفينا; ابن مريم is a badal (substitute) or a naʿt (adjective); مصدقا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); لما is attached to «مصدقا»; بين يديه is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, which is «ما»; and من التوراة is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَآتَيْناهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدىً وَنُورٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; آتيناه is a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and الإنجيل is a second mafʿūl bihi; فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); هدى is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and نور is conjoined to هدى; the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. (وَمُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ): مصدقا is conjoined to the position of the clause, so it has the status of an accusative as a ḥāl; لما is attached to «مصدقا»; بين يديه is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; and من التوراة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَهُدىً وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive, and هدى is conjoined, in line with «مصدقا», so both are accusative as ḥāl.
Some permitted them to be two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose), but this is far-fetched because of the presence of the wāw. موعظة is conjoined to هدى, and للمتقين is attached to an omitted naʿt. (وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْإِنْجِيلِ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ): the wāw is conjunctive and the lām is the lām of command; يحكم is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; أهل الإنجيل is the fāʿil of يحكم, and بما is attached to يحكم. In one of the seven readings: «وليحكم», making the lām one of purpose, with يحكم an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of purpose, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to آتينا or to قفينا [Translator's note: the source writes the reading with the same letters «وليحكم»; the variant meant is وَلِيَحْكُمَ, with kasra on the lām and the verb in the accusative]. فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحكم. (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ): the i'rab of this clause has been repeated, and the repetition conveys the meaning of emphasis.

* Rhetoric:
1- al-tashbīh al-balīgh (the eloquent simile): the likening of the Gospel to light and guidance, with the particle of comparison omitted so that they are the Gospel itself, for hyperbole.
2- Repetition: in the clauses, for added emphasis, as has preceded.

dervis-irab:83-84.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ): the wāw is resumptive, and it may also be conjunctive, so that the clause is conjoined to His words «لا يستكبرون». إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause سمعوا is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as the adverb is put in construct with it; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أنزل has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); and إلى الرسول are attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل. (تَرى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ترى is an imperfect verb, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you" (أنت); أعينهم is the object of ترى, which is the verb of visual seeing; the clause تفيض is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and من الدمع is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification). More explanation of this i'rab will come in the section on rhetoric. (مِمَّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تفيض; the clause عرفوا is the ṣila; and من الحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (يَقُولُونَ: رَبَّنا آمَنَّا فَاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): the clause يقولون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «عرفوا», namely the wāw, or from the genitive pronoun in «أعينهم»; the ḥāl may come from the muḍāf ilayhi here because the muḍāf is a part of it. It may also be resumptive, brought to answer an implied question, as if it were said: "So what is their state on hearing the Qur'an?" ربنا is a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf); آمنا is a verb and its agent, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); فاكتبنا: the fāʾ is resumptive, and اكتبنا is an imperative verb and its direct object, with the agent latent; and مع الشاهدين is an adverb attached to اكتبنا. (وَما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَما جاءَنا مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); لنا is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause لا نؤمن بالله is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; بالله is attached to نؤمن; ما is conjoined to الله; the clause جاءنا has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; and من الحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَنَطْمَعُ أَنْ يُدْخِلَنا رَبُّنا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الصَّالِحِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; نطمع is an imperfect verb whose agent is "we" (نحن); أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نطمع; ربنا is the agent; and the adverb مع القوم الصالحين is attached to يدخلنا. The whole clause is conjoined to the clause نؤمن. The wāw may also be circumstantial (ḥāliyya), with the clause in the accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor (majāz) in the overflowing of the eyes, the relationship being fullness.
2- Hyperbole in the tamyīz, which is one of the most eloquent constructions, because the intensification in it rises through three degrees: the first is "the tear of his eye overflowed" (فاض دمع عينه); the second is in converting the agent into a tamyīz; and the third is in presenting the tamyīz in the form of a cause (taʿlīl), so that alongside specification it conveys causation. Speech with causation is farther from the original than speech with tamyīz only because, in such cases, the tamyīz is established as having originally been an agent, as in طاب محمد نفسا ("Muhammad was pleased in soul") and اشتعل الرأس شيبا ("the head blazed with white hair"). So when you say فاضت عينه دمعا ("his eye overflowed with tears"), this origin is understood, given the habitual usage in its like; but with causation, that is not something customary.

dervis-irab:85-86.t:
* I'rab:
(فَأَثابَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما قالُوا جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; أثابهم is a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الله is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is conjoined to the clause قالوا آمنا. بما is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أثابهم; the clause قالوا is a ṣila (relative clause). The reward is coordinated with their saying «آمنا» because saying, when joined with sincere action, is faith. جنات is a second direct object of أثابهم, because it contains the sense of giving; the clause تجري is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري; and الأنهار is the agent of تجري. (خالِدِينَ فِيها وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «أثابهم»; فيها is attached to خالدين; the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and جزاء المحسنين its khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the accusative as a ḥāl, or resumptive. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا): the wāw is resumptive; الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause كفروا is a ṣila; كذبوا is conjoined to كفروا — denial is coordinated with disbelief because lying is a kind of it; and بآياتنا is attached to كذبوا. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; أصحاب الجحيم is the khabar of the demonstrative; and the clause is the khabar of الذين.

dervis-irab:87-88.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّباتِ ما أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ): resumptive speech, brought to address some of the believers who had agreed upon austerity and monasticism, wearing wool and turning away from permitted pleasures, and to forbid them from that.
لا is prohibitive; تحرموا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); طيبات is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause أحل is a ṣila (relative clause); الله is the agent; and لكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أحل. (وَلا تَعْتَدُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تعتدوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لا; and the clause is conjoined to the clause لا تحرموا. The meaning of transgression here is going beyond the lawful to the unlawful. إن and its noun; the clause لا يحب المعتدين is its khabar (predicate); and the clause إن الله etc. is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (وَكُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلالًا طَيِّباً): the wāw is conjunctive; كلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; مما is attached to كلوا; the clause رزقكم الله is the ṣila of the relative; and حلالا is a direct object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun or from its omitted referring pronoun, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "an eating that is lawful" (أكلا حلالا). The first is simplest. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; اتقوا is an imperative verb conjoined to كلوا; الله is its object; الذي is an adjective of الله; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); به is attached to «مؤمنون»; and the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative.

dervis-irab:89-89.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اللغو) of oaths: that which falls away and to which no ruling attaches. There is a juristic disagreement about it: according to al-Shāfiʿī it is what comes from a person without intent, such as his saying:
"No, by Allah" (لا والله) and "Yes, by Allah" (بلى والله); according to Abū Ḥanīfa it is to swear about something one believes to be so, when it is not as one thought.
(عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمانَ): it was read with a doubled consonant (tashdīd) and without it, and it was also read:
«عاقدتم». The binding (taʿqīd) of oaths is their confirmation by intent and resolve. Al-Farazdaq put this meaning into verse: it is related that al-Ḥasan was asked about the inadvertent oath while al-Farazdaq was with him, and he said: "Let me answer for you, O Abū Saʿīd," and recited:
ولست بمأخوذ بلغو تقوله ... إذا لم تعمّد عاقدات العزائم
(You are not held to account for idle words you say, so long as firmly bound resolves did not intend them.) That is: you are not taken to task for idle speech that falls away. تعمّد is originally تتعمد, one of the two tāʾs having been dropped; and عاقدات العزائم means the firm, decisive resolves; and attributing the requital to them is a rational metaphor (majāz ʿaqlī).
(فَكَفَّارَتُهُ): the expiation (kaffāra) is the act whose function is to "cover" (takfīr) the sin, i.e. to conceal it.

* I'rab:
(لا يُؤاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمانِكُمْ): resumptive speech establishing the ruling on inadvertent oaths. لا is negating; يؤاخذكم الله is an imperfect verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a fāʿil (agent); باللغو is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يؤاخذكم; and في أيمانكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلكِنْ يُؤاخِذُكُمْ بِما عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمانَ): the wāw is conjunctive; لكن is inoperative (muhmala); بما: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما is maṣdariyya, which together with عقدتم is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤاخذكم; and الأيمان is the direct object. (فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعامُ عَشَرَةِ مَساكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ ما تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa ("disclosing") fāʾ, i.e. "if you break what you have bound by oaths"; it is thus the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. كفارته is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the pronoun refers back to the breaking of the oath (al-ḥinth) understood from the implied condition, as has been stated. Al-Zamakhsharī held that it refers back to the relative ما, and a muḍāf must then be implied, i.e. "the expiation of breaking it". There are other views which we have passed over because they are far-fetched. إطعام is the khabar (predicate); عشرة مساكين is muḍāf ilayhi; من أوسط is attached to an omitted adjective of عشرة مساكين; ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause تطعمون is the ṣila (relative clause), and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. تطعمونه — that is, neither the highest nor the lowest; and أهليكم is the object of تطعمون.
(أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ): conjoined to طعام [Translator's note: the text reads «طعام»; the word in the verse is «إطعام».], and likewise تحرير رقبة. (فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of tense] and jussive; يجد is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links its apodosis; and صيام is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is fasting", or "his expiation"; and ثلاثة أيام is muḍāf ilayhi. (ذلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمانِكُمْ إِذا حَلَفْتُمْ): the clause is explicative; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; كفارة is the khabar; أيمانكم is muḍāf ilayhi; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to the omitted apodosis, indicated by what precedes it; and the clause حلفتم is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa). (وَاحْفَظُوا أَيْمانَكُمْ كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آياتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; احفظوا is an imperative verb and its agent; أيمانكم is the direct object; كذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or ḥāl; يبين الله is an imperfect verb and its agent; لكم is attached to يبين; آياته is the direct object; لعلكم: لعل and its noun; the clause تشكرون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is circumstantial.

dervis-irab:90-91.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصابُ وَالْأَزْلامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطانِ)
Resumptive speech to show that wine and gambling are not included among the good things that Allah has made lawful. إنما is [إنّ with] the restraining mā (kāffa and makfūfa); الخمر is a mubtadaʾ (subject); الميسر, الأنصاب and الأزلام are conjoined to it; رجس is the khabar (predicate); and من عمل الشيطان is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رجس, or it is a second khabar of الخمر. (فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa ("disclosing") fāʾ; اجتنبوه is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لعل and its noun; the clause تفلحون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِنَّما يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطانُ أَنْ يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ): resumptive speech giving further clarification of the reasons leading to the prohibition of the two.
إنما is kāffa and makfūfa; يريد الشيطان is an imperfect verb and its agent; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the object of يريد; بينكم is an adverb attached to يوقع or to an omitted ḥāl; العداوة is the direct object; البغضاء is conjoined to العداوة; في الخمر is attached to an omitted ḥāl; and الميسر is conjoined to الخمر.
(وَيَصُدَّكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنِ الصَّلاةِ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; يصدكم is conjoined to يوقع; عن ذكر الله is attached to يصدكم; عن الصلاة is also attached to يصدكم; the fāʾ is resumptive; هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is a command; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; and منتهون is the khabar.

dervis-irab:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثاقَهُ الَّذِي واثَقَكُمْ بِهِ): the wāw — the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to remind the believers of His favours upon them and of His covenant by which He bound them. (اذكروا نعمة الله) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نعمة); (ميثاقه) is conjoined to (نعمة الله); (الذي) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ميثاق); and the clause (واثقكم به) is the ṣila (relative clause).
(إِذْ قُلْتُمْ سَمِعْنا وَأَطَعْنا): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (واثقكم); the clause (قلتم) is in the position of genitive by annexation; the clause (سمعنا) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause (وأطعنا) is conjoined to it.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): resumptive speech. (اتقوا الله) is an imperative verb, its agent and its object; the clause of (إن) and what falls within its scope is causal (taʿlīliyya). (ذات الصدور) means the matters hidden in the breasts.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَداءَ بِالْقِسْطِ): resumptive speech, introduced to begin setting out matters concerning what passes between them and others. (كونوا) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, the wāw its noun and (قوامين) its khabar (predicate); (لله) is attached to (قوامين); (شهداء) is a second khabar of (كونوا); and (بالقسط) is attached to (شهداء).
(وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلى أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (يجرمنكم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the kāf is the direct object; (شنآن قوم) is the agent; (على) is a preposition, and (أن) with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by (على); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يجرمنكم), because it contains the meaning of «لا يحملنكم» (let it not drive you).
(اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوى): the clause (اعدلوا) is explicative; (هو) is a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), referring to the maṣdar understood from His saying «اعدلوا»; (أقرب) is the khabar, and the clause is resumptive; (للتقوى) is attached to (أقرب).
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): the parsing of its like has been given shortly before.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrīr) in demanding justice; the secret in it is emphasising justice and arousing longing for it. The gist of the meaning: let not your hatred of the polytheists drive you to abandon justice so that you transgress against them. This is the utmost that the highest ideals and the loftiest human values can reach.

dervis-irab:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): resumptive speech introduced to set out His promise, Glorified is He, for the human soul is by nature inclined to ask for an explanation of this promise. (وعد الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الذين) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the ṣila.
(لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ): (لهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (مغفرة) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause may be explicative of the omitted second object of the verb «وعد», whose implied form is «الجنة» (Paradise); or it may be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), as though He said: a people have a promise; and it was asked: what is it that He promised them? So He said: for them is forgiveness and a great reward. On this view too it has no grammatical position.
You may also make it the object of an omitted verb of saying, which contains additional confirmation of what was promised and emphasis on its occurrence. It has also been said: it is a clause in the position of accusative as the second object of His saying «وعد», in the sense: He promised them that for them is forgiveness, or He promised them forgiveness. So the clause stood in the place of a single word and dispensed with it.
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ): the wāw is resumptive; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila, and the clause (كذبوا بآياتنا) is conjoined to the ṣila; (أولئك) is a second mubtadaʾ; (أصحاب الجحيم) is the khabar of (أولئك); and the nominal clause is the khabar of (الذين).
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its parsing has been given many times.
(اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): its parsing has been given shortly before; the clause is resumptive.
(إِذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أَنْ يَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ): (إذ) is an adverb for the favour, attached to it; it may also be attached to (اذكروا). The clause (همّ قوم) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (أن يبسطوا) is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «همّ»; (إليكم) is attached to (يبسطوا); and (أيديهم) is the direct object.
(فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; (اتقوا الله) is a verb, its agent and its object; (على الله) is attached to (يتوكل); the fāʾ is resumptive and the lām is the lām of command; (يتوكل) is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command; and (المؤمنون) is the agent.

* Rhetoric:
"Stretching out the hand" is an expression of loose metaphor (majāz mursal) whose relation is causality, because the hand is the cause of harm; just as "stretching out the tongue" is a metaphorical expression whose relation is causality.

dervis-irab:12-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَقِيباً): the «نقيب» of a people is the one who investigates their conditions and looks into their affairs. It is of the pattern «فعيل» in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil), derived from «التنقيب», which is searching.
From it is the saying of the Exalted: «فنقّبوا في البلاد» (and they searched through the lands). He is so called because he searches into the conditions and secrets of the people. It has also been said that it is in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl), as though the people chose him knowingly. It has also been said that it is for intensiveness, like «عليم» and «خبير».
(عَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ): you supported them. In al-Mukhtār: «التعزير» is honouring and exalting.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): resumptive speech introduced to mention some of what issued from the Children of Israel; in it is an urging of the believers to remember the favour of Allah and to observe the right of the covenant, and a warning against breaking it. The lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (أخذ الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (ميثاق) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (بني إسرائيل) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(وَبَعَثْنا مِنْهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيباً): (بعثنا) is conjoined to (أخذ); (منهم) is attached to «نقيبا», or is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اثني عشر»; (اثني عشر) is the direct object of (بعثنا); and (نقيبا) is a tamyīz (specification).
(وَقالَ اللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, by way of iltifāt (shift of person); (قال الله) is a verb and its agent; (إني) is inna with its noun; (معكم) is an adverb attached to its omitted khabar (predicate); and (إن) with what falls within its scope is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ الصَّلاةَ وَآتَيْتُمُ الزَّكاةَ): the lām prepares for the omitted oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); (إن) is conditional; (أقمتم) is a verb and its agent, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الصلاة) is the direct object; (آتيتم الزكاة) is conjoined to (أقمتم الصلاة); and the oath clause is resumptive.
(وَآمَنْتُمْ بِرُسُلِي وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ وَأَقْرَضْتُمُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً): conjoined to what precedes; (برسلي) is attached to (آمنتم); (عزرتموهم) is also conjoined: a verb and its agent, the wāw being for prolonging the ḍamma, and the hāʾ the direct object; (أقرضتم الله) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (قرضا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and (حسنا) is an adjective.
(لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath that precedes it. (عنكم) is attached to (أكفرن); (سيئاتكم) is the direct object; (لأدخلنكم) is conjoined to «لأكفرن»; (جنات) is a second object by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition; and the clause (تجري من تحتها الأنهار) is an adjective of (جنات).
(فَمَنْ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ مِنْكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ):
the fāʾ is resumptive. (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (كفر) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; (بعد ذلك) is an adverb attached to (كفر); (منكم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; in (فقد) the fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar of «من»; and (سواء السبيل) is the object of (ضل).

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya).
Spending in the way of Allah for His sake is likened to a loan, by way of metaphor, because by giving the deserving person what is his for the sake of Allah, it is as though he lent it to Him.

dervis-irab:13-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَعَنَّاهُمْ): We expelled them and removed them far from Our mercy.
(خائِنَةٍ): «الخائنة» here means treachery (الخيانة). The Arabs sometimes express the maṣdar (verbal noun) with the form of the active participle, and the reverse; thus «القائلة» was used in the sense of «القيلولة» (the midday nap), and «الخاطئة» in the sense of «الخطيئة» (sin). Or it is an adjective of an omitted noun: either masculine, with the hāʾ for intensiveness, as they said «راوية للشعر» for one who transmits poetry a great deal; [the poet] said:
حدثت نفسك بالوفاء ولم تكن ... للغدر خائنة مغلّ الإصبع
(You told yourself of loyalty, yet you were not one given to treachery, a finger that steals [from the spoils].)
and «داعية» for one who has devoted himself to calling to something. Or it is feminine, with the implied form:
or «فرقة» (a faction). «[Translator's note: the text appears abridged here; the usual wording is «نفس خائنة أو فرقة خائنة» (a treacherous soul or a treacherous faction).]»

* I'rab:
(فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to show that the expulsion and removal from mercy that befell them arose from their breaking the covenant. The bāʾ is a preposition; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the statement; (نقضهم) is genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (لعناهم); (ميثاقهم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar, namely «النقض»; and (لعناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its direct object.
(وَجَعَلْنا قُلُوبَهُمْ قاسِيَةً): (جعلنا) is conjoined to (لعناهم); (قلوبهم) is the first object and (قاسية) the second object.
(يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to show the extent of the hardness of their hearts; (الكلم) is the object of (يحرفون); and (عن مواضعه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يحرفون).
(وَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ): conjoined to what precedes; (نسوا حظا) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (مما), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «حظا»; and the clause (ذكروا به) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَلا تَزالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلى خائِنَةٍ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا تزال) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, its noun latent (mustatir), implied as «أنت»; the clause (تطلع) is the khabar (predicate) of (لا تزال); (على خائنة) is attached to (تطلع); (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of (خائنة); (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (قليلا) is excepted from the genitive pronoun in «منهم»; (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of «قليلا». By "the few of them" He meant those who embraced Islam, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions.
(فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. if you know this, then pardon whoever comes to you declaring his repentance and his joining under the banner of the upright religion. (اعف) is an imperative verb; (عنهم) is attached to «اعف»; and (اصفح) is conjoined to (فاعف).
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): inna and its noun; the clause (يحب المحسنين) is the khabar of (إن); and the clause of (إن) and what falls within its scope is causal, with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:92-93.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَاحْذَرُوا): the wāw is conjunctive, and the speech is conjoined to the interrogative in the preceding verse, because the interrogative has the meaning of a command, as has been stated. The meaning is: "Desist, and obey." You may also make it resumptive. أطيعوا الله is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أطيعوا الرسول is conjoined to أطيعوا الله; and احذروا is likewise conjoined. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما عَلى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; توليتم is a past verb and its agent, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then your requital is upon Us" (فجزاؤكم علينا); the clause فاعلموا is conjoined to the apodosis. أنما is [أنّ with] the restraining mā (kāffa and makfūfa), and together with what it governs it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا; على رسولنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); البلاغ is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and المبين is a naʿt (adjective). (لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جُناحٌ فِيما طَعِمُوا): the clause is resumptive, brought in reply to the question of some of the Companions who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what then of our brothers who died while they were drinking [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «بشربون» for «يشربون».] wine and consuming [the proceeds of] gambling?" So there was revealed: ليس ... ليس is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; على الذين is attached to the omitted fronted khabar of ليس; the clause آمنوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause وعملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila; جناح is the delayed noun of ليس; فيما is attached to an omitted adjective of جناح; and the clause طعموا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (إِذا مَا اتَّقَوْا وَآمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; ما is redundant (zāʾida); the clause اتقوا is in the position of the genitive as the adverb is put in construct with it; what governs إذا is the sense of negation in ليس, i.e. "sin is negated from them"; the apodosis of إذا is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then there is no blame upon them"; آمنوا is conjoined to اتقوا; and عملوا الصالحات is likewise conjoined to what precedes. (ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَآمَنُوا ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَأَحْسَنُوا): likewise conjoined; the secret of this marvellous repetition will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يحب is the khabar; and المحسنين is the direct object.

* Rhetoric:
The discussion of repetition (al-takrār or al-tikrār — both maṣdars of the doubled verb كرّر) has preceded, and we said that its definition is that the writer or poet repeats a word, or two words or more, to emphasize what he is speaking about, so that it becomes more firmly fixed in the mind, or for some other purpose. In this verse the repetition may be an allusion to the relationships by which a person is bound in his life, namely: a person's relationship with himself, his relationship with others, and his relationship with his Lord; that is why it is followed by iḥsān (excellence) the third time. It may also be an allusion to the three stages of life through which a person passes on his life's journey: the stage of the beginning of life, the stage of the middle of life, and the final stage. Perhaps both possibilities are intended in this marvellous repetition, as an increase in piety, in adornment [of character] and in the upholding of just scales in all the stages of his life and his three states. There will come in this book instances of repetition that enchant the minds. Listen to the words of al-Buḥturī in love poetry:
ويوم تثنّت للوداع وسلّمت ... بعينين موصول بلحظهما السحر
توهمتها ألوى بأجفانها الكرى ... كرى النوم أو مالت بأعطافها الخمر
(And on the day she swayed for the farewell and greeted with two eyes whose glance is joined with magic, I imagined that drowsiness — the drowsiness of sleep — had bent her eyelids, or that wine had made her sides sway.) الكرى is sleep, but in repeating it here there is a meaning grasped intuitively, resembling the seizure of magic.
And listen to the words of al-Musāwir ibn Hind:
جزى الله عنّي غالبا من عشيرة ... إذا حدثان الدهر نابت نوائبه
فكم دافعوا من كربة قد تلاحمت ... عليّ وموج قد علتني غواربه
(May Allah reward on my behalf [the tribe of] Ghālib as kinsfolk, when the calamities of time strike; how many a distress that closed in upon me did they repel, and how many a wave whose crests had towered over me!) The first and second halves of the second verse indicate one meaning, because the closing in of distresses upon him is like the towering of the waves above him. What made this acceptable is that it is a context of praise and eulogy; do you not see that he describes the kindness of these people at the calamities of his time through repetition! And conversely, were the speaker satirizing, satire in this would be like praise.
Here we would like to add a qualification and say: not all repetition is good; some of it is insipid, such as the words of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī from his marvellous ode which opens:
أفاضل الناس أغراض لذا الزمن ... يخلو من الهمّ أخلاهم من الفطن
(The most excellent of people are targets for this age; the one freest of care is the one most devoid of intelligence.)
This is among the most beautiful and splendid poetry; yet soon afterwards he said:
العارض الهتن ابن العارض ال ... هتن العارض الهتن ابن العارض الهتن
(The pouring raincloud, son of the pouring raincloud, the pouring raincloud, son of the pouring raincloud.) This is not commendable repetition, because it is like your saying: "the one described as such-and-such, son of the one described as such-and-such", i.e. that he is of deep-rooted lineage in this quality; so he brought nothing new. Moreover, the wording is not acceptable in the way it has been used here, for using it in the compound state takes away its beauty. Among the delightful instances of repetition are the words of al-Muqannaʿ al-Kindī:
وإنّ الذي بيني وبين بني أبي ... وبين بني عمي لمختلف جدا
إذا أكلوا لحمي وفرت لحومهم ... وإن هدموا مجدي بنيت لهم مجدا
وإن ضيعوا غيبي حفظت غيوبهم ... وإن هم هووا غيّي هويت لهم رشدا
(What lies between me and my father's sons and my cousins is very different indeed: if they eat my flesh, I preserve their flesh; if they demolish my glory, I build glory for them; if they neglect me in my absence, I guard them in theirs; and if they desire my going astray, I desire right guidance for them.)
What has preceded is sufficient for us for now.

dervis-irab:94-94.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ): He will surely test your obedience.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ): resumptive speech brought to [speak of] testing them in relation to what the servants understand; as for the reality of testing, it is impossible with respect to Him the Exalted. ليبلونكم: the lām is [the lām of] the answer to an omitted oath, i.e. "By Allah, He will surely test you"; يبلون is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; الله is its fāʿil (agent); بشيء is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يبلونكم; من الصيد is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of شيء; and the clause يبلونكم has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the omitted oath. (تَنالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِماحُكُمْ لِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَخافُهُ بِالْغَيْبِ): the clause is an adjective of شيء; أيديكم is the agent of تناله; رماحكم is conjoined to أيديكم; the lām is causal; يعلم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām; الله is the agent of يعلم; من is a relative noun, the object of يعلم; the clause يخافه has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); and بالغيب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of يخاف, i.e. he fears Allah while being absent from Allah [Translator's note: so in the text: «غائبا عن الله».], or from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. he fears Allah while being clothed in the unseen.
