(فَمَنِ اعْتَدى بَعْدَ ذلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun; اعتدى is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the adverb بعد ذلك is attached to اعتدى, and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi; فله: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); عذاب is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); أليم is an adjective; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».

* Rhetoric:
In His words «بشيء من الصيد» there is a diminishing and belittling of this trial, as if He were saying: this trial is not of the kind of great tribulations and great ordeals before which neither strength nor bodies stand firm. This is what the great exegetes have mentioned, especially al-Zamakhsharī, whose wording most of them have transmitted almost verbatim. It is a strong intellectual leap, but it shrinks and weighs light in the balance when we recall that He, glory be to Him, used it for great tribulations and grievous ordeals, saying in another place: «ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات وبشر الصابرين». This is an objection that overturns what al-Zamakhsharī said and what many exegetes have transmitted from him, such as al-Khāzin, al-Nasafī, al-Bayḍāwī and others. The best that can be said in reply to this objection is that all ordeals, calamities, trials and tribulations are, in relation to what lies within the power of Allah the Exalted, nothing but a small part fit to be belittled and diminished, and that He, glory be to Him, inclined to addressing the believers with this formulation to lighten things for them, as a motive for them to be patient and an incentive for them to endure, out of gentleness toward them and kindness regarding what they suffer from it. So glory be to the One who is unique in this eloquence.

dervis-irab:14-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَصارى): In Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «النصير» is the helper (الناصر), and its plural is «أنصار», like «شريف» and «أشراف»; the plural of «الناصر» is «نصر», like «صاحب» and «صحب». «النصارى» is the plural of «نصران» and «نصرانة», like «الندامى», plural of «ندمان» and «ندمانة». «نصران» is only used with the yāʾ of relation (nisba). In al-Miṣbāḥ: a «نصراني» man, with fatḥa on the nūn, and a «نصرانية» woman. It is said to be a relation to a village named «نصرى»; for this reason one says in the singular «نصري», according to rule; then «النصراني» came to be applied to everyone who worships by this religion. In al-Munjid it says: «النصراني» is a relation to the city of al-Nāṣira (Nazareth), irregularly: one who follows the religion of the Lord Christ; the plural is «نصارى» and the feminine «نصرانية». In al-Lisān it says: «نَصَرى» with two fatḥas, «نَصْرى» with fatḥa then sukūn, «ناصرة» and «نصورية»: a village in Syria, and the Naṣārā are named after it. Ibn Sīdah said: this is the view of the lexicographers. He said: it is weak, except that irregular nisba forms can accommodate it. He said: As for Sībawayh, he said: as for «نصارى», al-Khalīl held that it is the plural of «نصري» and «نصران», just as they said «ندمان» and «ندامى»; but they deleted one of the two yāʾs, as they deleted [one] from «أثفيّة», and substituted an alif in its place, as they said «صحارى». He said: as for the way we ourselves explain it, it came on «نصران», because that has been spoken; so it is as though you pluralised «نصر» as you pluralised «مسمع», and said «نصارى» as you said «ندامى».
(أغرينا): We attached and made binding. It is from «غري بالشيء» when one clings to a thing and sticks to it; and «الغراء» means that by which something is stuck, «الغراء» being on the pattern of «كتاب». In al-Miṣbāḥ: «غري بالشيء غريا», of the pattern of «تعب»: he became infatuated with it without anyone driving him to it; «أغريته به إغراء», so «أغري به», in the passive; the noun is «الغَراء», with fatḥa and prolongation, and «الغِراء», like «كتاب»: that with which things are stuck (glue), made from hides, and sometimes made from fish.
«الغرا», like «العصا», is a dialectal form of it. «غروت الجلد أغروه», of the pattern of «عدا»:
I stuck it with glue. «أغريت بين القوم» is like «أفسدت» (I sowed discord) in form and meaning. «غروت غروا», of the pattern of «قتل»: I was amazed; and «لا غرو»: no wonder.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّا نَصارى أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَهُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to speak about the Christians. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أخذنا); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); (إن) with its noun, and (نصارى) its khabar (predicate); the clause (أخذنا) is resumptive, as stated; (ميثاقهم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (إنا نصارى) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). There are other views, which you will see in the section on benefits.
(فَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (نسوا) is conjoined to (أخذنا), the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); (حظا) is the direct object; (مما) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «حظا»; the clause (ذكروا) is the ṣila; (به), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (ذكروا); and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(فَأَغْرَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): conjoined to what precedes; (أغرينا) is a verb and its agent; the adverb is attached to (أغرينا); (العداوة) is the direct object; and (إلى يوم القيامة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.:
extending to the Day of Resurrection.
(وَسَوْفَ يُنَبِّئُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما كانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (سوف) is a particle of futurity; (ينبئهم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (بما) is attached to (ينبئهم); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; and the clause (يصنعون) is the khabar of (كانوا).

* Benefits:
Some parsers have brought the views they allowed in this verse to a number, among them the one we chose, which is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, except that he made the pronoun in (ميثاقهم) refer back to the Children of Israel, the implied form being: "and We took from the Christians a covenant like the covenant of the Children of Israel." There is a view worth mentioning: that His saying «ومن الذين» is attached to an omitted [element], being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) whose adjective stands in its place, the implied form being: "and among those who said 'We are Christians' are a people whose covenant We took."

dervis-irab:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ قَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنا): resumptive speech introduced to address the People of the Book in general, by way of iltifāt (shift of person). (يا) is a vocative particle for the one at a middle distance; (أهل الكتاب) is a vocative in construct, accusative; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (جاءكم) is a past verb with a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (رسولنا) is the delayed fāʿil (agent).
(يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيراً مِمَّا كُنْتُمْ تُخْفُونَ مِنَ الْكِتابِ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسولنا»; (لكم) is attached to (يبين); (كثيرا) is the direct object; (مما), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا»; (ما) is a relative noun; (كنتم) is kāna with its noun, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause (تخفون) is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of (كنتم); and (من الكتاب), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the omitted referent pronoun.
(وَيَعْفُوا عَنْ كَثِيرٍ): the clause is conjoined to the circumstantial clause «يبين» and enters into its ruling.
(قَدْ جاءَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ وَكِتابٌ مُبِينٌ): a resumptive clause introduced to set out the benefit of the Messenger's coming. (من الله), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (نور) and was placed before it. (نور) is the agent of «جاءكم»; (كتاب) is conjoined to «نور»; and (مبين) is an adjective.
(يَهْدِي بِهِ اللَّهُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوانَهُ سُبُلَ السَّلامِ): the clause is an adjective of (كتاب); (به) is attached to (يهدي); (الله) is the agent; (من) is a relative noun, the direct object; the clause (اتبع رضوانه) is the ṣila; and (سبل السلام) is a second object of (يهدي) by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (يهدي).
(وَيُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يخرجهم) is conjoined to (يهدي), the hāʾ being the direct object; (من الظلمات) is attached to (يخرجهم), and likewise (إلى النور); and (بإذنه), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): conjoined to what precedes; its parsing has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «من الظلمات إلى النور» there are two explicit, primary metaphors (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya aṣliyya): by the first is meant misguidance, and by the second guidance and faith; the relation is resemblance. The word for the thing likened was dropped «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «وقد لفظ المشبه», apparently for «وقد حذف لفظ المشبه» (the word for the thing likened was omitted)]», and the word for the thing it is likened to was borrowed in its place to stand for it, by claiming that the thing likened-to is the very thing likened. This reaches further in eloquence and is more deeply rooted in it. Since the thing likened-to is stated explicitly in this figurative usage, the metaphor is called explicit (taṣrīḥiyya); and it is called primary (aṣliyya) because it occurs in a noun. Among explicit metaphors is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī]:
وأقبل يمشي في البساط فما درى ... إلى البحر يسعى أم إلى البدر يرتقي
(He came forward walking on the carpet, not knowing whether he was striding to the sea or climbing to the full moon.)
He likened Sayf al-Dawla to the sea; then the word denoting the thing likened-to, namely the sea, was borrowed for the thing likened, namely Sayf al-Dawla, by way of explicit metaphor; the contextual clue (qarīna) is "he came forward walking on the carpet." The same is said of likening Sayf al-Dawla to the full moon.

dervis-irab:17-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَمْلِكُ): The Arabs say «ملك فلان على فلان أمره» when he has gained mastery over him, so that he can neither carry out any matter nor do anything except through him and with his permission.
Ibn Durayd said, describing wine whose sharpness has not been broken by mixing and whose effect fire has not nullified:
لم يملك الماء عليها أمرها ... ولم يدنّسها الضّرم المحتضى
(Water did not gain mastery over her affair, nor did the stirred-up blaze defile her.)
His saying, the Exalted, «فمن يملك من الله شيئا» is more eloquent than a saying like this, because it denies that anyone has power over any part of His affair, the Exalted, let alone power over His whole affair; so the meaning becomes that there is no one who can turn back His command and divert it from His will in any way.

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ): the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (كفر) is a past verb and (الذين) its fāʿil (agent); the clause (قالوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); the oath clause is resumptive; the clause (قد كفر) has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. (إن) with its noun and its khabar (predicate) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) conveying restriction, with no governing effect, and (المسيح) is the khabar of (إن); or «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (المسيح) its khabar, the clause being the khabar of (إن); and (ابن مريم) is a badal (substitute) or a naʿt (adjective).
(قُلْ فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): the clause is resumptive; (قل) is an imperative verb whose agent is «أنت»; the fāʾ conjoins to an omitted clause which is the object of «قل», i.e.:
say [this] by way of rebuke and to show the falsehood of their saying. (من) is a noun of rhetorical (denying) interrogation, a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يملك) is the khabar; (من الله), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) or to (يملك); and (شيئا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(إِنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ الْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ): the conditional clause is explicative, with no grammatical position. (إن) is conditional; (أراد) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (أن) with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of (أراد); (المسيح) is the direct object; (ابن مريم) is a badal or a naʿt; (أمه) is conjoined to (المسيح); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then who has any power at all against Allah."
(وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً): the wāw is a conjunction; (من) is a relative noun conjoined to (المسيح) and (أمه); (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted ṣila; and (جميعا) is a ḥāl.
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لله), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ملك السموات والأرض) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; as for (وما بينهما): the wāw conjoins to (ملك), (ما) is a relative noun, and the adverb is attached to an omitted ṣila.
(يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to show that He, Glorified is He, creates creation according to His will.
(وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the speech is resumptive, introduced to set out His power, the Exalted, over everything: everything to which His will is connected is carried out by His power, and some of His creation is counted strange only relative to deficient human knowledge, not relative to Him, the Exalted. Its parsing has been given before.

dervis-irab:18-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فترة): from «فتر الشيء», when a thing became still or its sharpness subsided. Al-Rāghib said:
«الفتور» is stillness after sharpness, softness after severity, and weakness after strength; and he mentioned the verse. What is meant by it here is the cessation of revelation and of the appearance of messengers for several centuries.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصارى): the wāw is resumptive; (قالت اليهود) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (النصارى) is conjoined to (اليهود).
(نَحْنُ أَبْناءُ اللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ): the clause is the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (أبناء الله) the khabar (predicate), and (أحباؤه) is conjoined to (أبناء الله).
(قُلْ: فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ؟): the speech is resumptive, introduced to refute these claims. (قل) is an imperative verb, the agent being «أنت»; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. if you are as you claim, then why does He punish you for the sins you commit! In (لم), the lām is a preposition and (ما) is an interrogative noun whose alif was dropped because the preposition entered upon it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يعذبكم). (يعذبكم) is an imperfect verb and its object, the agent being «هو»; (بذنوبكم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is also attached to (يعذبكم). The whole clause is the object of their saying «[Translator's note: so in the text; the clause is in fact the object of «قل» (say)]», and the clause (لم يعذبكم) has no grammatical position because it occurs as the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ): (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction, conjoining to an omitted [clause] drawn from the sense of the preceding speech, i.e. "so you are not, then, of this standing in nearness to Him, Glorified is He." (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ and (بشر) the khabar; (ممن), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (بشر); and the clause (خلق) is the ṣila (relative clause) of «من».
(يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the clause is resumptive; (لمن), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يغفر); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila; and the clause (يعذب من يشاء) is conjoined to the foregoing clause.
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ): the clause is resumptive; (لله) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ملك السموات) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); (ما) is also conjoined; the adverb is attached to an omitted ṣila. In (وإليه المصير), the wāw is a conjunction; (إليه), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (المصير) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is conjoined to the clause (ولله ملك السموات والأرض).
(يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ قَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنا): (يا) is a vocative particle; (أهل الكتاب) is a vocative in construct; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (جاءكم رسولنا) is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its agent; and the clause is resumptive.
(يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلى فَتْرَةٍ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ): the clause (يبين) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسولنا», i.e. "explaining to you"; (لكم) is attached to (يبين); (على فترة), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (جاءكم), i.e. he came to you at a time of lapse in the sending of messengers and the cessation of revelation; or [it is attached] to an omitted [element] occurring as a ḥāl from the pronoun of (يبين), or from the pronoun of (لكم).
I.e. he explains to you what has been mentioned while he is [coming] after a lapse of messengers, or while you are in it, at a time you were most in need of explanation. (من الرسل), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted adjective of (فترة), i.e. "occurring from the messengers."
(أَنْ تَقُولُوا: ما جاءَنا مِنْ بَشِيرٍ وَلا نَذِيرٍ): in (أن تقولوا), the maṣdar formed from «أن» and the verb after it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "out of aversion to your saying"; or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, with negation implied, i.e. «لئلا تقولوا» (lest you say). The clause (ما جاءنا) is in the position of accusative as the object of saying; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (بشير) is the agent of (جاءنا) in position; and (ولا نذير) is conjoined to (من بشير).
(فَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. if you excuse yourselves with that, then a bearer of good tidings and a warner has come to you.
(جاءكم بشير) is a verb, its direct object and its agent; (نذير) is conjoined to (بشير); and the clause has no grammatical position because it occurs as the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (قدير) its khabar; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (قدير).

dervis-irab:48-48.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُهَيْمِناً): i.e. a witness and a watcher over all the Books, because it bears witness to their soundness and firmness. Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:
إنّ الكتاب مهيمن لنبيّنا ... والحقّ يعرفه ذوو الألباب
(The Book is a guardian for our Prophet, and the truth is recognised by those of understanding.) [Translator's note: the source prints «لنبيّا»; the verse is usually cited «لنبيّنا», and it is glossed accordingly.]
There is disagreement about the origin of its verb: is it a root in itself, i.e. not substituted from anything? One says هيمن يهيمن, and the active participle is مهيمن, like بيطر يبيطر, so he is مبيطر. Or is its hāʾ substituted from a hamza, it being the active participle of آمن غيره من الخوف ("he made another safe from fear")? The original form would be مؤأيمن with two hamzas; the second was changed into a yāʾ out of dislike for two hamzas coming together, and then the first was changed into a hāʾ.
(شِرْعَةً): الشرعة with kasra on the shīn is religion, and الشرع is like it; it is taken from الشريعة, which is the watering place where people come to draw water. It is so called because of its clarity and evidentness. Its plural is شرائع. شرّع الله لنا كذا يشرعه: He made it evident and clear. المشرعة, with fatḥa on the mīm and the rāʾ, is the watering place (شريعة الماء). Al-Azharī said: The Arabs do not call it مشرعة until the water is perennial, never ceasing, like river water, and also exposed, not drawn with a well-rope. If it is from rainwater, it is الكرع, with two fatḥas. And "people are شرع in this matter", with two fatḥas, the rāʾ also being made vowelless for lightness: i.e. equal.
(مِنْهاجاً): In al-Mukhtār: النهج, on the pattern of الفلس, is المنهج, i.e. the way (المذهب). المنهاج is the clear road. نهج الطريق: he made the road clear; and نهجه also means he travelled it; the conjugation class of both is that of قطع. النهج with two fatḥas is panting. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «نهج الطريق ينهج, with two fatḥas, means it became clear and evident, and أنهج with alif is like it; نهجته and انتهجته mean I made it clear; they are used both intransitively and transitively.»

* I'rab:
(وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ): the wāw is conjunctive; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزلنا; and بالحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الكتاب. (مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتابِ): مصدقا is a ḥāl of الكتاب; لما is attached to «مصدقا»; بين is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause), and يديه is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl.
By الكتاب He meant the genus, i.e. the genus of the Books sent down from heaven. (وَمُهَيْمِناً عَلَيْهِ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): مهيمنا is conjoined to «مصدقا», and عليه is attached to «مهيمنا». فاحكم: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. "since such is the status of the Qur'an, judge between the People of the Book, when they bring their disputes to you, by what Allah has sent down". احكم is an imperative verb; بينهم is an adverb attached to «فاحكم»; بما is attached to احكم; and the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila. (وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ عَمَّا جاءَكَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تتبع is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; أهواءهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عما جاءك is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "deviating"; and the clause جاءك is the ṣila. It has been said that «تتبع» includes the meaning of «تنحرف» ("deviate") or «تتزحزح» ("shift away"), so that the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to it. من الحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاءك, or of the relative «ما» itself. (لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهاجاً): resumptive speech, brought to induce the people of the two Books among his contemporaries to submit to what he brought. لكل is attached to «جعلنا», or it is the first object of جعلنا; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the omitted noun replaced by the tanwīn of compensation that attaches to «لكل», i.e. "for every nation among you"; شرعة is the object of جعلنا, and منهاجا is conjoined to شرعة. (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً): the wāw is resumptive; لو is conditional; شاء الله is a verb and its fāʿil; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; the clause جعلكم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; أمة is the second object of جعلكم, and واحدة is a naʿt. (وَلكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي ما آتاكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened; in ليبلوكم the lām is of purpose, and يبلوكم is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of purpose; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, its implied form being "He willed"; فيما is attached to يبلوكم, and the clause آتاكم is the ṣila. (فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْراتِ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعاً): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if the aspect of wisdom in this has become clear to you, then race". استبقوا is a verb and its fāʿil; الخيرات is a mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and perhaps this is preferable, because the basic usage of «استبق» is to make it transitive with «إلى», unless «استبق» is made to include the meaning of «ابتدر» ("hasten to"), in which case it is transitive by itself. إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), and مرجعكم is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, brought as a reason for racing to good deeds. جميعا is a ḥāl of the kāf, because it is an agent in meaning, i.e. "you will return all together". (فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to the meaning of مرجعكم, i.e. "you will return, and He will inform you"; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; بما is attached to ينبئكم; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; the tāʾ is the noun of كان, and the clause تختلفون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In making the pronoun overt in His saying «الكتاب» [Translator's note: i.e. using the noun الكتاب again where a pronoun would have sufficed] there is a statement of its importance, and that it is the reference, the refuge and the safeguard when a matter becomes grave; this falls within the domain of the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿānī).
An instance of it in poetry is the saying of al-Buḥturī at the opening of his Sīniyya (ode rhyming in sīn):
صنت نفسي عما يدنس نفسي ... وترفعت عن جدا كلّ جبس
(I guarded my soul from what defiles my soul, and rose above the bounty of every base wretch.)

dervis-irab:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, setting out how to judge between them. Al-Zamakhsharī made it conjunctive, joining to الكتاب, and how far-fetched that is is not hidden. أن with what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and what the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) is omitted, i.e. "and We enjoined you to judge". Abū Ḥayyān chose that the interpreted maṣdar be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, the implied form being: "and your judging by what Allah has sent down is Our command and Our word"; or you may give its implied form by saying: "and among what is obligatory is your judging by what Allah has sent down". There is nothing wrong with what he said.
بينهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); بما is attached to «احكم»; and the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ وَاحْذَرْهُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ): the clause is conjoined to «احكم»; لا is prohibitive; تتبع is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا»; أهواءهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); احذرهم is also conjoined; and أن يفتنوك is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "of their tempting you". You may make the interpreted maṣdar a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for the hāʾ in «واحذرهم», because they contain the temptation. They also permitted the maṣdar to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with an implied lām of cause and a negating لا [Translator's note: i.e. "lest they tempt you"]; I see this as strained, but many of the analysts have analysed it so. (عَنْ بَعْضِ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يفتنوك; ما is a relative noun in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila; and إليك is attached to أنزل. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُصِيبَهُمْ بِبَعْضِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; تولوا is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; the clause اعلم is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أنما is the restraining (kāffa) ما with the restrained particle, and it with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of اعلم; يريد is an imperfect verb and الله its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar is the object of يريد; and ببعض is attached to يصيبهم. (وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ لَفاسِقُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; inna and its noun; من الناس is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كثير; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and فاسقون is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
Ambiguity (ibhām) in His saying: «ببعض ذنوبهم». Turning away — for all its enormity and gravity and the grievousness of the presumption in it — is one of them. What is meant is that they have sins great in number, and the turning away is among them and one of them. How great a loss is their bargain, and how hideous is what they committed! The use of «بعض» for ambiguity occurs often in their speech; an instance is the saying of Labīd ibn Rabīʿa in his Muʿallaqa:
ترّاك أمكنة إذا لم أرضها ... أو يعتلق بعض النفوس حمامها
(One who readily leaves places when he is not pleased with them — unless death seizes some soul.)
He meant his own soul, and intended to magnify its standing by this ambiguity. He says: I readily leave places when I am not pleased with them, unless its death seizes my soul so that it cannot depart. Whoever made «بعض النفوس» mean "all souls" has erred, because بعض does not convey generality and comprehensiveness; it is as though he said: "a great soul".

dervis-irab:50-51.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَحُكْمَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ): the speech is conjoined to what preceded, brought to show one pattern of their obstinacy and their following the path of falsehood. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Do they turn away from your judgement and seek the judgement of the Jāhiliyya?" حكم is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of His saying «يبغون»; الجاهلية is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); يبغون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; من is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and أحسن is its khabar (predicate); من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحسن; حكما is a tamyīz (specification); and لقوم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Jalāl and others said: the lām means عند ("in the view of"), attached to أحسن, i.e. "in the view of a people who are certain". The clause يوقنون is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصارى أَوْلِياءَ): the i'rab of the vocative has preceded. لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا», and the wāw is the fāʿil; اليهود is a mafʿūl bihi, النصارى is conjoined to اليهود, and أولياء is a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. (بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ): بعضهم is a mubtadaʾ and أولياء بعض the khabar; the nominal clause is a naʿt of أولياء, or inceptive, mentioned as a reason for the prohibition. (وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتولهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; منكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. فإنه: the fāʾ is linking, إنّ and its noun, and منهم its khabar; the nominal clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): inna and its noun; لا is negative; يهدي is an imperfect verb; القوم is a mafʿūl bihi and الظالمين a naʿt; the clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون» there is a delightful art, the art of īghāl (penetration): the speaker completes his speech before bringing its close, and when he wishes to bring the close he brings something that conveys a meaning additional to the meaning of that speech. It is of two kinds:
1- Īghāl of choice (īghāl takhyīr): as in this verse, for the meaning was complete with His saying: «ومن أحسن من الله حكما». When the speech needed a verse-ending (fāṣila) suited to what is before and after it, it came conveying an additional meaning which would not have been obtained without it. That is because none knows that Allah's judgement is better than every judgement except one who is certain that He is One, Wise and Just — so that His oneness negates any partner in the judgement in which He alone is unique, there being no rival to Him in it and none to contradict Him; and from His wisdom follows putting each thing in its place, so that putting the right out of its place is safe from Him; and justice negates from Him injustice in judgement. Then He turned away from saying «يعلمون» ("who know") to saying «يوقنون» ("who are certain"), so that their knowledge of their Lord would be knowledge of conclusiveness and certainty.

Precautionary īghāl in poetry:
As for precautionary īghāl in poetry, it occurs specifically in the rhymes and does not go beyond them; some call it al-tablīgh. Al-Ḥātimī related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad, who said: al-Tawwazī told me: I said to al-Aṣmaʿī: "Who is the greatest of poets?" He said: "The one who makes a mean meaning great by its wording, or comes to a great meaning and makes it mean, or completes his speech before the rhyme and, when he needs the rhyme, conveys a meaning by it." I said: "Such as whom?" He said: "Such as al-Aʿshā, when he says:
كناطح صخرة يوما ليوهنها ... فلم يضرها وأوهى قرنه الوعل
(Like one butting a rock one day to weaken it; it did not harm it, and the mountain goat weakened its own horn.)
The comparison was complete with his saying: وأوهى قرنه ('and weakened its horn'); then, when he needed the rhyme, he said: «الوعل» ('the mountain goat')." I said: "And how did the mountain goat come to be preferred over everything that butts?" He said: "Because it hurls itself down from the mountain peak onto its horn and is not harmed." I said: "Then such as whom?" He said: "Such as Dhū al-Rumma in his saying:
قف العيس في أطلال ميّة واسأل ... رسوما كأخلاق الرّداء المسلسل
(Halt the camels at the ruins of Mayya and question traces like the worn-out rags of a threadbare cloak.)
His speech was complete; then he needed the rhyme and said: المسلسل ('threadbare'), and so added something. And his saying:
أظن الذي يجدي عليك سؤالها ... دموعا كتبديد الجمان المفصّل
(I think that what questioning them will bring you is tears like the scattering of pearls from a strung necklace separated by beads.)
He completed his speech; then he needed the rhyme and said «المفصل» ('separated by beads'), and also added something." There is no disagreement among people that Imruʾ al-Qays was the first to originate this idea, in his saying describing the horse:
إذا ماجرى شأوين وابتل عطفه ... تقول: هزيز الريح مرت بأثأب
(When he has run two heats and his flank is wet, you would say: the roar of the wind passing through the athʾab trees.)
He went to the utmost in describing it, presenting it in this state after it has run two heats and its flank has become wet with sweat; then he added «الأثأب» as a penetration in its description: it is a tree in whose folded branches the wind makes a great rustling and a loud sound. Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā followed him and said:
كأن فتات العهن في كل منزل ... نزلن به حبّ الفنا لم يحطّم
(As though the shreds of dyed wool at every halt where they alighted were fanā berries not yet crushed.)
So he penetrated deeply in the simile by likening the scattered shreds of purple wool to fanā berries not yet crushed, because it is red outside and white inside; if it is not crushed, no white at all appears in it, and it is pure red. Al-Aʿshā followed them both and said, describing a woman:
غرّاء فرعاء مصقول عوارضها ... تمشي الهوينى كما يمشي الوجي الوحل
(Radiant, long-haired, her side-teeth polished; she walks slowly, as one with sore hooves walks stuck in mud.)
He penetrated with his saying «الوحل» ("stuck in mud") after having said «الوجي» ("sore-footed"). Al-Rashīd greatly admired the saying of Ṣarīʿ al-Ghawānī:
إذا ما علت منّا ذؤابة شارب ... تمشّت به مشي المقيّد في الوحل
(When it rises to the forelock of a drinker among us, it makes him walk like a fettered man in mud.)
And he would say: "May Allah fight him! It was not enough for him to make him fettered until he put him in mud."
2- Precautionary īghāl (īghāl iḥtiyāṭ):
It is that the speaker completes the meaning of his speech before ending it, and when he wishes to bring the close he brings something conveying an additional meaning to complete the hyperbole, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء» ("nor can you make the deaf hear the call"); then He, Mighty and Majestic, knew that the speech needed a verse-ending matching the endings of what is before and after it, so He brought it conveying a meaning additional to the meaning of the speech, where He said: «إذا ولّوا مدبرين» ("when they turn their backs, retreating"). If it is said: what is the meaning of مدبرين, when the mention of turning away has made it unnecessary? We say: that does not make it unnecessary, since turning away may be with one side rather than another, as aversion may be. More of it will come when discussing Sūrat al-Naml, if Allah the Exalted wills.

dervis-irab:95-95.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حُرُمٌ): plural of حرام. In حرام masculine and feminine are the same.
You say: "this is a man in the sacred state (حرام)" and "this is a woman in the sacred state (حرام)"; but if محرم is said, then for the woman محرمة is said. Iḥrām is entering into it; one says: أحرم القوم ("the people entered the sacred state") when they enter the sacred month or the sacred precinct. So the interpretation of the words is: do not kill game while you are in iḥrām for Ḥajj or ʿUmra.
(عَدْلٍ): an equivalent.
(وَبالَ): al-wabāl, with fatḥa on the wāw: the hateful thing and the harm that reaches someone in the outcome of an evil deed, because of its heaviness upon him. Al-Rāghib said: al-wābil is rain with heavy drops, and in consideration of heaviness, a matter whose harm is feared is called wabāl. Allah the Exalted said:
«فذاقوا وبال أمرهم». And one says: "unwholesome food" (طعام وبيل) and "unwholesome pasture" (كلأ وبيل), whose ill effect is feared. Allah the Exalted said: «فأخذناه أخذا وبيلا». And استوبلت الأرض: I disliked the land for fear of its ill effects.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَقْتُلُوا الصَّيْدَ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ): resumptive speech brought to begin explaining what the word "transgression" in the previous verse includes.
لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الصيد is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وأنتم: the wāw is circumstantial, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and حرم its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of تقتلوا. (وَمَنْ قَتَلَهُ مِنْكُمْ مُتَعَمِّداً فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the clause of the condition and the apodosis; قتله is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of قتل; متعمدا is also a ḥāl from the agent of قتل, i.e. mindful of his iḥrām, or knowing that what he kills is among what is forbidden to him to kill — the details are in the books of jurisprudence. فجزاء: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); جزاء is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a compensation"; the reverse is also possible, i.e. "then what is obligatory upon him is a compensation"; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. مثل is a naʿt (adjective) of جزاء; ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive in construct with مثل; the clause قتل is the ṣila (relative clause); and من النعم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from مثل. (يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ هَدْياً بالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ): the clause يحكم is a second adjective of جزاء; به is attached to يحكم; ذوا is an agent in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the alif because it is a dual; عدل is muḍāf ilayhi; منكم is attached to an omitted adjective of «ذوا»; هديا is a ḥāl from جزاء, or accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "he offers it as an offering", or accusative as tamyīz (specification) — the three views are equally weighty; and بالغ الكعبة is an adjective of «هديا», because the construct is not pure, and it does not convey [Translator's note: the text reads «لا تقيد», evidently a misprint for «لا تفيد».] definiteness, as will come in the section on benefits. (أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعامُ مَساكِينَ أَوْ عَدْلُ ذلِكَ صِياماً): أو is conjunctive; كفارة is conjoined to جزاء; طعام مساكين is a badal (substitute) from كفارة; أو is a conjunction; عدل is conjoined to كفارة; ذلك is muḍāf ilayhi; and صياما is a tamyīz of العدل, as in your saying: "I have the like of him as a man" (لي مثله رجلا). (لِيَذُوقَ وَبالَ أَمْرِهِ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَفَ): the lām is causal; يذوق is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) latent in the khabar, i.e. "upon him is the compensation so that he may taste"; they may also be attached to طعام or صيام, or to «جزاء», i.e. "it is upon him to be requited so that he may taste the evil outcome of his violation of the sanctity of iḥrām". The clause عفا الله is resumptive, i.e. He has not taken you to task for the game you hunted before in the state of iḥrām, before it was made forbidden; عما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عفا; and the clause سلف is the ṣila of the relative. (وَمَنْ عادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقامٍ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; عاد is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ is linking; ينتقم الله is an imperfect verb and its agent, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then he — Allah takes vengeance on him"; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». منه is attached to ينتقم; the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; عزيز is a first khabar and ذو انتقام a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
Tasting in the verse is a dependent implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya): the evil outcome resulting from violating the sanctity of iḥrām is likened to unwholesome, indigestible food that he tastes; the thing likened [Translator's note: the text reads «فحذف المشبه»; in an implicit metaphor it is normally the thing likened-to (al-mushabbah bihi) that is omitted.] was omitted and something of its properties was kept, namely tasting. Similar cases have preceded.

* Benefits:
Construct (iḍāfa) is of three kinds:
1- A kind that conveys definiteness of the muḍāf through the muḍāf ilayhi if it is definite, or specification of it if it is indefinite, such as "ʿAlī's book" (كتاب علي) and "a student's book" (كتاب تلميذ).
2- A kind that conveys specification of the muḍāf without definiteness. Its criterion is that the muḍāf be deeply immersed in vagueness, such as غير ("other than"), مثل ("like") and شبه ("similar to"). The construct in these two kinds is called pure (maḥḍa) or genuine (ḥaqīqiyya); and the meaning of their saying "pure" is that it is free from the implication of separation.
3- A kind that conveys nothing of definiteness or specification, namely when the muḍāf is an adjective resembling the imperfect verb in denoting the present or the future, such as the active participle, the passive participle and the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha). An indefinite noun may be described by it, as in the verse we are dealing with: هديا is an indefinite noun in the accusative as a ḥāl, and بالغ الكعبة is its adjective; the meaning of «بالغ الكعبة» is that it is slaughtered in the sacred precinct; and an indefinite noun is not described by a definite one. Among its properties also is that it can come as a ḥāl, as in:
«ثاني عطفه», where ثاني is a ḥāl, as will come; and the ḥāl must be indefinite. Of this kind are the words of Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī:
فأتت به حوش الفؤاد مبطّنا ... سهدا إذا ما نام ليل الهوجل
(She bore him keen of heart, lean of flank, wakeful when the sluggard sleeps at night.) حوش is a resembling adjective meaning "sharp of heart", and it is put in the accusative as a ḥāl because it has acquired neither definiteness nor specification. Among its properties also is that «ربّ» may enter upon it, as in the words of Jarīr:
يا ربّ غابطنا لو كان يطلبكم ... لاقى مباعدة منكم وحرمانا
(How many a one who envies us — were he to seek you, he would meet with distance from you and deprivation!) He put «ربّ» before «غابطنا», and had it been definite, that would not have been correct. For this reason this construct is called verbal (lafẓiyya), because it conveys a merely verbal matter, namely the dropping of the tanwīn and of the nūn of the dual and plural — matters that go back to the wording alone.
There are other discussions relating to construct, which may be consulted in their proper places in the books of grammar.

dervis-irab:52-53.t:
* Vocabulary:
(دائِرَةٌ): الدائرة is one of the predominant attributes with which the thing described is not mentioned. Al-Rāghib in his Mufradāt distinguished between الدائرة and الدولة: الدائرة is the encircling line; then it was used to express an event, and it is said only of what is disliked, whereas الدولة is said of what is liked. It is reported that ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "I have allies among the Jews, many in number, and I declare myself free before Allah and His Messenger of their alliance, and I take Allah and His Messenger as allies." ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy said: "I am a man who fears turns of fortune (الدوائر); I will not declare myself free of the alliance of my allies." They were the Jews of Banū Qaynuqāʿ.
(حَبِطَتْ): i.e. the works which they used to affect in people's view became void.

* I'rab:
(فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يُسارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ): the fāʾ may be resumptive, with the speech resumptive, brought to show the manner of their alliance, its cause, and what their affair and their destiny would come to. It may also be conjunctive, with the speech conjoined to His saying: «إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين». In either case it has no grammatical position. ترى is an imperfect verb, and the seeing is either visual or cognitive; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في قلوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), and مرض is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause). The clause يسارعون is either a ḥāl (circumstantial), if the seeing is visual, or a second mafʿūl bihi, if the seeing is cognitive; and فيهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يسارعون. (يَقُولُونَ نَخْشى أَنْ تُصِيبَنا دائِرَةٌ): the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun of «يسارعون»; the clause نخشى is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); the interpreted maṣdar from أن and what is in its scope is the object of نخشى; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; and دائرة is the fāʿil (agent). (فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; عسى is one of the verbs of hope and operates like «كان»; الله is its noun, and أن يأتي is an interpreted maṣdar as its khabar. It has preceded that the khabar of عسى is most commonly an imperfect verb joined with أن. بالفتح is attached to يأتي; أو أمر is conjoined to الفتح; and من عنده is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمر. (فَيُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما أَسَرُّوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ نادِمِينَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive or causative; يصبحوا is conjoined to يأتي, or accusative by an implied أن after the causative fāʾ, because it is preceded by عسى, which is for hope. يصبحوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and the wāw is its noun; على ما is attached to نادمين; the clause أسروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; في أنفسهم is attached to أسروا; and نادمين is the khabar of «أصبح». (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: أَهؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to state what the believers say.
يقول الذين is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. It has been read with يقول in the accusative, conjoined to «أن يأتي», and it has been read without the wāw, so it is also resumptive. The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and الذين the khabar; the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying; the clause أقسموا is the ṣila; بالله is attached to أقسموا; and جهد أيمانهم is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a ḥāl. (إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and معكم is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar of إنّ. (حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا خاسِرِينَ): a resumptive clause. It has been said that it is the speech of Allah, and most analysts hold this; it has also been said that it is the speech of the believers, and al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān hold this. أعمالهم is the fāʿil of حبطت; the fāʾ is conjunctive; أصبحوا is a defective past verb, the wāw is its noun, and خاسرين its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted: «حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين» there is an art which Qudāma called al-ighrāb wa-l-ṭurfa (the rare and the novel). It is of three kinds:
1- A kind in which the rarity lies in the wording, and it is plentiful.
2- A kind in which the rarity lies in the meaning, as in the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
يطمّع الطير فيهم طول أكلهم ... حتى تكاد على أحيائهم تقع
(Their long feeding on them makes the birds covet them, until they almost alight upon their living.)
He took the well-known idea that birds alight only on the slain and follow armies, trusting they will be sated, and went beyond it, by an increase of hyperbole made pleasing by its being joined with «تكاد» ("almost"), to what he said; so his verse attained a rarity and novelty that no other attains.
3- And a kind in which the rarity is neither in its meaning nor in the outward form of its wording, but in its interpretation: it is that which, if taken in its outward sense, would make the speech faulty, but if interpreted, the interpretation returns it to a pattern of eloquent speech and removes the fault from its outward form.
The noble verse is of this kind, for one might say: the word «أصبحوا» ("they became by morning") is outwardly padding with no benefit, for these who are reported to be losers were in the evening in the same state as in the morning; and if you said: "the honey became sweet by morning" (أصبح العسل حلوا), the word «أصبح» would be redundant padding with no benefit, because it was likewise in the evening.
Al-Rummānī devised for this word an interpretation by which the great benefit is obtained, which would not be obtained without its coming. It is that, when he said: since the sick man who has spent the night suffering severe pains has his condition assessed in the morning — if by morning he is recovering and relieved of those pains, good is hoped for him, and his cure and recovery from that illness are thought most likely; and if by morning he is as he was in the evening, his perishing is certain, by the established pattern that illnesses flare up at night and subside in the morning [Translator's note: the sentence in the source, beginning «وهي أنه لما قال», has no main clause for لما; it is translated as it stands]. The state of the wretched has been likened to the sick man who by morning is in the same pain as in the evening, so he is one whose amendment is despaired of. On this basis the word «فأصبحوا» conveys a fine and beautiful meaning and ceases to be useless padding. And when Allah, glorified is He, reported that their works had become void, it was known conclusively that they had become losers; so no other word is fit in the place of «أصبحوا», and the meaning is not complete without it. As for the example given by al-Rummānī, «أصبح العسل حلوا وقد أمسى كذلك» ("the honey became sweet by morning, having been so in the evening") [Translator's note: in the source this example was earlier attributed to an objector, not to al-Rummānī], this is said only of matters occurring in the abode of this world, because its time has morning and evening; when a thing is in the morning in the state in which it is in the evening, mentioning morning and evening in it is padding with no benefit. But as for the Day of Resurrection, in which there is no evening, likening it to what is in the morning in a time accompanied by an evening is a likening that does not correspond to it.

dervis-irab:96-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ): i.e. travellers. It is the plural of سيار, and is made feminine in the sense of a company or group.

* I'rab:
(أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ وَطَعامُهُ مَتاعاً لَكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ): أحل is a passive past verb; لكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أحل; صيد البحر is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); طعامه is conjoined to «صيد»; متاعا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of your enjoyment, and it may also be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "He has given you enjoyment (متعكم تمتيعا)". لكم is attached to «متاعا»; للسيارة is conjoined to «لكم»; and the clause is resumptive. (وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ ما دُمْتُمْ حُرُماً): the wāw is conjunctive; حرم is a passive past verb; عليكم is attached to حرم; the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause; صيد البر is the deputy agent; ما دمتم: [دام is] a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and «ما» together with what follows it is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and the adverb is attached to حرم; the tāʾ is the noun of ما دام, and حرما is its khabar (predicate). (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذي is a naʿt (adjective); إليه is attached to تحشرون; تحشرون is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; and the clause تحشرون is the ṣila (relative clause).

dervis-irab:97-98.t:
* I'rab:
(جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الْكَعْبَةَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرامَ قِياماً لِلنَّاسِ وَالشَّهْرَ الْحَرامَ وَالْهَدْيَ وَالْقَلائِدَ): resumptive speech brought to explain the Kaʿba, which is the Sacred House. As for «جعل», you may consider it to be in the sense of «صيّر» ("to make into") or in the sense of «خلق» ("to create"). جعل الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); الكعبة is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); البيت الحرام is a badal (substitute) from الكعبة, the benefit of the substitution being praise; قياما is, on the first view, a second direct object, and on the second, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكعبة. It is from the roots with wāw [as the middle radical]; and it was said: قياما [is written with yāʾ] because of the kasra of the qāf, and it is originally قواما and صواما [Translator's note: the passage is compressed in the source; the point is that قيام was originally قِوام, the wāw becoming yāʾ after kasra, like صيام from صِوام.]. للناس is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قياما», i.e. they maintain, by repairing to it, the affair of their livelihoods and benefits. الشهر is conjoined to الكعبة; الحرام is a naʿt (adjective); and الهدي and القلائد are also conjoined to الكعبة. (ذلِكَ لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): the clause is resumptive, and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
The reference is to the whole of what has been mentioned before. لتعلموا: the lām is the causal lām, and تعلموا is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ذلك, i.e. "that ruling is the truth and nothing else". It was also said: ذلك is in the position of the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the ruling that We have established is that". The demonstrative may also be accusative by an implied verb, with لتعلموا attached to it, i.e. "We have legislated that". All the views are equally weighty. أن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of تعلموا; أن and its noun; the clause يعلم is its khabar; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause); and ما في الأرض is conjoined to «ما في السموات». (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): conjoined to the first «أن»; أن and its noun; بكل شيء is attached to «عليم»; and عليم is the khabar of أن. (اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): conjoined to what precedes; and غفور رحيم are two khabars of أن.

dervis-irab:99-100.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْخَبِيثُ): the opposite of good (al-ṭayyib). The plural is خبث with two ḍammas, and خبثاء, أخباث and خبثة with two fatḥas. خبثت نفسه: his soul became heavy and nauseated. The khāʾ and the bāʾ, as the first and second radicals of a verb, have a remarkable property, namely that they indicate effect and speed in concealment. One says خبّ, i.e. he deceived and corrupted, and the meaning of effect upon the one deceived and his corruption in it is not hidden; الخبب is a kind of running and going; خبأ الشيء: he covered and concealed the thing; خبر الشيء يخبره خبرا, with ḍamma on the khāʾ, and خبرا with kasra: he knew it through experience; خبز الخبز: he made the bread; خبس فلانا حقه: he wronged him and oppressed him; خبش الأشياء: he took things from here and there; خبص الشيء بالشيء: he mixed it; خبّص, with doubling: he made khabīṣa or khabīṣ, i.e. mixed sweetmeat; خبطه خبطا: he struck him a violent blow; خبله and خبّله, with doubling: he corrupted him; خبن الثوب: he folded the garment and sewed it; and خبن الشاعر: the poet used khabn in his poetry, which is the dropping of the second, quiescent [letter]. This is among the wonders of our noble language and its unique properties.

* I'rab:
(ما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ): the speech is resumptive, brought to stress the obligation of carrying out what has been commanded, i.e. the proof has been established against you and obedience has become binding on you, so you have no excuse if you overstep the limits. This saying has come to function as a proverb, and it will be discussed in detail in the section on rhetoric. ما is negating; على الرسول is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); إلا is a particle of restriction; and البلاغ is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تُبْدُونَ وَما تَكْتُمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يعلم is the khabar; ما is a relative noun, the object of تعلمون [Translator's note: so in the text; the verb in the verse is «يعلم».]; the clause تبدون is the ṣila (relative clause); and ما تكتمون is conjoined to His words ما تبدون. (قُلْ لا يَسْتَوِي الْخَبِيثُ وَالطَّيِّبُ): the clause is resumptive; قل is an imperative verb; and the clause لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). This clause too is among those that have become current as proverbs. (وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكَ كَثْرَةُ الْخَبِيثِ): the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; أعجبك is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); كثرة الخبيث is the fāʿil (agent) of أعجبك; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of لا يستوي, i.e. they are not equal, whatever their state. The apodosis of لو is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then they are not equal". (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ)
The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa ("disclosing") fāʾ, i.e. "if this has become clear to you, then fear Allah". اتقوا الله is a verb, its agent and its direct object; يا is a vocative particle; أولي الألباب is a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf); لعلكم: لعل and its noun; and the clause تفلحون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is irsāl al-mathal (sending forth a proverb), which consists in the speaker bringing, in part of his speech, something that functions like a current proverb, whether a piece of wisdom, a description or otherwise. Of this kind are the words of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
لأن حلمك حلم لا تكلفه ... ليس التكحل في العينين كالكحل
(Because your forbearance is a forbearance you do not affect: applying kohl to the eyes is not like eyes naturally dark.)
Abū al-Ṭayyib became famous for this feature until it became proverbial. He said:
خذ ما تراه ودع شيئا سمعت به ... في طلعة الشمس ما يغنيك عن زحل
(Take what you see and leave something you have merely heard of: in the rising of the sun there is what makes you do without Saturn.)
There will come of his proverbs what astonishes the mind; for now it is sufficient for us to cite selections from the ode of Ibn Zaydūn:
ما على ظني بأس ... يجرح الدهر وياسو
ولقد ينجيك إغفا ... ل ويرديك احتراس
ولكم أجدى قعود ... ولكم أكدى التماس
وكذا الحكم إذا ما ... عزّ ناس ذلّ ناس
لا يكن عهدك وردا ... إن عهدي لك آس فأدر ذكري كأسا ... ما امتطت كفّك
كاس واغتنم صفو الليالي ... إنما العيش اختلاس
(There is no harm in my thinking: time wounds and heals. Heedlessness may save you, and caution may ruin you. How often has sitting still availed, and how often has seeking come to nothing! Such is the rule: when some people rise to might, others fall low. Let not your pledge be a rose [that fades]; my pledge to you is a myrtle [that stays green]. So pass round the cup of my remembrance as long as a cup rides upon your palm, and seize the clear moments of the nights: life is nothing but snatched moments.)
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between «تبدون» and «تكتمون». [Translator's note: the source numbers this point "2" without a preceding "1"; the first point is evidently the irsāl al-mathal above.]

dervis-irab:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ): resumptive speech introduced to set out what they did and what issued from some of them after the covenant was taken. (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to an omitted «اذكر» (remember); the address is to the Prophet, so that what issued from them may be recounted to him. The clause (قال موسى), of verb and fāʿil (agent), is in the position of genitive by annexation; (لقومه) is attached to (قال).
(يا قَوْمِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (يا) is a vocative particle; (قوم) is a vocative annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; (اذكروا نعمة الله) is an imperative verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (عليكم) is attached to (نعمة).
(إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِياءَ وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُلُوكاً): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to «النعمة»; the clause (جعل) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (فيكم) is attached to (جعل) as being its first object «[Translator's note: so in the text; i.e. the prepositional phrase (فيكم) occupies the place of the first object]», and (أنبياء) is its second object; (وجعلكم ملوكا) is conjoined to what precedes, and (ملوكا) is a second object.
(وَآتاكُمْ ما لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَداً مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (آتاكم) is a verb and its first object, the agent being «هو»; (ما) is a relative noun, the second object; the clause (لم يؤت أحدا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (من العالمين) is attached to an omitted ṣila «[Translator's note: so in the text; it is more naturally an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (أحدا)]». What is meant by "the worlds" is the nations that had passed up to their time and the world of their time: [the favours] such as the parting of the sea, the shading by clouds, the manna and the quails, and other great matters.
(يا قَوْمِ ادْخُلُوا الْأَرْضَ الْمُقَدَّسَةَ): the clause is resumptive; (ادخلوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (الأرض) is a direct object by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (ادخلوا); and (المقدسة) is a naʿt of (الأرض).
(الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ): (التي) is a second adjective of (الأرض); the clause (كتب الله) is the ṣila; and (لكم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (كتب).
(وَلا تَرْتَدُّوا عَلى أَدْبارِكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (ترتدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), the wāw being the agent; and (على أدباركم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (ترتدوا).
(فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خاسِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تنقلبوا) is conjoined to (ترتدوا), so it is jussive like it. The fāʾ may also be the causative fāʾ (al-sababiyya), since a prohibition precedes it, so that [the verb] is accusative by an implied «أن» after it. (خاسرين) is a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
The vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker is of four kinds:
1- That which has one dialectal form: it is the word ending in a weak letter, yāʾ or alif; its yāʾ to which it is annexed must be retained and given fatḥa, e.g. «يا قاضيّ» and «يا فتايَ».
2- That which has two forms: it is the adjective resembling the imperfect verb, by which we mean the active and passive participles and the intensive forms of the active participle; its yāʾ is always retained, either with fatḥa or with sukūn «[Translator's note: the text reads «مكسورة» (with kasra); the standard rule is fatḥa or sukūn]», e.g. «يا مكرمي» and «يا ضاربي».
3- That which has six forms: it is everything other than that, which is neither «أب» nor «أم», e.g. «يا غلامي». The most common is to drop the yāʾ and make do with the kasra, e.g.:
«يا غلامِ»; then retaining it with sukūn as in the original, e.g. «يا غلامِيْ»; or with fatḥa, e.g. «يا غلامِيَ». Then turning the kasra into fatḥa and the yāʾ into alif, e.g. «يا حسرتا».
Then dropping the converted alif and making do with the fatḥa, so you say «يا حسرةَ»; then dropping the yāʾ, relying on its being intended, and giving ḍamma to the noun annexed to the yāʾ, as in «يا غلامُ».
4- That which has ten forms: it is «الأب» and «الأم». In them, in addition to the six forms mentioned, there are four other forms: that you substitute the tāʾ of the feminine for the yāʾ of the speaker and give it kasra, which is the most common; or give it fatḥa; or give it ḍamma, which is rare; and sometimes the tāʾ and the alif are combined, so that it is said: «يا أبتا» and «يا أمتا».

dervis-irab:22-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جَبَّارِينَ): «الجبار» is the insolent rebel; of the pattern «فعّال», from «جبره على الأمر» in the sense of «أجبره عليه» (he compelled him to it); he is the one who compels people to what he wants. What is meant here is that they were possessed of strength.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا: يا مُوسى إِنَّ فِيها قَوْماً جَبَّارِينَ): the clause is resumptive; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the vocative clause and what follows it is the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); (فيها) is attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (إن); (قوما) is its delayed noun; and (جبارين):
is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوما».
(وَإِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَها حَتَّى يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها): the wāw conjoins to what precedes; (إن) with its noun; the clause (لن ندخلها) is its khabar; (حتى) is a particle of limit and a preposition; (يخرجوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after it, and the preposition and its genitive noun [the interpreted maṣdar] are attached to (ندخلها); and (منها) is attached to (يخرجوا).
(فَإِنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها فَإِنَّا داخِلُونَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (يخرجوا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is linking, because the clause after it is nominal and not fit to be an apodosis [without it]; (إن) with its noun, and (داخلون) its khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(قالَ رَجُلانِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا): the clause is resumptive; (قال رجلان):
a verb and its agent; (من الذين), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted adjective; the clause (يخافون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause (أنعم الله) is a second adjective, or parenthetical (muʿtariḍa), in which case it has no grammatical position. Ibn Hishām has a view on it which we present in the section on benefits. (عليهما) is attached to (أنعم).
(ادْخُلُوا عَلَيْهِمُ الْبابَ): the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of the two men's saying.
(فَإِذا دَخَلْتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمْ غالِبُونَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached to «غالبون»; the clause (دخلتموه) is in the position of genitive by annexation; the fāʾ links the answer of (إذا); (إن) with its noun, and (غالبون) its khabar.
(وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to counsel them to rely on Allah first, and to take the means of caution and wariness second. The fāʾ in His saying «فتوكلوا» is the answer to an omitted command that must be supplied: "take heed, then rely on Allah." (على الله) is attached to (توكلوا), just as the Arabs said «زيدا فاضرب», its implied form being "take heed, then strike Zayd"; very often what is governed by [the verb] after the fāʾ comes placed before it. (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, the tāʾ its noun and (مؤمنين) its khabar; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then rely [on Him]."

* Benefits:
1- Ibn Hishām said, at the beginning of his discussion of this verse: [As for] the saying of the Exalted:
«قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما», the clause «أنعم الله عليهما» may be a supplication, in which case it is parenthetical, or a statement, in which case it is a second adjective. Its being a ḥāl (circumstantial) is weak in terms of meaning, though not weak in terms of grammatical technique, because [the noun] has been described.» This is what Ibn Hishām said. Ibn Hishām, may Allah have mercy on him, did not explain the reason for the weakness in terms of meaning: making it a ḥāl would require that their saying took place only at the time of His bestowing favour, whereas their saying is not restricted by that. In sum, being a ḥāl requires restricting the governing word, whereas the meaning is not one of restriction.
2- The wording of al-Samīn: al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said:
In this clause there are five views. The most evident is that it is a second adjective, so its position is nominative; here the more eloquent of the two usages was employed, in that the description by a prepositional phrase was placed before the description by a clause, because it is closer to the single word. The second: that it is parenthetical «[Translator's note: the printed text has «متعرضة», a misprint for «معترضة»]», and this too is evident. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يخافون»; Makkī said this.
The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «رجلان», the ḥāl coming from an indefinite noun because it has been specified by description. The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, namely «من الذين», because it occurs as the adjective of a described noun. If you make it a ḥāl, then «قد» must be implied with the past verb, according to a disagreement on the question.
3- The two men on whom Allah bestowed favour are Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn (Joshua), who was made a prophet after Mūsā, and Kālib ibn Yūqannā (Caleb); «كالب» with fatḥa or kasra on the lām.

dervis-irab:24-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَبَداً): an adverb of time; here it ties the emphasised negation to long-extended time.
(يَتِيهُونَ): they travel through the land bewildered, finding no way.
«التيه»: the open desert in which one gets lost.
(تَأْسَ): you regret and grieve; «الأسى» is grief. Its final radical may be from wāw, given their saying «رجل أسواة», i.e. much given to grief; or it may be from yāʾ, for «رجل أسيان» has been reported. In Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ:
«أسي على مصيبته», of the pattern of «صدي», i.e. he grieved; and «قد أسي له», i.e. he grieved for him.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا: يا مُوسى إِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَها أَبَداً ما دامُوا فِيها): resumptive speech introduced to indicate their persistence in disobedience. (قالوا): a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the vocative clause and what follows it is in the position of accusative as the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); (إن) with its noun; the clause (لن ندخلها) is the khabar (predicate); (أبدا) is an adverb of time attached to (ندخلها). In (ما داموا), «ما»:
is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (a temporal maṣdar particle); (داموا) is the defective (nāqiṣ) «دام», the wāw its noun, and (فيها) is attached to its omitted khabar. This adverbial [phrase] is a badal (substitute) of «أبدا», because it serves as its explanation; so it is a corresponding substitute, i.e. whole for whole. It has also been said: it is a substitute of part for whole, because «الأبد» covers all future time, while the remaining of the tyrants in it is part of it.
(فَاذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقاتِلا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, as though they harboured speech implying contempt and mockery of Allah and His Messenger. (اذهب) is an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), implied as «أنت»; (أنت) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent agent; (ربك) is conjoined to the latent agent in «اذهب», and this is permitted because of the emphasis by the pronoun, as Ibn Mālik stated in al-Khulāṣa [the Alfiyya]:
وإن على ضمير رفع متصل ... عطفت فافصل بالضمير المنفصل
(If you conjoin to an attached nominative pronoun, separate [them] with the detached pronoun.)
(فقاتلا) is conjoined to «اذهب», and the alif is the agent of (قاتل).
(إِنَّا هاهُنا قاعِدُونَ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to show their insistence that they would not advance. (إن) with its noun; the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and (هنا) is a demonstrative in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to «قاعدون»; and (قاعدون) is the khabar of (إن).
(قالَ: رَبِّ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِي وَأَخِي): the clause is resumptive, introduced to pour out [his grief] and complain to Allah, with sorrow and tenderness of heart, which are among the means by which mercy is sought and victory brought down. (قال) is a past verb, the agent being «هو»; (رب) is a vocative annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker — the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker has been discussed at length before; (إن) with its noun, and the clause is the object of saying; the clause (لا أملك) is the khabar of (إن); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (نفسي) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أخي) is one of the curiosities of i'rab: it admits the nominative, the accusative and the genitive, all equally.

The nominative readings:
The nominative is on three grounds:
1- That it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «أملك».
2- That it is conjoined to the position of (إن) with its noun.
3- That it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being: "and my brother has power only over himself."

The two accusative readings:
The accusative is on two grounds:
1- That it is conjoined to the noun of (إنّ).
2- That it is conjoined to (نفسي).

The genitive reading:
The genitive is on one ground:
that it is conjoined to the yāʾ which is genitive by the annexation of (نفس) to it.
(فَافْرُقْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (افرق) is a verb of supplication meaning: judge for us with what we deserve, and judge against them with what they deserve.
(بيننا) is an adverb attached to «افرق», and (بين القوم الفاسقين) is conjoined to «بيننا».
(قالَ فَإِنَّها مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً يَتِيهُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): the clause is resumptive; the agent of «قال» is latent, its implied form being "Allah the Exalted"; the fāʾ is redundant in i'rab, for strengthening the emphasis; (إن) with its noun, and (محرمة) its khabar; (عليهم) is attached to (محرمة); (أربعين) is an adverb of time attached to (يتيهون), in which case the prohibition is not limited to this period; or it is attached to (محرمة), in which case the prohibition is restricted to this period. (سنة) is a tamyīz (specification); the clause (فإنها محرمة) is the object of saying; and the clause (يتيهون في الأرض) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), i.e. while they are wandering lost, travelling through the wastes of the earth and the expanses of the deserts, sorrow buffeting them and bewilderment overtaking them by turns.
(فَلا تَأْسَ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. if you know this, then do not grieve. (لا) is prohibitive; (تأس) is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive (لا), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (على القوم) is attached to «تأس»; and (الفاسقين) is an adjective of (قوم).

* Benefits:
Someone may ask: how did Mūsā say "I have power only over myself and my brother," when the two men mentioned, namely Yūshaʿ and Kālib, were with them? The answer is that he did not feel assured of their steadfastness after he had seen the overwhelming majority persisting in obstinacy; and prophethood had not yet descended upon Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn, so he mentioned with himself only the infallible prophet, namely his brother Hārūn. There are lengthy stories here, for which the reader may refer to the extended works of exegesis.

dervis-irab:101-102.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَسْئَلُوا عَنْ أَشْياءَ إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ): resumptive speech brought to forbid asking much about matters that do not concern them, because being charged with them is among the things that burden souls. In this there is a loftiness worthy of taking heed and of good manners. لا is prohibitive; تسألوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); عن أشياء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to تسألوا; أشياء is a diptote, and it will be discussed at length in the section on benefits. إن is conditional; تبد is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is passive, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) referring [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «بعود» for «يعود».] to أشياء; لكم is attached to «تبد»; تسؤكم is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the conditional clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «أشياء».
