(وَإِنْ تَسْئَلُوا عَنْها حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ الْقُرْآنُ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; إن is conditional; تسألوا is the protasis; حين is an adverb of time attached to تسألوا; the clause ينزل القرآن is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); تبد is the apodosis; and لكم is attached to «تبد».
(عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْها وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ): the clause عفا الله عنها is resumptive, brought to show that the prohibition concerning them was only because of their exhaustive detail and the impossibility of carrying them out in the most perfect way, and Allah has pardoned [you] concerning them. The clause may also be a second adjective of «أشياء». The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); غفور is a first khabar (predicate) and حليم a second khabar. (قَدْ سَأَلَها قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَصْبَحُوا بِها كافِرِينَ).
The clause is either resumptive, which is preferable, or you may make it a second adjective of «أشياء». سألها is a past verb and a fronted direct object, the pronoun referring back to «أشياء»; a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "asked about the like of them", considering them similar to them in consequence and in bringing on ill effects. They have spoken at length about the referent of the pronoun to no benefit. قوم is the agent; من قبلكم is attached to an omitted adjective of قوم; ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; أصبحوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «كافرين»; and كافرين is the khabar of أصبحوا.

* Benefits:
1- It is related that Surāqa ibn Mālik, or ʿUkkāsha ibn Miḥṣan, said:
"O Messenger of Allah, is the Ḥajj [due] from us every year?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him, until he repeated his question three times. Then he ﷺ said:
"Woe to you! What makes you safe from my saying yes? By Allah, had I said yes, it would have become obligatory; and had it become obligatory, you would not have been able [to do it]; and had you abandoned it, you would have disbelieved. So leave me alone as long as I leave you alone, for those who were before you were destroyed only by their much questioning and their disagreeing with their prophets. So when I command you to do something, do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you from something, avoid it."
2- أشياء: it is a diptote. The scholars of language and grammar have delved into the reason for its being diptote, and what they have set forth can be summed up in the following views:
1- The view of Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and the majority of the Basrans:
It is diptote because of the extended alif of femininity. It is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) of «شيء», and the original form is «شيئاء» on the pattern فعلاء; the lām [i.e. the hamza, the final radical] was placed before the alif out of dislike for two hamzas coming together with an alif between them.
2- The view of al-Farrāʾ:
أشياء is a plural of «شيء», and its original form is «أشيئاء»; when two hamzas came together with an alif between them, they dropped the first hamza for lightness.
3- The view of al-Kisāʾī:
He held that the pattern of أشياء is أفعال, and that they made it diptote only by likening it to what has the alif of femininity at its end.
There are other views which we have passed over because they do not go beyond this substance.

dervis-irab:103-103.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَحِيرَةٍ): with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ; it is on the pattern faʿīla in the sense of mafʿūla (passive), and the tāʾ was attached to it irregularly, because it was stripped of its adjectival character and came to have the sense of concrete nouns. The lexicographers differed greatly about it. The strongest view about it is that the people of the Jāhiliyya, when a she-camel had produced five births, the last of them male, would slit her ear and forbid riding her; she would not be driven away from water or pasture, and when an exhausted person came upon her he would not ride her. It varies with the varying customs of the Arabs.
(سائِبَةٍ): in the Jāhiliyya a man among them would say: "If I return from my journey, or recover from my illness, then my she-camel is sāʾiba (set loose)." It was also said: when a man freed a slave, he would say: "He is sāʾiba." It is an active participle from ساب يسيب, i.e. to go loose, like the flowing of water (سيّب الماء); it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of سيّبته; one says: سيّبه فساب وانساب ("he let it loose, so it went loose and flowed").
(وَصِيلَةٍ): they differed sharply over its meaning, beyond what the present context has room for. The closest thing said about it is that the people of the Jāhiliyya, when a ewe bore a female, it was theirs, and if it bore a male, it was for their gods. It is faʿīla in the sense of fāʿila (active), so its tāʾ is regular.
(حامٍ): an active participle from حمى يحمي, when he prevents. The disagreement about it is sharp. They used to say: when ten births have been produced from the loins of a stallion, its back has become protected (ḥamā), so it is not ridden, nothing is loaded on it, and it is not prevented from water or pasture. All of these are customs, none of which Allah commanded, and He did not legislate them.

* I'rab:
(ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَحِيرَةٍ وَلا سائِبَةٍ وَلا وَصِيلَةٍ وَلا حامٍ): resumptive speech brought to condemn innovated customs and practices among their customs and practices, which Allah neither commanded nor legislated. ما is negating; جعل is in the sense of خلق ("to create"), so it takes one object, or in the sense of صيّر ("to make into"), so it takes two, the second being omitted, i.e. "made it legislated". الله is the fāʿil (agent); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; بحيرة is "genitive in form" (majrūran lafẓan) [Translator's note: so in the text, «مجرورا لفظا», in the accusative case; the expected form is «مجرور».], a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) accusative in position; and what follows it is conjoined to it. (وَلكِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; لكن and its noun; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position.
The clause يفترون is the khabar (predicate) of لكن; على الله is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يفترون; and الكذب is the direct object. The wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause لا يعقلون is the khabar of أكثرهم.

dervis-irab:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ): resumptive speech, brought to show the state of apostates in general. The i'rab of the vocative has preceded many times. من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يرتد is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the sukūn, and it was given the fatḥa because of its lightness, as has preceded under the rule of the doubled verb. منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). It has been read «يرتدد», with the assimilation undone. عن دينه is attached to يرتد; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause سوف يأتي الله is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of «من». يأتي الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بقوم is attached to يأتي; the clause يحبهم is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم; and the clause يحبونه is conjoined to the clause يحبهم. On Allah's love for the servant and the servant's love for Allah there are engaging discussions about which disagreement has raged; this is not the place to examine them, so let the reader refer to them in the long works. (أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ): أذلة is a second naʿt of قوم; على المؤمنين is attached to أذلة, which is an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha); أعزة is a third naʿt; and على الكافرين is attached to أعزّة. (يُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلا يَخافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لائِمٍ): the clause يجاهدون is a fourth naʿt of قوم, and the clause ولا يخافون is conjoined to the clause يجاهدون, so it is in effect a fifth naʿt. (ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and فضل الله its khabar. «ذلك» may be used to point to the singular, the dual and the plural, and here it points to the qualities of which the first is: يحبهم ويحبونه. The clause يؤتيه is a second khabar, or you may make it resumptive; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of يؤتيه. The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, واسع a first khabar, and عليم a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- The servant's love for Allah is by his obedience to Him; this is the kind of majāz (figurative usage) in which the effect is named by the cause.
2- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between أذلة and أعزّة.

dervis-irab:55-56.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّما وَلِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): resumptive speech, brought to establish the ruling concerning one who takes Allah, His Messenger and the believers as allies. إنما is the restraining (kāffa) ما with the restrained particle; وليكم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الله a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject), and the reverse is also permissible; رسوله is conjoined to الله, and likewise الذين آمنوا; and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause). (الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ): the relative noun is a badal (substitute) for الذين; the clause يقيمون is the ṣila, and الصلاة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and يؤتون الزكاة is conjoined to what precedes it. (وَهُمْ راكِعُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and راكعون the khabar; the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The wāw may also be conjunctive, with the clause conjoined to what preceded it, so that it falls within the ṣila of the relative noun [Translator's note: the source has «في خبر الصلة», literally "in the predicate of the ṣila"]. (وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتولّ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and الله its object; رسوله is conjoined to الله, and الذين آمنوا is also conjoined. (فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْغالِبُونَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); inna and its noun; هم is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and الغالبون is the khabar of إنّ. Or «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and الغالبون the khabar of «هم», and the clause «هم الغالبون» is the khabar of «إن». The clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». It is also possible that the apodosis is omitted because the speech indicates it, i.e. "he will prevail", with His saying «فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون» indicating it; Ibn Hishām preferred this view in al-Mughnī.

dervis-irab:57-58.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكُمْ هُزُواً وَلَعِباً): resumptive speech, brought to address some of the believers and warn them against the hypocrites.
The i'rab of the vocative word has preceded. لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause اتخذوا is the ṣila (relative clause); دينكم is the first mafʿūl bihi, هزوا the second mafʿūl bihi, and لعبا is conjoined to «هزوا». (مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَالْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِياءَ): من الذين: the preposition and its genitive noun are a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the first relative noun, or of the fāʿil of اتخذوا; the clause أوتوا is the ṣila; أوتوا is a passive imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; أُوتُوا is a passive past verb], and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); الكتاب is the second mafʿūl bihi; and من قبلكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أوتوا. الكفار is conjoined to الذين أوتوا; it has also been read in the genitive, conjoined to the relative noun made genitive by من. Makkī said: "Were it not for the agreement of the majority on the accusative, I would have chosen the genitive, for its strength in i'rab and in meaning." أولياء is the second mafʿūl bihi of تتخذوا. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun, and مؤمنين is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then fear Allah". (وَإِذا نادَيْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ اتَّخَذُوها هُزُواً وَلَعِباً): the wāw is conjunctive, joining to the ṣila of الذين, which is a mafʿūl bihi. إذا is an adverb of future time that includes the meaning of condition; the clause ناديتم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); إلى الصلاة is attached to ناديتم; the clause اتخذوها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the wāw is the fāʿil, the hāʾ the first mafʿūl bihi, هزوا the second mafʿūl bihi, and لعبا is conjoined to it. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition; أنّ with its noun and its khabar is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; لا is negative; يعقلون is an imperfect verb and the wāw its fāʿil; and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

dervis-irab:59-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَنْقِمُونَ): the imperfect of نقم, in which there are two dialect forms. The more eloquent, reported by Thaʿlab in his Faṣīḥ, is نقم with fatḥa on the qāf, ينقم with kasra on it; the other is نقم with kasra on the qāf, ينقم with fatḥa on the qāf, reported by al-Kisāʾī. Its meaning is "you resent and dislike"; it has also been said: "you disapprove". ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said:
ما نقموا من بني أمية إلّا ... أنّهم يحلمون إن غضبوا
(They resented nothing in Banū Umayya except that they are forbearing when they are angered.)

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ): resumptive speech, brought to address the People of the Book among the Children of Israel. قل is an imperative verb; يا is a vocative particle; and أهل الكتاب is a vocative in genitive construct (munādā muḍāf). (هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ): the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). هل is a particle of the interrogative of disapproval; تنقمون is an imperfect verb and the wāw its fāʿil (agent); منا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنقمون; إلا is a particle of restriction; أن with what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the object of تنقمون. It has been said that the maṣdar is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) omitted; the first view is preferable. بالله is attached to آمنا. The meaning is: you dislike nothing in us but faith; or: you are angry with us only because of our faith. (وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنا وَما أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar; the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause); إلينا is attached to أنزل; the second «ما» is conjoined to the first «ما»; the clause أنزل is the ṣila; and من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive. The majority read «أن» with fatḥa, so it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar whose position is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) omitted, the implied form being: "and your transgression is established and known to you", because you know that we are upon the truth and that you are upon falsehood; but your racialism and your love of leadership and of amassing wealth have driven you to mount this rough mount. It is possible that the position of the maṣdar is accusative, conjoined to «أن آمنا», the meaning being: "and you resent nothing in us except the combination of our faith with your rebellion and your departure from faith". Or the wāw is of accompaniment, with the interpreted maṣdar a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the implied form being: "and you resent nothing in us except faith, along with the fact that most of you are transgressors". It is also possible that its position is genitive, conjoined to الله, i.e. "and you resent nothing in us except faith in Allah, in what was sent down, and in the fact that most of you are transgressors".

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is a delightful art: confirming praise by what resembles blame (taʾkīd al-madḥ bi-mā yushbih al-dhamm).
It is an art of widespread fame, but with few examples, and I have found in the Qur'an only this verse. For the exception after the interrogative, which functions as a rebuke for the faith with which they found fault in the believers, gives the impression that after the interrogative there will come something for which its doer deserves to be resented, by which he is blamed; so when after the interrogative there came something that requires praise of its doer, the speech contained confirmation of praise by what resembles blame. The scholars of rhetoric have defined this art as the exception of an attribute of praise from an attribute of blame negated of a thing, by supposing it to be included in the negated attribute of blame. An instance is the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them, except that their swords have notches from clashing with the battalions.)
The confirmation in it is clear: he mentioned the particle of exception, «غير», before mentioning what follows it, giving the impression of excluding something from what precedes it; then, when an attribute of praise follows it, the confirmation comes. Notches in swords from much striking in wars belong to the domain of boasting and are signs of courage. Of this type also is that you affirm an attribute of praise for a thing and follow it with a particle of exception followed by another attribute of praise for that thing, as in the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: «أنا أفصح العرب بيد أني من قريش» ("I am the most eloquent of the Arabs, except that I am from Quraysh").
He mentioned the particle of exception, «بيد», which matches «غير» in pattern and meaning, before mentioning what follows it; then following it with another attribute of praise — his being from Quraysh, who are the most eloquent of the Arabs — adds beauty to the confirmation of the meaning. Al-Nābigha said, of this kind:
فتى كملت أوصافه غير أنه ... جواد فما يبقي على المال باقيا
(A youth whose qualities are perfect, except that he is generous, so he leaves nothing of wealth remaining.)

dervis-irab:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ: هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech, brought to address the Jews in a manner befitting their defiance, their obstinacy and their deep penetration into disbelief.
قل is an imperative verb, and the interrogative clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). هل is an interrogative particle; أنبئكم is an imperfect verb in the position of an accusative [Translator's note: so in the source; أنبئكم is in fact a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and it is the clause that is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying], and the kāf is its first object; بشرّ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the second object; من ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «شرّ», because it is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl); مثوبة is a tamyīz (specification) of شر, and it is a tamyīz of relation (tamyīz nisba), because الشر applies to persons; more detail will come in the section on Rhetoric. عند ذلك [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic text is عند الله] is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ): من is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); for when He said: "Shall I inform you of what is worse than that?", it is as though someone said: "Who is that?" and it was said: "He is the one whom Allah has cursed"; the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative. The position of «من» may also be genitive as a badal (substitute) for «شر». The clause لعنه الله has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause غضب عليه is conjoined to the ṣila. (وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنازِيرَ وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ): the wāw is conjunctive; جعل is conjoined to لعنه الله; منهم is attached to something omitted that is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and القردة is the second object; الخنازير is conjoined to القردة. عبد is a past verb, conjoined to the ṣila of «ما» [Translator's note: so in the source; the relative noun here is «من»], as though it were said: "and whoever worshipped the ṭāghūt"; the relative noun was omitted and the attribute (ṣifa) set in its place. (أُولئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً وَأَضَلُّ عَنْ سَواءِ السَّبِيلِ): the clause is explicative with no grammatical position; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and شر the khabar; مكانا is a tamyīz; أضل is conjoined to شر; and عن سواء السبيل is attached to أضلّ.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains several kinds of rhetoric, which we set out below:
1- al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical figurative usage) in His saying: «مثوبة» ("recompense"), the relation being contrariety, like: «فبشرهم بعذاب أليم» ("so give them glad tidings of a painful punishment"). What is intended by this majāz is sarcasm (tahakkum). The overall meaning is: Say, O Muḥammad, to these who have taken your religion as play and amusement, of those who were given the Book before you and the disbelievers: "Shall I inform you of what is worse than the people of that which you resent in us, and worse than its recompense?", i.e. its punishment. The speech was framed according to their saying and their belief; otherwise there is no sharing between the believers and them in the very fact of punishment, such that it could be said that the punishment of one of the two parties is worse than that of the other. But they judged that the religion of Islam was evil, so it was said to them: suppose the matter is so; yet the curse of Allah the Exalted and His anger, being kept far from His mercy, being driven out of the court of His good pleasure, and the transformation of form into the ugliest and vilest kinds of animal, are worse than that which you claim is evil. And you know what baseness and vileness belong to the two kinds, apes and swine, and what ugliness, deformity, hideousness of appearance, meanness of soul, lowliness of worth, baseness of nature, repulsiveness of form and character, ugliness of voice and lowness of aspiration they have in the minds of common people and elite alike — such as no other kinds of animal have.
2- Sarcasm (tahakkum): it is contained within the majāz mursal. Sarcasm has been discussed in detail before.
3- al-majāz al-mursal in His saying: «شر مكانا» ("worse in place"), its relation being locality (maḥalliyya): He mentioned the place and meant its people. This too has preceded.

* Benefits:
You may say: an elative noun must have something preferred and something over which it is preferred, so how can it be said that they are worse than the believers, when the believers have no evil at all?
The answer is that it came by way of concession and granting the opponent his claim, to silence him and proclaim against him the crushing argument; or that it is specific to the disbelievers, who are of differing grades in the measure of evil ascribed to them.

dervis-irab:61-62.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا جاؤُكُمْ قالُوا آمَنَّا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to address the Prophet ﷺ and those with him. إذا is an adverb of future time that includes the meaning of condition; the clause جاءوكم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); جاءوكم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and the clause آمنا is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا بِالْكُفْرِ وَهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا بِهِ): the wāw is circumstantial and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); the clause دخلوا is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «قالوا»; بالكفر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of دخلوا. The second wāw is also circumstantial, and the clause is likewise in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the wāw in «قالوا»; به is attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of خرجوا, i.e. "they entered as disbelievers and left as disbelievers". (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما كانُوا يَكْتُمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم the khabar (predicate); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم; the clause كانوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); and the clause يكتمون is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا. (وَتَرى كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ): the wāw is conjunctive or resumptive; ترى is an imperfect verb; كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi; منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); the clause يسارعون is a ḥāl of «كثيرا», or a naʿt of it; في الإثم is attached to يسارعون; and العدوان is conjoined to الإثم. (وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): أكلهم is conjoined to الإثم and العدوان; السحت is the mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is «أكل»; the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; ما is a complete indefinite noun in the position of an accusative as a tamyīz (specification), or a relative noun, in which case it is the fāʿil; the clause كانوا has no grammatical position on either view; and the clause يعملون is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:104-105.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ: تَعالَوْا إِلى ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the coming apodosis; the clause تعالوا is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إلى ما أنزل الله: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تعالوا; أنزل الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is a ṣila (relative clause); and إلى الرسول is conjoined to it. (قالُوا حَسْبُنا ما وَجَدْنا عَلَيْهِ آباءَنا): the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; حسبنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ما is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate); the clause وجدنا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; عليه is attached to وجدنا; and آباءنا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أَوَلَوْ كانَ آباؤُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئاً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; the wāw is conjunctive, [conjoining] to something implied, its implied form being "Is that sufficient for them?", or circumstantial, i.e. "even if their fathers were ignorant and astray". لو is conditional and its apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "they say that". كان and its noun; the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar; شيئا is a direct object; and the clause لا يهتدون is conjoined to the clause لا يعلمون. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): the clause is resumptive, brought to show that every person is responsible for himself. It cannot be objected to this that it offers a way out of commanding right and forbidding wrong, because that is contingent upon capacity.
He ﷺ said: "Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; and if he is unable, then with his heart." عليكم is a transferred verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr manqūl) in the sense of "hold to" (الزموا), and أنفسكم is the direct object of the verbal noun. (لا يَضُرُّكُمْ مَنْ ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ): the clause is resumptive; لا is negating; يضركم is an imperfect verb, and the kāf is the direct object; من is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the agent of يضركم [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «بضركم».]; the clause ضل is the ṣila; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to the implied apodosis, i.e. "then he does not harm you"; and the clause اهتديتم is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa). (إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعاً فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): the clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مرجعكم is a delayed mubtadaʾ; جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); فينبئكم: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ينبئكم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object; بما is attached to ينبئكم; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; the tāʾ is the noun of كان; and the clause تعملون is its khabar.

* Benefits:
The grammarians differed about the pronoun attached to «عليكم», «إليكم», «لديكم» and «مكانكم». The correct view is that it is in the position of the genitive, as it was before the word was transferred to [the function of] incitement (ighrāʾ); it is either genitive by the preposition, as in «عليكم», according to what it was, or by construct, as in «لديكم». It was also said: the kāf is a particle of address, and this view is, in my opinion, simpler; Ibn Bābashādh supported it. We give here an important summary of verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl); they are of two kinds:
1- Improvised (murtajal): that which was coined as such from the outset, i.e. as a name for the verb, such as شتان ("how far apart!"), أفّ ("ugh!") and صه ("hush!").
2- Transferred (manqūl): that which was coined from the outset for something other than a verbal noun and was then transferred from it to that. It is of three kinds:
a- From a preposition and its genitive noun, such as عليك in the sense of "hold to" (الزم).
b- From an adverb of place, such as دونك الكتاب, i.e. "take it"; مكانك, i.e. "stay firm"; أمامك, i.e. "go forward"; and وراءك, i.e. "step aside".
c- Transferred from a maṣdar (verbal noun), such as رويد خالدا, i.e. "give Khālid time", and بله هذا الأمر, i.e. "leave this matter aside".
A poet said, describing swords:
تذر الجماجم ضاحيا هاماتها ... بله الأكفّ كأنها لم تخلق
(They leave the skulls with their crowns laid bare — let alone the hands — as if they had never been created.)
And Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī used it, saying:
أقلّ فعالي بله أكثره مجد ... وذا الجد فيه نلت أم لم أنل جدّ
(The least of my deeds — let alone the most of them — is glory; and this earnestness is earnestness, whether I attained good fortune or not.)
Verbal nouns have other details, which may be consulted in their proper places.

dervis-irab:106-108.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): i.e. you travelled.
(الْأَوْلَيانِ): dual of الأولى, i.e. the two most entitled to give testimony because of their kinship and their knowledge.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ حِينَ الْوَصِيَّةِ اثْنانِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ): resumptive speech brought to set out rulings relating to the affairs of this world, after setting out the states relating to the affairs of the Hereafter. شهادة is a mubtadaʾ (subject); بينكم is muḍāf ilayhi; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted apodosis, i.e. "then [it is] the testimony of two"; the clause حضر أحدكم الموت is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); حين الوصية is an adverb attached to حضر; and اثنان is the khabar (predicate) of شهادة. An omitted muḍāf must be implied so that the mubtadaʾ and the khabar correspond, because the testimony cannot itself be the two [men], since a concrete being cannot be a khabar of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Zamakhsharī allowed شهادة to be a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e. "among what has been prescribed for you is testimony", with اثنان being the fāʿil (agent) of شهادة, i.e.
"that two should testify". This is also what Ibn Hishām followed. ذوا عدل is a naʿt (adjective) of «اثنان», and منكم is also an adjective. (أَوْ آخَرانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): أو is a conjunction; آخران is conjoined to «اثنان»; من غيركم is attached to an omitted adjective of «آخران», i.e. from other than your religious community; إن is conditional; أنتم is the agent of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then the two witnesses are two others"; the clause ضربتم is explicative with no grammatical position; في الأرض is attached to ضربتم; and the conditional clause is parenthetical with no grammatical position. (فَأَصابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةُ الْمَوْتِ تَحْبِسُونَهُما مِنْ بَعْدِ الصَّلاةِ): the fāʾ is conjunctive, for sequence with immediacy; أصابتكم is conjoined to ضربتم; مصيبة الموت is the agent of أصابتكم; تحبسونهما is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). They differed about the position of this clause; the most apparent view is that it is an adjective of «آخران».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the position of تحبسونهما? I say: it is a resumption of speech, as if it were said, after the stipulation of probity in them: 'So what are we to do if we have doubts about them?' and it was said: 'Detain them.'" Abū Ḥayyān commented on that, saying:
"What al-Zamakhsharī said about resumption is more apparent than the adjectival reading, because of the long separation, by the condition and what is conjoined to it, between the thing described and its adjective; and there is nothing necessitating this claim." [Translator's note: so in the text; the last clause appears to sit oddly with the preceding one.]
من بعد الصلاة is attached to تحبسونهما. (فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ لا نَشْتَرِي بِهِ ثَمَناً وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى): the fāʾ is conjunctive; يقسمان is conjoined to تحبسونهما; بالله is attached to يقسمان; إن is conditional; ارتبتم is a verb and its agent in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, its implied form being: "if you have doubts about them, then make them swear". The protasis and its implied apodosis form a clause with no grammatical position, because it is parenthetical between the oath and its answer. This verse is not among those in which a condition and an oath come together so that the earlier of the two is answered and the answer of the other is omitted because the answer of the condition indicates it, because that case is conditional on the oath being fit to serve as the answer of the condition, so that it stands in place of its answer, as in: "By Allah, if you visit me I will surely honour you" — for if you imply "If you visit me, I will honour you", it is correct. Here, the answer of the condition is not implied as being what is the answer of the oath; rather its answer is implied as an independent oath. Do you not see that its implied form here is "if you have doubts, make them swear", and that if you implied something other than that it would not be correct! Others said: there is an omitted saying, its implied form being: "then they swear by Allah and say this saying in their oaths".
The Arabs often leave the saying implied, as in His words, the Exalted: «والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب سلام», i.e. saying: «سلام عليكم». لا is negating; نشتري is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of the oath; به is attached to نشتري; ثمنا is the direct object; the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), i.e. the one for whom the oath is sworn; ذا قربى is the khabar of كان; the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.
"then we will not sell it"; and the conditional clause of لو and what is in its domain is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلا نَكْتُمُ شَهادَةَ اللَّهِ إِنَّا إِذاً لَمِنَ الْآثِمِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive, and the clause لا نكتم is conjoined to what is arranged with it under the ruling of the oath; شهادة الله is the direct object; إن and its noun; إذن is an inoperative particle of answer and requital; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); من الآثمين is attached to an omitted khabar of إن; and the clause إن and what is in its domain has no grammatical position, serving as the cause for not concealing. (فَإِنْ عُثِرَ عَلى أَنَّهُمَا اسْتَحَقَّا إِثْماً): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; عثر is a passive past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; على أنهما is a preposition and its genitive noun as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. "if it is discovered that they deserved sin"; أن and its noun; the clause استحقا is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن; the alif is the agent of استحقا; and إثما is the object of استحقا. (فَآخَرانِ يَقُومانِ مَقامَهُما مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَوْلَيانِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; آخران is a mubtadaʾ — beginning with it is permissible because it is a description — or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause يقومان is in the position of the nominative as khabar on the first view, or an adjective on the second; مقامهما is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); من الذين is an adjective of «آخران»; the clause استحق has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); عليهم is attached to استحق; الأوليان is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the two most entitled", or the agent of استحق; and the clause فآخران is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ لَشَهادَتُنا أَحَقُّ مِنْ شَهادَتِهِما): the fāʾ is conjunctive; يقسمان is an imperfect verb in the nominative, conjoined to يقومان; the alif is the agent; بالله is attached to يقسمان; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; شهادتنا is a mubtadaʾ and أحق the khabar; من شهادتهما is attached to أحق; and the clause شهادتنا has no grammatical position because it occurs as the answer of the oath. (وَمَا اعْتَدَيْنا إِنَّا إِذاً لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is negating; اعتدينا is a past verb and its agent; إن and its noun; إذن is an inoperative particle of answer and requital; من الظالمين is the khabar of إن; and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِالشَّهادَةِ عَلى وَجْهِها): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and أدنى the khabar, and the clause is resumptive; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in construct with أدنى; بالشهادة is attached to يأتوا; and على وجهها is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَوْ يَخافُوا أَنْ تُرَدَّ أَيْمانٌ بَعْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): أو is a conjunction; يخافوا is conjoined to يأتوا; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, the object of يخافوا; أيمان is the deputy agent of ترد; the adverb بعد is attached to «ترد»; and أيمانهم is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْمَعُوا وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object; اسمعوا is conjoined to اتقوا; the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is the direct object; and الفاسقين is an adjective of القوم.

* Benefits:
These three verses have greatly occupied the exegetes and the parsers, and they have spoken at length, though there is nothing calling for length. Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib mentioned in his book called «al-Kashf» that these verses, in their readings, i'rab, exegesis, meanings and rulings, are among the most difficult verses of the Qur'an. Al-Sakhāwī said:
"I have not seen anyone among the scholars whose discussion of them came out clear from beginning to end." Al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī said: "I seek Allah's help in accounting for their i'rab, the derivation of their single words, the morphology of their words, their readings and knowledge of their composition; as for the rest of their sciences, we ask Allah for help in refining it." We for our part have tried to be as brief as possible, and have confined ourselves to the reading of Ḥafṣ; as for the rest of their rulings, one must consult the books of ḥadīth and the lengthy books of exegesis.

dervis-irab:27-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قُرْباناً): «القربان», with ḍamma on the qāf; there are two views on it:
1- It is a noun for that by which one draws near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whether charity, a sacrifice or other than that; like «الحلوان», also with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ: the name of what is given (yuḥlā, i.e. given).
One says: «قرّب صدقة» and «تقرّب بها», because «تقرّب» is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «قرّب».
2- That it was originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and was then applied to the thing by which one draws near, as in their saying «نسج اليمن» (the weave of Yemen, i.e. what is woven). Evidence for this is that it was not put in the dual, though the place calls for the dual, because each of Qābīl and Hābīl had his own offering, and the base form would be to say «قربانين». The holders of the first view said: there is no proof in this, because the meaning is: when each one of them offered an offering, as in the saying of the Exalted: «فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة» (then flog them eighty lashes), i.e. each one of them eighty lashes.
(تَبُوءَ): you return [bearing].

* I'rab:
(وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ بِالْحَقِّ): the clause is conjoined to the implied verb in His saying «وإذ قال موسى لقومه», meaning: "mention, O Muḥammad, to your people and tell them the account of the two sons of Ādam," namely Hābīl and Qābīl, and the story of the offering and its cause. The story of Qābīl's killing of Hābīl fills the lengthy works of exegesis.
(اتل) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; (عليهم) is attached to «اتل»; (نبأ) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ابني) is annexed to «نبأ», the nūn having been dropped because of annexation; (آدم) is annexed to «ابني»; (بالحق) is attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a recitation bound up with the truth"; or [it is] a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), so the implied form is: "while you are bound up with the truth," i.e. with truthfulness; or from the direct object, i.e. "recite their account as bound up with truth and truthfulness."
(إِذْ قَرَّبا قُرْباناً فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِما وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الْآخَرِ): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (نبأ), i.e. "recite their story and their account that took place at that time"; or it is a badal (substitute) from it, i.e. "and recite to them the account, the account of that time," supposing the omission of the muḍāf. The clause (قربا) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (قربا) is a verb and its agent, and (قربانا) is the direct object. In (فتقبل): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تقبل) is a past verb in the passive; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as «هو», referring to «قربانا»; (من أحدهما), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (تقبل); and (ولم يتقبل من الآخر) is conjoined to (تقبل).
(قالَ: لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ قالَ: إِنَّما يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the clause (لأقتلنك) is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); (أقتلنك) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it must be emphasised with the heavy nūn; the kāf is the direct object. (إنما) is [inna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); and the clause (إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين) is the object of saying.
(لَئِنْ بَسَطْتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِي ما أَنَا بِباسِطٍ يَدِيَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ): the lām prepares for the oath; (إن) is conditional; (بسطت) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ being the agent; (إلي) is attached to (بسطت); (يدك) is the direct object; and the clause is resumptive, explaining what he meant to say. In (لتقتلني), the lām is the causal lām; (تقتلني) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ the direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بسطت). (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative, operating like «ليس»; (أنا) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (باسط) is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position as its khabar (predicate); (يدي) is the direct object of (باسط), because it is an active participle; (إليك) is attached to (باسط). In (لأقتلك), the lām is the causal lām, and (أقتلك) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām. The clause is the answer to the oath because [the oath] precedes the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it.
(إِنِّي أَخافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ): the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); (إن) with its noun, and the clause (أخاف الله) its khabar; and (رب العالمين) is a badal from (الله) or an adjective.
(إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ النَّارِ): the clause is a second reason for his refraining from fighting, after the first reason. (إن) with its noun; the clause (أريد) is its khabar, the agent being latent, implied as «أنا»; (أن تبوء) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of accusative as the direct object of (أريد); (بإثمي), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted [element] in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (تبوء), i.e. "you return carrying it," or "bound up with it." In (فتكون), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تكون) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb conjoined to (تبوء), following it in the accusative; its noun is «أنت»; and (من أصحاب النار) is attached to the omitted khabar of (تكون).
(وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and (جزاء الظالمين) is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين» there is comprehensive, all-encompassing speech (al-kalām al-jāmiʿ al-māniʿ): this clause gathers many meanings in brief words, for it contains the gist of the story from beginning to end, and the story is long; the reader will find it in the lengthy works. The gist of the meaning is that Allah the Exalted accepts obedience only from a God-fearing believer. It is reported of ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh that he wept when death came to him, and it was said to him:
"What makes you weep? You were such-and-such and such-and-such." He said: "I hear Allah saying: «إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين»."
2- In His saying «إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك» there is the device of ittisāʿ (amplitude).
It is that the speaker brings speech in which interpretation is wide, according to what its words can bear, so that its interpretation widens according to people's intellects and the differences in their understanding. In the verse it lies in his wanting his brother's sin, because its meaning is: "I do not want to kill you and be punished."
Since one of two things had to be wanted — either his own sin, supposing that he defended himself and killed his brother, or his brother's sin, supposing that he surrendered — and he did not want the first, he was compelled to the second. So he did not then want his brother's sin for its own sake; rather he meant that sin lies in defending oneself in a way that leads to killing, which was not lawful at that time, and from that it followed that he wanted his brother's sin. This is like a person's wishing for martyrdom.
Its meaning is that the unbeliever returns bearing his killing and the sin he incurs thereby; but [the martyr] did not intend the unbeliever's sin for its own sake; he only wanted to give himself in the way of Allah, hoping [for that], the unbeliever's sin in killing coming implicitly and consequentially. What indicates this is that there is no difference in attaining the rank of martyrdom and its merit between the killer dying in unbelief and his life being sealed with faith, so that the sin of the killing, through which the martyr became a martyr, is annulled for him — I mean, whether the sin remains on his killer or is annulled for him, that neither diminishes nor increases the merit of his martyrdom. If the unbeliever's sin in killing were intended, the wish would differ according to its remaining or being annulled. So this shows that it is a necessary, consequential matter, not an intended one.

Views of the scholars:
The scholars of exegesis, grammar and rhetoric have spoken at length «[Translator's note: the printed text has «أقاض», a misprint for «أفاض»]» on this verse. What they have presented comes down to three interpretations:
a- That it is with the omission of the interrogative hamza, i.e. «إني أريد أأن تبوء؟» (do I want that you should return…?); and it is a disapproving question, because wanting disobedience is disobedience.
b- That «لا» is omitted, the implied form being «إني أريد أن لا تبوء بإثمي» (I want that you not return with my sin), like the saying of the Exalted: «يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا» (Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray), i.e. that you not go astray.
c- That the wanting is as it stands, being either figurative or real wanting; wanting that was permissible for him for reasons the exegetes mentioned, among them that indications appeared to him showing that his death was near, that his brother was an unbeliever, and that wanting punishment for an unbeliever is good.
3- The condition came in the form of a verb, namely His saying «بسطت», and the answer in the form of an active participle, namely His saying «ما أنا بباسط», to convey that he does not do what would earn this abominable deed; therefore He emphasised it with the redundant bāʾ that emphasises the negation.
Al-Mutanabbī and ittisāʿ:
In any case, this verse and the ittisāʿ in it appear to be among the things subtle for the understanding; but it is a necessary subtlety, containing many meanings drawn out from the speech. Al-Mutanabbī gazed toward its heaven, and he very often inclined to this kind of eloquence, so that his speech became subtle. Among his ittisāʿ is his saying:
لولا مفارقة الأحباب ما وجدت ... لها المنايا إلى أرواحنا سبلا
(Were it not for parting from loved ones, the fates would not have found for themselves paths to our souls.)
The outward form of the speech suggests at first glance that «لها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «وجدت»; but that would involve the verb of an overt [agent] passing to that agent's own attached pronoun, which is not allowed. So it must be taken as originally an adjective of «سبلا», which became a ḥāl when it was placed before it; and His saying «إلى أرواحنا» is likewise, since the meaning is: "paths travelled to our souls." You also have a strange view on «لها»: that you take «لها» as the plural of «لهاة» (uvula), like «حصى» and «حصاة», with «المنايا» annexed to it; ascribing uvulas to the fates is then a metaphor, likening them to something that swallows people; and he put «اللها» in place of mouths because the uvulas are adjacent to the [sense of] taste «[Translator's note: the text reads «للنعم»; perhaps a misprint for «للطعم» (taste) or «للفم» (the mouth)]». «اللهاة», with fatḥa, is the piece of flesh overhanging the throat at the far end of the roof of the mouth.
Of this kind is his saying in love poetry:
كشفت ثلاث ذوائب من شعرها ... في ليلة فأرت ليالي أربعا
واستقبلت قمر السماء بوجهها ... فأرتني القمرين في وقت معا
(She uncovered three locks of her hair in one night, and showed four nights; and she faced the moon of the sky with her face, and showed me the two moons at one time together.)
The meaning is not as people think, that he saw two moons at one time, the moon and her face; rather, the accurate view is that when she faced the moon of the sky, its image was imprinted on her face, so he saw both at one time, just as shapes face a mirror and the image is imprinted in it, so you see the mirror and the shapes imprinted in it at one time together.
Al-Tibrīzī erred when he explained the verse, saying: it is possible that he meant a moon and a moon, because two real moons do not come together in one night, just as the sun and moon do not come together. One of the poets clung to the fringes of al-Mutanabbī and composed two verses most like sleight-of-hand and tricks:
رأت قمر السماء فذكرتني ... ليالي وصلها بالرقمتين
كلانا ناظر قمرا ولكن ... رأيت بعينها ورأت بعيني
(She saw the moon of the sky and reminded me of the nights of her union at al-Raqmatayn; each of us gazes at a moon, but I saw with her eye and she saw with mine.)
The best that can be said about them is that "two moons" means a real moon, which is the moon of the sky, and a figurative moon, which is the face of the beloved. So he says: she saw the figurative moon, which is the moon of the sky, and I saw her face, which is the real moon; because she looked at the moon of the sky and he looked at her face, so it holds true that he saw with her eye and she saw with his. This is hyperbole and excess in description; but the poets have customarily made the beloved the real moon and the one in the sky the figurative moon. Others said in explaining them:
This poet alludes «[Translator's note: the printed text has «يتسير», apparently a misprint for «يشير»]» to the moon of the sky being one of his beloved's lovers, and that his beloved saw it one night and, by her seeing it, clothed it with the light of her beauty and the charms of her qualities, cast her likeness upon it, and lent it her name. So she reminded this lover of those nights of union at al-Raqmatayn, and that by her union with him she annihilated him and overcame him with her qualities, until she became with him like a single moon, and both look at it. Hence he said "each of us gazes at a moon," i.e. a single moon whose manifestation became multiple; but she looks at it with his eye, which is the eye of love, because the lover has become beloved; and he looks with her eye, because she lent him an eye with which he saw her, so it is as though the one who sees her is she herself. The discussion of ittisāʿ is long; we content ourselves here with what has been said.

dervis-irab:30-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طوّعت): made easy and made attractive; from «طاع المرعى له», when the pasture became ample for him.
(سَوْأَةَ): «السوءة», with fatḥa on the sīn: the private parts, and what of the body may not be uncovered. «السوءة» is also disgrace. The «سوءة» was singled out for mention because concern for covering it is greater.

* I'rab:
(فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (طوعت) is a past verb; (له) is attached to (طوعت); (نفسه) is the fāʿil (agent); (قتل أخيه) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فقتله) is also conjoined, and (فأصبح) is also conjoined, its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as «هو»; and (من الخاسرين): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar (predicate).
(فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُراباً يَبْحَثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (بعث) is a past verb, (الله) the agent and (غرابا) the direct object; the clause (يبحث في الأرض) is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «غرابا»; and (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يبحث).
(لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوارِي سَوْأَةَ أَخِيهِ): the lām is causal; (يريه) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām, and the hāʾ is the direct object; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بعث), so the latent pronoun in the verb refers to Allah; they may also be attached to (يبحث), i.e. it digs and stirs up the earth in order to show, so the latent pronoun refers to the raven. The interrogative clause suspends (muʿalliqa) the visual seeing, so it is in the position of accusative as a second object, standing in its place; because «رأى» of sight, before being made transitive by the hamza, takes one object, and by the hamza it acquired another object, which is the first object. Its like has come before in the saying of the Exalted:
«رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى» (My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead).
(قالَ يا وَيْلَتى أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هذَا الْغُرابِ): the clause is resumptive, as though said as an answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: what did he say when he saw the raven doing that? (يا) is a vocative particle; (ويلتا) is a word of anguish and sorrow. He called it as though woe were not present with him, so he called it to come: "O woe, come, for this is the time for your coming."
You may also take the one addressed as omitted and make «الويل» accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb which the Arabs let fall out of use; the alif is a substitute for the yāʾ of the speaker; and the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The hamza is for interrogation and wonder, as though he wondered at himself:
how was he not guided to what the raven was guided to? (عجزت) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is included in the object of saying. (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (أكون) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative by (أن); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (عجزت), i.e. «أعجزت [عن]»; the noun of (أكون) is a latent pronoun implied as «أنا»; (مثل) is the khabar of (أكون); (هذا) is a demonstrative, the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (الغراب) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative.
(فَأُوارِيَ سَوْأَةَ أَخِي فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ النَّادِمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (أواري) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (أن أكون). This is preferable to making it causative (sababiyya) because it is preceded by an interrogative, [in which case] (أواري) would be an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causative fāʾ; for the fāʾ that occurs as the answer to an interrogative forms, from the interrogative clause and the answer, a condition and its consequence, and here that is not formed. You say: «أتزورني فأكرمك» (will you visit me so that I honour you?), meaning: «إن تزرني أكرمك» (if you visit me I will honour you). But if you said here: «إن أعجز عن أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب أوار سوءة أخي» (if I am unable to be like this raven, I will cover my brother's corpse), it would not be correct, because the covering does not result from his inability to be like the raven. For this reason we have considered the conjunction preferable. (سوءة أخي) is the direct object. In (فأصبح) the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أصبح) is a defective past verb, its noun a latent pronoun implied as «هو», and (من النادمين) its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (majāz) in His saying «يا ويلتا», because he called upon something that does not reason, whereas the basis of the vocative is that it be addressed to one who reasons.

* Benefits:
This story which the Quran has presented is fit to be the kernel of a great story; it needs a creative pen to make of it a splendid work of art. It is reported that Ādam remained for a hundred years after the killing of Hābīl without laughing, and that he lamented him in poetry; this is a falsely attributed lie, for it is established that the prophets do not compose poetry. Maymūn ibn Mihrān reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: whoever says that Ādam composed poetry has lied; rather he would mourn over him and describe his grief in prose speech resembling an elegy; then the centuries handed it down, and when it reached Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān, who was the first to write in Arabic, he put it into verse and said:
تغيّرت البلاد ومن عليها ... فوجه الأرض مغير قبيح
(The lands and those upon them have changed; the face of the earth is dust-covered and ugly.)
They mentioned six verses after this one; and not content with that, they fabricated a report whose content is that Iblīs answered him in the same metre and rhyme with five verses. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «All of that is sheer lies, and the poetry is nothing but falsely attributed and full of grammatical errors.» Al-Zamakhsharī is pointing to the second verse, which is:
تغيّر كل ذي لون وطعم ... وقل بشاشة الوجه المليح
(Everything of colour and taste has changed, and the cheerfulness of the comely face has diminished.)
They transmitted it with iqwāʾ (a vowel fault in the rhyme), i.e. with «المليح» in the genitive. Some transmit it with «بشاشة» in the accusative without nunation and «الوجه المليح» in the nominative, and then it is not an error; they explained it as the dropping of the nunation from «بشاشة» and its being accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Our philosopher-poet Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī alluded to this story in Risālat al-Ghufrān; refer to it if you wish — and may Allah protect you. He singled out the Children of Israel with this story, as will come, because killing was their habit, even reaching the prophets.

dervis-irab:109-110.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَكْمَهَ): the blind person whose sight is wiped out.

* I'rab:
(يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ: ماذا أُجِبْتُمْ): resumptive speech brought to set out what took place between Him and all the messengers. يوم is an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); the clause يجمع is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); الله is the fāʿil (agent); الرسل is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is a conjunction; يقول is an imperfect verb conjoined to يجمع; ماذا is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "with what answer were you answered?" You may also parse «ما» as an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» as a relative noun, the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; the clause أجبتم has no grammatical position in either case; similar cases have preceded. The clause ماذا أجبتم is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(قالُوا: لا عِلْمَ لَنا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ): قالوا is a verb and its agent, and the clause is resumptive; لا is the lā of generic negation; علم is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; لنا is attached to its omitted khabar; the clause لا علم لنا is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; إن and its noun; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and علام الغيوب the khabar of أنت, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إن; and the clause إن and what is in its domain is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (إِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): إذ is an adverb of past time, attached to what يوم is attached to, because it is a badal (substitute) from it; the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by construct; يا is a vocative particle; عيسى is a single proper-name vocative, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, in the position of the accusative; ابن is a badal from, or a naʿt (adjective) of, عيسى; and مريم is muḍāf ilayhi. (اذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكَ وَعَلى والِدَتِكَ): the whole clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; اذكر is an imperative verb; نعمتي is the direct object; عليك is attached to نعمتي; and على والدتك is conjoined to «عليك». (إِذْ أَيَّدْتُكَ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا): the adverb is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from نعمتي, and it may also be attached to نعمتي; the clause أيدتك is in the position of the genitive by construct; بروح القدس is attached to أيدتك; the clause تكلم الناس is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in أيدتك; في المهد is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. while you were an infant; and كهلا is conjoined to it, so it too is a ḥāl. The meaning is: joining the state of infancy to the state of maturity in perfection of intellect and completeness of reflection. (وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the adverb is conjoined to إذ أيدتك; the clause علمتك is in the position of the genitive by construct, and it is a verb, its agent and its first direct object; الكتاب is a second direct object, i.e. writing; and what follows it is conjoined to it. (وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ بِإِذْنِي): the adverb is conjoined to what preceded it; the clause تخلق is in the position of the genitive by construct; من الطين is attached to تخلق; كهيئة: the kāf is a noun in the sense of مثل ("like"), in the position of the accusative as the direct object of تخلق; هيئة is muḍāf ilayhi and is itself muḍāf; الطير is muḍāf ilayhi; and بإذني is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَتَنْفُخُ فِيها فَتَكُونُ طَيْراً بِإِذْنِي)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; تنفخ is conjoined to تخلق; فيها is attached to تنفخ; فتكون is conjoined to فتنفخ; طيرا is the khabar of تكون; and بإذني is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَتُبْرِئُ الْأَكْمَهَ وَالْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِي): conjoined to what precedes. (وَإِذْ تُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتى بِإِذْنِي): likewise conjoined. (وَإِذْ كَفَفْتُ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَنْكَ): likewise conjoined; بني إسرائيل is the object of كففت; and عنك is attached to «كففت». (إِذْ جِئْتَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the adverb is attached to كففت, not with regard to the coming with clear proofs alone, but with regard to what followed that and resulted from it, when they intended to kill him; the clause جئتهم is in the position of the genitive by construct; بالبينات is attached to جئتهم; فقال: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and قال is a past verb conjoined to جئتهم; الذين is the agent; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); منهم is attached to كفروا; إن is negating; هذا is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; سحر is the khabar of هذا; مبين is a naʿt; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.

dervis-irab:111-113.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مائِدَةً): al-māʾida is the table (khiwān) when there is food on it; if there is no food on it, it is not a māʾida. This is the well-known view, as al-Thaʿālibī stated; however, al-Rāghib said: al-māʾida is the tray on which there is food, and it is also said of the food itself. But this goes against what is well known and widely recognized among the scholars of language.
This matter has parallels in the language: a khiwān is not called māʾida unless there is food on it — otherwise it is a khiwān, with the khāʾ vowelled in three ways. One does not say kaʾs unless there is wine in it — otherwise it is a qadaḥ (cup). One does not say dhanūb or sajl unless there is water in it — otherwise it is a dalw (bucket). One does not say jirāb unless it is tanned — otherwise it is ihāb (raw hide). One does not say:
qalam unless it is sharpened — otherwise it is unbūb (a reed tube). One does not say kūz unless it has a handle — otherwise it is kūb. One does not say farw unless there is wool on it — otherwise it is its skin. One does not say rayṭa unless it is of two joined pieces — otherwise it is mulāʾa (a sheet). One does not say:
rumḥ unless it has a spearhead on it — otherwise it is qanāt (a shaft). One does not say laṭīma unless it carries perfume — otherwise it is ʿīr (a caravan). One does not say khātam unless it has a stone set in it — otherwise it is fatkha. This is what al-Thaʿālibī mentioned, transmitting from Abū ʿUbayda.
And it is transmitted from leading lexicographers other than Abū ʿUbayda: one does not say nafaq unless it has an exit — otherwise it is sarab (a burrow). One does not say ʿihn unless it is dyed — otherwise it is ṣūf (wool). One does not say khidr unless it encloses a young woman — otherwise it is sitr (a curtain). One does not say rakiyya unless there is water in it, little or much — otherwise it is biʾr (a well). One does not say waqūd unless fire has gone forward in it — otherwise it is ḥaṭab (firewood).
One does not say siyāʿ unless there is straw in it — otherwise it is ṭīn (clay). One does not say ʿawīl unless there is raising of the voice in it — otherwise it is bukāʾ (weeping). One does not say tharā unless it is moist — otherwise it is turāb (dust). One does not call a slave ābiq unless his going is without fear or toil of work — otherwise he is hārib (a fugitive). One does not call the water of the mouth ruḍāb except as long as it is in the mouth — otherwise it is buzāq (spittle). One does not call a brave man kamiyy unless he is fully armed — otherwise he is baṭal (a hero). And one does not call a woman ẓaʿīna except as long as she is riding in the howdah. Further, the lexicographers differed on the derivation of māʾida. Abū ʿUbayda said — and al-Zamakhsharī chose it — that it is fāʿila in the sense of mafʿūla, derived from مادة, i.e. "he gave him", and امتاده in the sense of "he asked him for a gift"; so it has the sense of mafʿūla, like «عيشة راضية» ("a pleasing [i.e. pleasant] life").

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى الْحَوارِيِّينَ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِي وَبِرَسُولِي): the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what precedes; the clause أوحيت is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); أن is explicative, because it has come after something with the meaning of saying but not its letters; and the clause آمنوا has no grammatical position because it is explicative. (قالُوا آمَنَّا وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنا مُسْلِمُونَ): the clause is resumptive; the clause آمنا is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the bāʾ is a preposition, and أن and what is in its domain are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اشهد»; and مسلمون is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ. (إِذْ قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): the clause is resumptive, recounting a past situation; the adverb is attached to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by construct; الحواريون is the fāʿil (agent); يا is a vocative particle; عيسى is a single proper-name vocative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ابن is a badal (substitute) from «عيسى», following its form or its position, so the nūn may take ḍamma or fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the text; according to the rule set out in the Benefits below, the two options of ḍamma and fatḥa apply to the vocative noun itself, while ابن is accusative in either case.], as will come in the section on benefits; and مريم is muḍāf ilayhi. (هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنا مائِدَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; هل is an interrogative particle; يستطيع ربك is an imperfect verb and its agent; أن ينزل: the maṣdariyya أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, the object of يستطيع; مائدة is the object of ينزل; and من السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينزل, and there is no harm in their being attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of مائدة. (قالَ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to show what he said to them regarding their request. The clause اتقوا الله is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; إن is conditional; كان, its noun and its khabar; كان is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, understood from the context, i.e. "if you believe in His power, the Exalted, and in the truth of my prophethood, then avoid these obstinate questions". (قالُوا: نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنْها وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنا): the speech is resumptive, brought to show what they said as a justification [Translator's note: the text reads «تسويفا», apparently a misprint for «تسويغا» ("justification").] of their request; the clause نريد is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; أن and what is in its domain are an interpreted maṣdar, the object of نريد; منها is attached to نأكل; and تطمئن قلوبنا: the clause is conjoined to «أن نأكل منها». (وَنَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْها مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; نعلم is conjoined to نأكل and تطمئن — and that it be a proof for us before those of the Children of Israel who did not witness it, so that the believers may grow firmer in faith, doubt may vanish from the breasts of the doubters and waverers, and the disbelievers may believe. أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause قد صدقتنا is its khabar; نكون is conjoined to نعلم; the noun of نكون is latent (mustatir), implied as "we" (نحن); من الشاهدين is attached to an omitted khabar of نكون; and عليها is attached to الشاهدين.

* Benefits:
If the one addressed (munādā) is a single proper name followed by «ابن» with nothing separating them, and «ابن» is in construct with a proper name, two options are permitted in the vocative: ḍamma, as indeclinable, and fatḥa, following the vowel of «ابن». ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm said:
بأي مشيئة عمرو بن هند ... تطيع بنا الوشاة وتزدرينا
(By what will, O ʿAmr son of Hind, do you obey the slanderers against us and scorn us?)

dervis-irab:63-64.t:
* I'rab:
(لَوْلا يَنْهاهُمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبارُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمُ الْإِثْمَ وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ): resumptive speech, brought to urge and to put fear into the scholars and rabbis among them for their turning away from enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. In it there is a generalisation of the rebuke to the scholars of every nation and creed for this shameful trait. For this reason Ibn ʿAbbās said: "This is the severest verse in the Qur'an", meaning with respect to the scholars, for their negligence in forbidding evils. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an more fearsome to me than it." لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning «هلّا» ("why not"); ينهاهم الربانيون is an imperfect verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent); الأحبار is conjoined to His saying «الربانيون»; عن قولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينهاهم; الإثم is the mafʿūl bihi of «قول»; أكلهم is conjoined to قولهم; and السحت is the mafʿūl bihi of أكل. (لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ): its i'rab has preceded shortly before. One does not say صنع ("craft") of a deed unless it has become a habit and a custom. (وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ: يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ): the wāw is resumptive; قالت اليهود is a verb and its fāʿil; يد الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مغلولة the khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَلُعِنُوا بِما قالُوا): the clause is an imprecation and parenthetical; غلت is a passive past verb and أيديهم the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and لعنوا is conjoined to غلت أيديهم. (بَلْ يَداهُ مَبْسُوطَتانِ يُنْفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشاءُ): بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; يداه is a mubtadaʾ and مبسوطتان the khabar; and the clause is conjoined to the clause يد الله مغلولة. The clause ينفق may be resumptive, brought to emphasise the perfection of His generosity, glorified is He; the meaning is: His spending is according to what His will requires, for He is the One who withholds and the One who extends. I do not know how they permitted it to be a second khabar of «يداه», following Abū Ḥayyān. كيف here is conditional, in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ طُغْياناً وَكُفْراً): the wāw is the wāw of the omitted oath, and the omitted [thing sworn by] is genitive by the wāw [Translator's note: the source says «والقسم المحذوف مجرور بالواو», "and the omitted oath is genitive by the wāw", meaning the omitted noun sworn by]; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, its implied form being "I swear". The lām occurs in the answer to the oath; يزيدن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi; منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); ما is a relative noun, the fāʿil of يزيدن — what is meant is that they increase in rancour and in persistence in denial; the clause أنزل has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); إليك is attached to أنزل; من ربك is attached to an omitted ḥāl; طغيانا is a tamyīz (specification) or the second mafʿūl bihi of يزيدن; and كفرا is conjoined to «طغيانا». (وَأَلْقَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): the wāw is resumptive; ألقينا is a verb and its fāʿil; بينهم is an adverb attached to ألقينا; العداوة is a mafʿūl bihi and البغضاء is conjoined to العداوة; and إلى يوم القيامة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (كُلَّما أَوْقَدُوا ناراً لِلْحَرْبِ أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ): كلما is accusative as an adverb of time, and the clause is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نارا is a mafʿūl bihi; للحرب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوقدوا; the clause أطفأها الله has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and the whole clause is also resumptive. (وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَساداً): the wāw is resumptive; يسعون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; في الأرض is attached to يسعون; فسادا may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), it may be a ḥāl meaning "corrupting", or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "they strive for the sake of corruption". The three views are equally weighty. (وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, the clause لا يحب is the khabar, and المفسدين is a mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
This verse is full of kinds of rhetoric, which we summarise below:
1- al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical figurative usage) in the fettering of the hand and its extending, for stinginess and generosity. The relation of this majāz is causality, because the hand is the cause of spending; and the benefit of this majāz is depicting the reality in a sensory image that usually accompanies it. Some made His saying «بل يداه مبسوطتان» a metaphor (istiʿāra): the thing borrowed is the extending, that from which it is borrowed is the hand of the spender, and that for which it is borrowed is the hand of the Real (al-Ḥaqq) — so that the hearer imagines that there are two hands extended in spending, while in reality there are no hands and no extending.
The effect of the sense of sight: that is because sensory depiction makes it more firmly fixed in the mind and more effective. The sense of sight is foremost among the senses that appreciate beauty, perceive it and convey it to the soul.
