In this regard «Guyau» [Translator's note: the source writes «جوير»; presumably the French thinker Jean-Marie Guyau], the well-known modern critic, says: The sensations that most fully deserve to be described as beautiful are visual sensations. Indeed «Descartes», the French philosopher, went further than that and defined beauty by saying: It is what pleases the eye. Since generosity and stinginess are abstract and not perceived by the senses, and are accompanied by two images that are perceived by the senses — the extending of the hand for generosity and its fettering for stinginess — they were expressed by what accompanies them, for the benefit of clarification and of moving from abstractions to sensibles.
2- al-mushākala (resemblance of expression): in His saying «غلت أيديهم» ("their hands are fettered"), for He invoked against them the very thing they had falsely alleged and spread rumours about. Hence the Jews became the stingiest of Allah's creation absolutely, and the most given to amassing wealth from whatever source it came. The Arabs used to avoid this blameworthy description and refrain from it; al-Ashtar said:
بقّيت وفري وانحرفت عن العلا ... ولقيت أضيافي بوجه عبوس
(May I keep my wealth and turn away from lofty deeds, and meet my guests with a frowning face.) [Translator's note: the line is an oath-imprecation on the poet himself, i.e. may this befall me if I do not do what he swears to do.]
Most of Ahl al-Sunna held that the Hand of Allah is one of the attributes of His essence, glorified is He, like hearing, sight and the Face; so we must believe in it and affirm it of Him without asking how and without likening.
3- al-tankīt (pointed subtlety): in His saying «بل يداه مبسوطتان» ("rather, His two hands are extended"). The context required Him to say: يده مبسوطة ("His hand is extended"), for they expressed it in the singular by saying: «يد الله مغلولة»; but He departed from correspondence for a subtle point too fine for primitive understandings: the negation of corporeality from Him, glorified is He. For they meant that He gives with His hand, whereas a man does not give with both his hands; so He answered them, invalidating that He has anything of a known body, with a right hand and a left hand. When He affirmed that both are a hand, He negated corporeality, because both of them are equal in generosity and giving.
4- al-kināya (metonymy): in kindling war, for war and its flaring up.
5- al-ṭibāq (antithesis): between kindling and extinguishing.

dervis-irab:65-65.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to show their state in the Hereafter. لو is a non-jussive conditional particle; أنّ with its noun and its khabar (predicate) is in the position of a nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb — this has been discussed before. The clause آمنوا is the khabar of «أن», and the clause اتقوا is conjoined to the clause آمنوا. (لَكَفَّرْنا عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وَلَأَدْخَلْناهُمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of «لو»; كفرنا is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كفرنا; سيئاتهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause ولأدخلناهم is conjoined to the clause لكفرنا. جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to أدخلناهم; and النعيم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

dervis-irab:66-66.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive; أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل: its i'rab has preceded shortly before. ما is conjoined to التوراة and الإنجيل, and the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause); by the relative noun He meant other Books besides the two, such as the Book of Isaiah, the Book of Daniel and the Psalms of David. إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزل, and من ربهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; the clause أكلوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; من فوقهم is attached to أكلوا, and من تحت أرجلهم is conjoined to «من فوقهم». The secret of the omission of the object will come in the section on Rhetoric. (مِنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ مُقْتَصِدَةٌ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ ساءَ ما يَعْمَلُونَ): the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; منهم is attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); أمة is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and مقتصدة a naʿt (adjective). In وكثير the wāw is conjunctive; كثير is a mubtadaʾ, and beginning with it was permissible because it is qualified by the preposition and its genitive noun; the clause ساء ما يعملون is the khabar of كثير; and the clause يعملون is the ṣila of «ما».

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are two eloquent omissions, falling within the domain of majāz (figurative usage), which is the element and elixir of eloquence. They are:
1- The omission of the muḍāf in His saying: «أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل»; what is meant is the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel and their limits, and the far-reaching rulings and widespread lessons contained in them.
2- The omission of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), whose subtleties are ever renewed. The saying of the Exalted: «لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم» reaches the furthest limits of eloquence: the object of «أكلوا» is omitted with the intent of generality, or with the intent of the act itself, as in their saying: "So-and-so loosens and binds, ratifies and annuls, harms and benefits". The basis in all of this is affirming the meaning intended in your mind for the thing absolutely. In the omission under discussion there are three views:
a- That He would pour upon them the blessings of the heaven and the blessings of the earth.
b- That He would multiply fruit-bearing trees and productive crops.
c- That He would provide them with gardens of ripe fruit, from which they would pick what hangs down from the tops of the trees and gather what has fallen to the ground beneath their feet.

dervis-irab:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ): its i'rab has preceded. (بَلِّغْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): resumptive speech, brought to console the Prophet ﷺ when he felt distressed by the call. بلغ is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is "you"; ما is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause); إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزل; and من ربك is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ): the wāw is resumptive; إن is conditional; لم تفعل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; ما is negative; and the clause بلغت is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). In the identity of protasis and apodosis there is a wonderful secret, which we shall set out in the section on Rhetoric. رسالته is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause يعصمك is its khabar (predicate), and من الناس is attached to يعصمك. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكافِرِينَ): inna and its noun; the clause لا يهدي is its khabar; القوم is a mafʿūl bihi, and الظالمين is a naʿt (adjective) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in this verse is الكافرين].

* Rhetoric:
In the identity of protasis and apodosis there is a secret without equal. That is because the consequence must differ from the condition for a benefit to be obtained; when they are identical the speech becomes defective, because outwardly it comes down to: "and if you do not do, then you have not done". But here He intended them to be identical, because not conveying the message is a matter known to people and settled in minds as something enormous and hideous for which its perpetrator is condemned; and because a scholar's failure to spread knowledge is something that deserves blame — so what then of the Message? So He made the consequence the very same as the condition, so that the extent of the concern for conveying would become clear. It has also been said in this regard: i.e. if you leave out anything, you have left out everything, and what you have conveyed becomes of no account; so the meaning becomes: and if you do not fully convey what you were commanded to convey, your ruling in disobedience and non-compliance is the ruling of one who has conveyed nothing at all.

dervis-irab:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لَسْتُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ): resumptive speech, brought to negate their false conjectures that they follow the Torah. قل is an imperative verb; يا أهل الكتاب is a vocative in genitive construct (munādā muḍāf); لستم is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and على شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate). More about ليس will come in the section on Benefits. (حَتَّى تُقِيمُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; تقيموا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «لستم»; التوراة is the object of تقيموا, and a muḍāf must be supplied, i.e. "their rulings and the lofty ideals they contain". (وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ طُغْياناً وَكُفْراً): the wāw is resumptive and the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; يزيدن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا»; ما is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of يزيدن; من ربك is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); طغيانا is a second mafʿūl bihi or a tamyīz (specification); and كفرا is conjoined to طغيانا. (فَلا تَأْسَ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكافِرِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. "if you know this, then do not grieve"; لا is prohibitive; تأس is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; على القوم is attached to تأس; and الكافرين is a naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
The tanwīn in «شيء» conveys paucity and disparagement, i.e. "you stand on nothing worth counting until you uphold the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel".

* Benefits:
(لَسْتُمْ): the middle radical of «ليس», the yāʾ, was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, i.e. the yāʾ and the sīn. Its original form is لَيِسَ with kasra on the yāʾ; then the yāʾ was made vowelless for lightness, and the fāʾ was not changed as analogy would require [Translator's note: so in the source, «ولم تقلب الفاء»; what is meant is that the yāʾ was not changed into an alif], because lightening by making vowelless is easier in an inflexible (jāmid) word than changing the letter. When it was joined to a vowelled nominative pronoun, the final radical [Translator's note: the source says «العين», the middle radical; the letter made vowelless is the sīn, the final radical] was made vowelless, so two vowelless letters met, the yāʾ and the sīn, and the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of the two vowelless letters.

dervis-irab:69-69.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصَّابِئُونَ): from صبأ, i.e. he left his religion. They were a people who worshipped the stars, whose seat was in Ḥarrān in Mesopotamia; from them came scholars, philosophers and astrologers, among them the secretary and poet Abū Isḥāq al-Ṣābiʾ.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هادُوا): resumptive speech, brought to set out those who believe in Allah and do righteous deeds. inna and its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); and الذين هادوا is conjoined to الذين آمنوا. (وَالصَّابِئُونَ وَالنَّصارى مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً): the wāw is resumptive; الصابئون is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) is omitted, and it is intended to come after what is in the scope of «إنّ», its noun and its khabar, as though it were said: "Those who believe, those who are Jews and the Christians — their ruling is such-and-such, and the Sabians likewise." This is what Sībawayh preferred regarding the departure from the expected case, and he cited as evidence for it:
وإلّا فاعلموا أنّا وأنتم ... بغاة ما بقينا على شقاق
(Otherwise, know that we — and you — are transgressors as long as we remain in discord.)
i.e. "know that we are transgressors, and you likewise". The conjunction is then of the type of conjoining clauses: الصابئون with its omitted khabar is a clause conjoined to the clause of His saying إن الذين آمنوا, and it has no grammatical position, just as the clause to which it is conjoined has none. «الصابئون» was put forward only to draw attention to the fact that these are deeper in error and further gone in straying, because they were stripped of every creed. Other views on this departure in case will come in the section on Benefits. النصارى is conjoined to الذين, and من is a relative noun, a badal (substitute) for الذين. You may also parse النصارى as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «فلا خوف عليهم», with the clause the khabar of «إن» [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense of this alternative is unclear as printed]. The clause آمن بالله is the ṣila; اليوم الآخر is conjoined to الله; عمل is conjoined to آمن; and صالحا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a righteous deed". (فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): the clause is the khabar of إنّ, and the fāʾ entered because of the hint of condition in the relative noun; خوف is a mubtadaʾ, and beginning with it was permissible because the negation precedes it; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar; and ولا هم يحزنون is conjoined to what precedes.

* Benefits:
We have given the preferred view, held by al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and the grammarians of Basra, on the i'rab of «والصابئون». There are other views, which we set out briefly below:
a- The wāw is conjunctive, and الصابئون is conjoined to the position of the noun of إنّ, because before «إنّ» entered it was in the position of a nominative. This is the school of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ.
b- It is nominative, conjoined to the nominative pronoun in «هادوا»; this is reported from al-Kisāʾī.
c- That «إنّ» means نعم ("yes"), i.e. a particle of reply, and what follows it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, so «والصابئون» is conjoined to what precedes it.

What Ibn Hishām says:
Ibn Hishām's account of the verse comes down to two things:
a- The khabar of «إنّ» is omitted, i.e. "rewarded" or "safe" or "joyful", and الصابئون is a mubtadaʾ with what follows it as its khabar. Evidence for it is the saying:
خليليّ هل طبّ فإني وأنتما ... وإن لم تبوحا بالهوى نفان
(My two friends, is there any cure? For I and you two, even if you do not disclose your love, are [wasted with love].) [Translator's note: the last word is printed «نفان» in the source; the verse is usually cited with «دنفان», "two wasted with love".]
It is weakened by the fact that the omission is from the first because the second indicates it, whereas what is common is the reverse.
b- The khabar mentioned is that of «إنّ», and the khabar of «الصابئون» is omitted. Evidence for it is the saying:
فمن يك أمسى بالمدينة رحله ... فإني وقيار بها لغريب
(Whoever has his lodging in Madīna by evening — I, and Qayyār, am a stranger there.)
since the lām does not enter the khabar of a mubtadaʾ unless it is fronted, as in: القائم لزيد [Translator's note: so in the source]. It is weakened by putting the conjoined clause before part of the clause to which it is conjoined.

dervis-irab:114-115.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عِيداً): al-ʿīd (festival) is well known. It is derived from al-ʿawd (returning), because it returns [Translator's note: the text has «يعول», evidently a misprint for «يعود».] every year. Its first radical has kasra only because the wāw came after a kasra; the original form is:
عويد, just as ميزان was originally موزان, and the wāw was changed to yāʾ because it came after a kasra.

* I'rab:
(قالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ): resumptive speech brought for his beginning the supplication after their sincerity had become clear to him. قال عيسى is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ابن is a badal (substitute) or naʿt (adjective); and مريم is muḍāf ilayhi. (اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنا أَنْزِلْ عَلَيْنا مائِدَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ): اللهم was originally يا الله; the vocative particle was dropped and the doubled mīm was substituted for it — this has been discussed before. ربنا is a second vocative; أنزل is an imperative verb for supplication, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "You" (أنت); علينا is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل; مائدة is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and من السماء is attached to an omitted adjective of مائدة, or is also attached to أنزل.
(تَكُونُ لَنا عِيداً لِأَوَّلِنا وَآخِرِنا وَآيَةً مِنْكَ): the clause تكون is a second adjective of مائدة, i.e. the day of its descent will be a festival; the noun of تكون is latent, implied as "it" (هي); عيدا is the khabar (predicate) of تكون; لنا is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective placed before the thing it describes, namely His word «عيدا»; لأولنا: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted badal from «لنا», with repetition of the governing element; آخرنا is conjoined to «أولنا»; آية is conjoined to «عيدا»; and منك is attached to an omitted adjective of آية. (وَارْزُقْنا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; ارزقنا is an imperative verb for supplication, its agent latent, and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as direct object; the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير الرازقين the khabar; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive, or is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (قالَ اللَّهُ: إِنِّي مُنَزِّلُها عَلَيْكُمْ): resumptive speech brought to show Allah's answering of his supplication. إني and what is in its domain are in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إن and its noun; منزلها is the khabar; and عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to منزلها, because it is an active participle. (فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنْكُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; يكفر is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بعد is an adverb cut off from construct in wording but not in meaning, so it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and it is attached to يكفر; and منكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَإِنِّي أُعَذِّبُهُ عَذاباً لا أُعَذِّبُهُ أَحَداً مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; إن and its noun; the clause أعذبه is its khabar; the clause إني أعذبه is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) in the sense of التعذيب; لا is negating; أعذبه is an imperfect verb, and the pronoun in the second «أعذبه» stands in for the absolute object because it refers back to it — the implied sense being "I will punish him with a punishment such that I will not punish anyone with the like of that punishment"; أحدا is the direct object; the negated clause is an adjective of «عذابا»; and من العالمين is attached to an omitted adjective of «أحدا».
The clause of the protasis and its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «من».

* Benefits:
Thirteen things stand in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) and are given its ruling. They are:
1- The noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar): أعطيتك عطاء ("I gave you a gift").
2- Its adjective: «اذكروا الله كثيرا».
3- Its pronoun referring back to it: as in the preceding verse.
4- Its synonym: فرح جذلا ("he rejoiced with glee").
5- A maṣdar that meets it in derivation: «أنبتكم نباتا».
6- What indicates its kind: رجع القهقرى ("he went back walking backwards"), and the words of al-Aʿshā:
غراء فرعاء مصقول عوارضها ... تمشي الهويني كما يمشي الوجي الوحل
(Fair-faced, long-haired, her teeth polished, she walks slowly, as one with sore hooves walks in mud.)
7- What indicates its instrument: ضربت اللص سوطا ("I struck the thief with a whip").
8- Interrogative أيّ, and interrogative or predicative كم, as in: «وسيعلم الذين ظلموا أيّ منقلب ينقلبون», and the words of al-Mutanabbī: كم قد قتلت وكم قد متّ عندكم ... ثم انتفضت فزال القبر والكفن (How often have I been slain, and how often have I died among you; then I shook myself, and the grave and the shroud were gone!)
9- What indicates its number: «فاجلدوا كلّ واحد منهما مئة جلدة».
10- The conditionals ما, مهما and أي: ما تفعل أفعل ("whatever you do, I do"), مهما تقف أقف ("however you stand, I stand"), and أي عمل تعمله تجاز عليه ("whatever deed you do, you will be requited for it").
11- The words كل and بعض in construct with the maṣdar: «فلا تميلوا كل الميل», and اجتهد بعض الاجتهاد ("he strove somewhat").
12- The demonstrative, pointing to the maṣdar: اجتهدت ذلك الاجتهاد ("I strove with that striving").
13- The أيّ of perfection (al-kamāliyya): that which indicates the meaning of perfection when it occurs in construct with the maṣdar, as in اجتهدت أي اجتهاد ("I strove with what a striving!"). When it occurs after an indefinite noun it is an adjective of it, as in the words of Abū al-ʿAtāhiya:
إنّ الشّباب والفراغ والجده ... مفسدة للمرء أيّ مفسده
(Youth, leisure and wealth are a corruption for a man — what a corruption!)
So «أي» is an adjective of «مفسدة». And when it occurs after a definite noun it is a ḥāl, as in: مررت بعبد الله أيّ رجل ("I passed by ʿAbdallāh — what a man!").

dervis-irab:32-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَجْلِ): «الأجل», with sukūn on the jīm, is a maṣdar (verbal noun). One says «أجل عليهم شرا», i.e. he committed evil against them and stirred it up; then it came to be used for crimes, as in their saying «من جراك فعلته» (I did it on your account), i.e. "from the fact that I committed it [for you]," i.e. I perpetrated it; then its use was broadened, and it came to be used for every [expression of] cause.

* I'rab:
(مِنْ أَجْلِ ذلِكَ كَتَبْنا عَلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): the clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (كتبنا), and (على بني إسرائيل), a preposition and its genitive noun, is also attached to (كتبنا); i.e. We legislated retaliation (qiṣāṣ) upon the killer, so that the legitimacy of retaliation would be a fixed ruling in all nations. He singled out the Children of Israel only — as we mentioned just now — because killing was the habit and custom of the Children of Israel, to the point that they ventured to kill prophets and messengers; because the purpose is to console the Prophet ﷺ and comfort him on account of their attempts to assassinate him and his Companions.
(أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ): (أن) and what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (كتبنا). The hāʾ is the noun of (أنّ), and it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (قتل) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (نفسا) is the direct object; (بغير نفس), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (قتل), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «قتل», i.e. "he killed it wrongfully"; (أو) is a conjunction; (فساد) is conjoined to (نفس), which is genitive by the annexation of (غير) to it; and (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (فساد).
(فَكَأَنَّما قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (كأنما) is [kaʾanna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (قتل الناس) is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and the direct object; (جميعا) is a ḥāl; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar (predicate) of «من»; and the conditional clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of «أنه».
(وَمَنْ أَحْياها فَكَأَنَّما أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً): the parsing of its like has been given.
(وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); the clause (قد جاءتهم):
has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; (رسلنا) is the fāʿil (agent); and (بالبينات) is attached to (جاءتهم).
(ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (إن) with its noun; (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of «كثيرا»; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of genitive by annexation; (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to «مسرفون»; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (مسرفون) is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
Representative simile (tashbīh tamthīlī): the basis of the simile is that the two acts of killing share in violating the sanctity of blood, in audacity against Allah, and in encouraging people to kill. The point of the simile is to make the matter of killing appear dreadful and to magnify the matter of saving life, by depicting each of them in an image befitting it.

dervis-irab:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّما جَزاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): resumptive speech introduced to set out the ruling of Allah concerning every highway robber, whether unbeliever or Muslim, because waging war on the Muslims is in the ruling of waging war on Allah and His Messenger. It was originally revealed concerning the ʿUranīs.
(إنما) is [inna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (جزاء) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذين) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (يحاربون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (الله) is its object; and (رسوله) is conjoined to (الله).
(وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَساداً): (يسعون) is conjoined to (يحاربون); (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يسعون). (فسادا) may properly be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they wage war and strive for the sake of corruption, the conditions for the accusative being met. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "and they strive in the land as corrupters," or "possessed of corruption"; they were made corruption itself, by way of hyperbole.
It may also be accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. it is a kind of the governing verb before it, because «يسعون في الأرض» really means «يفسدون» (they corrupt); so (فسادا) is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) standing in place of «الإفساد», the implied form being: "they corrupt in the land by their striving, a corrupting."
(أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ مِنْ خِلافٍ أَوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): the interpreted maṣdar from (أن) and what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of (جزاء). (أو) is a conjunction; (يصلبوا) is conjoined to (يقتلوا); (أو) is a conjunction; (تقطع) is also conjoined to (يقتلوا). (أيديهم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (تقطع); (أرجلهم) is conjoined to (أيديهم); and (من خلاف) is attached to an omitted ḥāl from (أيديهم) and (أرجلهم), i.e. "cut off alternately," meaning that his right hand and his left foot are cut off.
(ينفوا) is also conjoined, and (من الأرض) is attached to (ينفوا).
(ذلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيا): the clause is resumptive, setting out the purpose of these punishments. The demonstrative is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (لهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (خزي) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; (في الدنيا) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (خزي); and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. «خزي» may also be parsed as the khabar of «ذلك», with (لهم) attached to an omitted [element] in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from (خزي), because it was originally its adjective, and when it was placed before it, it became a ḥāl.
(وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (في الآخرة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (عذاب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and (عظيم) is an adjective.
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ): the clause of exception is accusative as a ḥāl from those being punished «[Translator's note: so in the text; the usual parsing is that (الذين) is accusative as the excepted (mustathnā)]»; (إلا) is a particle of exception; (الذين) is the excepted; the clause (تابوا) is the ṣila; (من قبل) is attached to (تابوا), «قبل» being made genitive with kasra because of annexation; (أن تقدروا) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of genitive by annexation; and (عليهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (تقدروا).
(فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (اعلموا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); and (أن) with its noun and its two predicates stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا».

* Benefits:
«أو» is a conjunction with meanings which the author of al-Mughnī brought to twelve; we content ourselves with the following principal meanings: 1- Doubt: to make the hearer doubt about a matter the speaker intends, so he leaves it vague to him while he himself knows it. From it is the saying of the Exalted: «وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون» (And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more).
2- Choice (takhyīr): as in "take a garment or ten dirhams." Allah the Exalted said:
«فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة» (its expiation is feeding ten poor persons from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave). He made one of these three obligatory, and the reins of choice are in the hand of the one charged; whichever of them he does, he has expiated and discharged the obligation, and he is not required to combine them.
3- Permission (ibāḥa): "sit with so-and-so or so-and-so"; and the saying of the Exalted: «ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا» (and do not obey from among them a sinner or an ingrate).
4- Division and diversification, as in the verse, i.e. dividing their punishment in a division distributed according to their situations and crimes. Al-Shāfiʿī said: «أو» throughout the Quran is for choice, except in this verse.
2- «[Translator's note: so numbered in the text; this is a second benefit after the four meanings of «أو».]» The interpreters differed on the meaning of the banishment (nafy) which Allah the Exalted mentioned in this place. Some of them said: the meaning of banishment is banishing him from one town to another, and confining him in prison in the town to which he is banished. The original meaning of «النفي» in the speech of the Arabs is driving away. Aws ibn Ḥajar said:
تنفون عن طرق الكرام كما ... تنفي المطارق ما يلي القرد
(You are driven away from the paths of the noble, as the beating-rods drive off what adjoins the matted wool.)
«القرد», with two fatḥas: the hair and wool that has fallen off, become matted and whose ends have knotted; it is the refuse of wool. From this, base dirhams and the like are called «النفاية» (refuse).

dervis-irab:35-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْوَسِيلَةَ): everything by which one seeks access (yutawassalu), i.e. draws near, whether kinship, a favour done, or other than that; it was then borrowed for that by which one seeks access to Allah the Exalted, namely doing acts of obedience and abandoning acts of disobedience. Labīd ibn Rabīʿa said:
أرى الناس لا يدرون ما قدر أمرهم ... ألا كل ذي لبّ إلى الله وأسل
(I see people not knowing the measure of their affair; indeed, everyone of understanding is seeking to draw near to Allah.)
In al-Miṣbāḥ: «وسلت إلى الله أسل», of the pattern of «وعد»: I desired and drew near; from it «الوسيلة» is derived, which is that by which one draws near to a thing; the plural is «الوسائل». «الوسيل» is said to be a plural of «وسيلة», and also said to be a dialectal form of it. From it is the saying of ʿAntara to a woman who reproached him over a horse which he preferred to the rest of his horses and to which he gave the milk of his camels to drink:
لا تذكري مهري وما أطعمته ... فيكون جلدك مثل جلد الأجرب
إنّ الغبوق له وأنت مسوءة ... إن كنت سائلتي غبوقا فاذهبي
إن الرجال لهم إليك وسيلة ... إن يأخذوك تكحلي وتخضبي
ويكون مركبك العقود وحدجه ... وابن النعامة يوم ذلك مركبي
(Do not mention my colt and what I fed him, lest your skin become like the skin of a mangy [camel]. The evening milk is his, though you be displeased; if you are asking me for evening milk, then go. The men have a way of access to you: if they seize you, you will be adorned with kohl and henna; your mount will then be the young camel and its litter, while Ibn al-Naʿāma [my horse] on that day is my mount.)

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the parsing of its likes has been given many times.
(اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَابْتَغُوا إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ): resumptive speech introduced to set out God-fearing and seeking the means of access to Allah, after He had shown the enormity of killing and corruption in the land and pointed to those who are forgiven after their repentance. (اتقوا الله) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ابتغوا) is conjoined to (اتقوا); (إليه) is attached to (ابتغوا) or to (الوسيلة), because it is of the pattern «فعيلة» in the sense of a passive participle, i.e. "that by which access is sought," and is not a maṣdar (verbal noun), such that it would be impossible «[Translator's note: the printed text has «يستنع», a misprint for «يمتنع»]» for what it governs to precede it; and (الوسيلة) is the direct object.
(وَجاهِدُوا فِي سَبِيلِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ): conjoined to what precedes; (لعل) with its noun; the clause (تفلحون) is its khabar (predicate); and the clause of hope is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً): resumptive speech introduced to emphasise the obligation of complying with the preceding commands and to encourage the believers to hasten to take the means of access to Him. (إن) with its noun; (لو) is conditional; (أن) is a particle resembling the verb; (لهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to the omitted fronted khabar of «أن»; (ما) is a relative noun, its delayed noun; (أن) and what falls within its scope is a maṣdar in the nominative as the agent of an omitted verb whose implied form is:
«ثبت» (it were established) «[Translator's note: the printed text has «نبت», a misprint for «ثبت»]», or in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); this has been discussed in detail before. (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted [element] which has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the condition and its answer form the khabar of «إن»; and (جميعا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لِيَفْتَدُوا بِهِ مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): you may make the wāw a conjunction, with (مثله) conjoined to the noun of (أن), namely the relative «ما». You may also make the wāw denote accompaniment (maʿiyya), with (مثله) a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), governed in the accusative by the verb omitted before the agent, or by a similar verb if you parse (أن) and what follows it as a nominal clause. (معه) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl. The lām is the causal lām; (يفتدوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the [notion of] being-established to which the khabar, namely «لهم», is attached; (به) is attached to (يفتدوا); and (من عذاب يوم القيامة) is also attached to (يفتدوا), since their meanings differ. The pronoun is singular although what it refers back to is two things, because the pronoun is in the sense of a demonstrative, i.e. «بذلك» (with that); or in the sense of «مع», so that what is referred to becomes single; or it is of the type of the saying of ʿUmayr ibn Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī:
فمن يك أمنى بالمدينة رحله ... فإني وقيّار بها لغريب
(Whoever has his abode in Medina — I and Qayyār are strangers there.) «[Translator's note: the printed text has «أمنى»; the well-known wording is «أمسى».]»
The explanation of this verse will come in the section on benefits.
(ما تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): (ما تقبل منهم): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; the answer came, as is most common, without a lām because it is negated. The wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; (لهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (عذاب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and (أليم) is an adjective.
(يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنَ النَّارِ وَما هُمْ بِخارِجِينَ مِنْها): the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); (يريدون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (أن) and what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, the direct object of (يريدون); (من النار) is attached to (يخرجون) «[Translator's note: so in the text; the verb in the verse is (يخرجوا)]»; the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative, operating like «ليس»; (هم) is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (خارجين) is genitive in form by the bāʾ and accusative in position because it is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī «ما»; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (عذاب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and (مقيم): an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ليفتدوا به» there is a representative metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) for the punishment's clinging to them and its permanence upon them, and that they have no way of escaping it. In the noble ḥadīth: «It will be said to the unbeliever on the Day of Resurrection: Do you think that if you had the earth's fill of gold you would ransom yourself with it? He will say: Yes. It will be said to him: You were asked for what was easier than that.»

* Benefits:
The saying of ʿUmayr ibn Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī in the verse, «وقيار»: Qayyār is the name of his horse; it is also said his camel, and also said his servant. It is a mubtadaʾ, or conjoined to the position of (إن) with its noun. If it is parsed as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar is omitted for brevity, because what is mentioned indicates it by the conjunction; this involves conjoining before the completion of what is conjoined to, which is based on hearing (samāʿī) and may not be taken as a basis for analogy. It is not permissible to make «غريب» a khabar for both, lest two governing words converge on a single governed word; and it is not permissible to make it a khabar of «قيار», because the lām of initiation (lām al-ibtidāʾ) does not enter upon the khabar. We have brought it as evidence that [the predicate] is omitted from the second because what is in the first indicates it.

dervis-irab:116-120.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ: يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is coordinated with «إذ قال الحواريون»; so the adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [verb], its implied form being:
"remember" (اذكر). The clause قال الله is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa), and the clause يا عيسى بن مريم is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (أَأَنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّي إِلهَيْنِ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ)
The hamza is interrogative; أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause قلت للناس is the khabar (predicate); and the interrogative clause is the object of the saying. The clause اتخذوني, consisting of the imperative verb, the fāʿil (agent) and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. وأمي: the wāw is of accompaniment or conjunction, and أمي is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the yāʾ; إلهين is a second direct object of اتخذوني; and من دون الله is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of إلهين, i.e.
"being besides Him, the Exalted". There is nothing to prevent attaching them to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of اتخذوني, i.e. "passing over [Allah]". (قالَ: سُبْحانَكَ ما يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ): the clause is resumptive, brought to disavow what was attributed to him.
قال is a past verb; سبحانك is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause is the object of the saying; ما is negating; يكون is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; لي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of يكون; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the delayed noun of يكون; the clause ما يكون لي is resumptive; the clause ليس has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the noun of ليس is latent (mustatir), implied as "it" (هو); بحق: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and حق is the khabar of ليس; لي is attached to an omitted ḥāl because it precedes what it describes; and ما is a relative noun, the object of أقول, because it contains the meaning of a clause. There are other parsings which we have passed over. (إِنْ كُنْتُ قُلْتُهُ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ): the clause is resumptive; إن is conditional; كنت is a defective past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and the defective verb is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause «قلته» is the khabar of كنت; the fāʾ is linking; the clause قد علمته is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the jussive condition; and علمته is a verb, its agent and its direct object. (تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ): the clause is resumptive; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as direct object; في نفسي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila; and the clause ولا أعلم ما في نفسك is conjoined to what precedes. (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ): إن and its noun; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and علام الغيوب the khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «إن»; or «أنت» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Translator's note: the text reads «ضمير فعل», a misprint for «ضمير فصل».] and علام is the khabar of «إن»; the nominal clause is the khabar of إن [Translator's note: so in the text, repeating the first analysis.]; and the clause إنك and what follows it has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya). (ما قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلَّا ما أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ): ما is negating; قلت is a verb and its agent; لهم is attached to قلت; إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is a relative noun, the object of قلت; and the clause أمرتني به is the ṣila. (أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ): the interpreted maṣdar is a badal (substitute) from «ما», or from the hāʾ in «به», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «هو». Some made it explicative, and affirmed that ʿĪsā, upon him be peace, conveyed the meaning of Allah's speech in this wording, as if he said: "I said nothing to them other than Your saying to me: Say to them, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." ربي is a badal from الله or an adjective. More on the i'rab of these words will come in the section on benefits. (وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيداً ما دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; كان and its noun; شهيدا is its khabar; عليهم is attached to «شهيدا»; ما دمت: [دام is] a defective past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and فيهم is attached to its omitted khabar; and the adverb formed from ما دمت is attached to «شهيدا», i.e. "for the duration of my remaining settled among them". (فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنْتَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; لما is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking, so it is either an adverb or a particle containing the sense of a condition; the clause توفيتني is in the position of the genitive by construct, or has no grammatical position; توفيتني is a verb, its agent and its direct object, i.e.
"You took me fully, by raising [me] to heaven", which is the original sense of wafāh. The clause كنت has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; كان and its noun; أنت is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in كنت, and you may parse it as a detached pronoun with no grammatical position; الرقيب is the khabar of كنت; عليهم is attached to الرقيب; the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and شهيد the khabar; and على كل شيء is attached to شهيد. (إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبادُكَ وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): إن is conditional; تعذبهم is the protasis; the hāʾ is the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; the clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; إن, its noun and its khabar; and the conditional sentence is resumptive, brought by way of seeking compassion — which is why he did not say "If You punish them, they have disobeyed You". (قالَ اللَّهُ هذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ): resumptive speech brought to conclude what the discourse began with when He said: يوم يجمع الله الرسل. The demonstrative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and يوم the khabar; the clause ينفع is in the position of the genitive by construct; الصادقين is a fronted direct object; and صدقهم is a delayed agent. (لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً): the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the benefit mentioned; لهم is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; جنات is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause تجري is an adjective of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري; الأنهار is the agent; خالدين is a ḥāl; and أبدا is an adverb of time attached to خالدين. (رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the clause is a supplication, parenthetical with no grammatical position; the clause ورضوا عنه is conjoined to it; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, الفوز the khabar, and العظيم an adjective. (لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما فِيهِنَّ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the clause is resumptive, brought to establish the truth; لله is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ملك السماوات والأرض is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the wāw is conjunctive; ما is a relative noun conjoined to الملك; فيهن is attached to an omitted ṣila; «ما» was used giving preponderance to non-rational beings, because it indicates greatness more strongly; هو is a mubtadaʾ and قدير its khabar; and على كل شيء is attached to قدير.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم» there is one of the arts of rhetoric, matchless and difficult to grasp; one who contemplates it needs a great deal of fineness of perception and refinement of disposition. It is called the art of takhyīr (selection). The scholars of rhetoric defined it as the poet or prose-writer bringing a passage of speech or a verse of poetry which could acceptably be rhymed with various rhymes, and choosing from them one rhyme that is preferred over the rest; his preferring it is taken as evidence of his good choice and true perception. First intuition may dictate that it should be other than what he chose, but he refrained from that for a subtle secret, as in the words of one of them:
إنّ الغريب الطويل الذيل ممتهن ... فكيف حال غريب ما له قوت
(The stranger, though long of train [i.e. well-off], is humiliated; so what of a stranger who has no sustenance?)
It would have been acceptable for him to say: "who has no wealth", or "who has no master", or "who has no one".
But if you look at what he said, namely «ما له قوت» ("who has no sustenance"), you find it more eloquent than all of them, more indicative of poverty and want, more closely touching on the mention of need, more moving to the heart, and more apt to elicit compassion. For that [Translator's note: the text reads «فذلك», apparently for «فلذلك» ("for that reason").] it was preferred over the others.

Discussion of the verse:
Returning, after this brief introduction to this art, to the verse we are dealing with, we say: first, primitive intuition would dictate that the closing phrase (fāṣila) be:
«إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم», because of its suitability to His words «إن تغفر» and the correspondence between forgiveness (ghufrān) and the All-Forgiving (al-Ghafūr). But the effect of this illusion arising from that intuition quickly vanishes when the one under the illusion remembers that these people have deserved punishment rather than forgiveness, so the closing phrase must be «العزيز الحكيم»; for if «الغفور الرحيم» had come after the mention of forgiveness — while He does not forgive them — [Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source.] so the closing phrase had to be as it came, because Allah, glory be to Him, is unassailable by any compulsion or opposition, and al-ʿAzīz is the unassailable one; and after describing Himself with might, He must describe Himself with wisdom, because He is the All-Wise who puts everything in its place.

Al-Aṣmaʿī's anecdote:
Al-Aṣmaʿī's anecdote has come up before: he mentioned that one day he was reciting, and recited: «والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله غفور رحيم», and a Bedouin was listening to him; he objected and declared him mistaken. Al-Aṣmaʿī checked the verse again, and it was «والله عزيز حكيم». He said to the Bedouin: "How did you know that?" He said: "O you, He was mighty, so He judged, so He cut off; had He forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut off." Al-Aṣmaʿī was astonished and silenced.

This secret was hidden from Abū Ḥayyān:
The secret of this art was hidden from Abū Ḥayyān, despite his eminence. He said in «al-Baḥr», attempting to account for the objection, the following verbatim: "Abū Bakr Ibn al-Anbārī said: Someone attacked the Qur'an by saying that His words «فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم» do not suit His words «وإن تغفر لهم», because what suits it is «فإنك أنت الغفور الرحيم». The answer is that it admits of nothing but what Allah the Exalted revealed, and whenever it is transferred to what this attacker said, its meaning becomes weak, for then «الغفور الرحيم» would be confined to the second condition and would have no connection with the first condition.
It is what Allah the Exalted revealed, and what the Muslims have agreed upon in reciting." We say: had Abū Ḥayyān known this art, he would have answered with what we have presented, and would not have resorted to far-fetched answers.

* Benefits:
Between Ibn Hishām and al-Zamakhsharī:
Ibn Hishām mentioned in «Mughnī al-Labīb» the following: "Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned regarding His words, the Exalted, «ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله» that it may be an explicative [أن] explaining the saying, on its interpretation as a command, i.e. 'I commanded them only what You commanded me: that they worship Allah' — and this is good. On this basis it is said in the criterion: that the letters of saying be in it, unless the saying is interpreted as something else [Translator's note: the wording of the criterion is compressed in the source.]. In the verse it may not be explicative of أمرتني, because it is not correct to say 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord' as said by Allah the Exalted; so it cannot be explicative of His command, because what is explained is identical with its explanation."

Ibn Yaʿīsh's wording:
Ibn Yaʿīsh's wording: "So «أن» is in the sense of «أي» ('that is'), and it is an explanation of «ما أمرتني به», because the command has the meaning of saying; and because, when this is explicative, [it has] three conditions [Translator's note: a word such as «لها» appears to be missing in the source.]:
1- The first is that the verb which it explains and expresses contain the meaning of saying without being [the verb of] saying.
2- The second is that nothing of the complement of the verb which it explains be attached to «أن», because if anything of that is attached to it, it becomes part of its clause and is not an explanation of it — as in أوعزت إليه بأن قم ('I instructed him to stand') and كتبت إليه بأن قم ('I wrote to him to stand'), because the bāʾ here is attached to the verb, and when it is attached to it, it becomes part of its clause, while explanation is only by a clause other than the first.
3- The third is that what precedes it be a complete utterance, because of what we mentioned, namely that it and what follows it are a clause explaining a clause before it. For that reason they said regarding His words, the Exalted:
«أن الحمد لله رب العالمين» that «أن» in it is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], the meaning being:
'that praise be to Allah' (أنه الحمد لله); it is not explicative, because what precedes it is not a complete clause — do you not see that if you stopped at His words «وآخر دعواهم» it would not be a complete utterance?"
I say: for this reason we inclined to what we chose in parsing it as maṣdariyya, to avoid falling into these pitfalls.
2- When «ما» occurs before «ليس», «لم» or «لا», or after «إلّا», it is a relative noun; when it occurs after the kāf of comparison it is maṣdariyya; when it occurs after the bāʾ it admits both; and when it occurs between two verbs, the first being [a verb of] knowing, awareness or looking, it admits being relative or interrogative. [Translator's note: the preceding discussion is unnumbered in the source, which then continues with "2-".]
3- Every noun of time that is vague and refers to the past may be put in construct with a clause; if what follows it is indeclinable, then indeclinability on the fatḥa is preferable, for harmony. Al-Nābigha said: على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا ... وقلت: ألمّا أصح والشيب وازع (At the time I reproached grey hair for [my] youthful passion, and said: "Have I not yet sobered up, while grey hair restrains?")
«على حين» is related in the genitive as declinable, and «على حين» indeclinable on the fatḥa, which is preferable. If what follows it is a declinable verb or a nominal clause, then declinability is preferable, as came in the verse: «هذا يوم ينفع».

dervis-irab:38-39.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَكالًا): In al-Miṣbāḥ it says: «نكل به ينكل», of the pattern of «قتل», «نكلة قبيحة»: he afflicted him with a calamity [as an exemplary punishment]. «نكّل به», with doubling, is intensive; and the noun is «النكال».

* I'rab:
(وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما): resumptive speech introduced to begin setting out the ruling on theft. (السارق) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being:
"among what is recited to you," or "among what has been prescribed for you, [is] the male thief and the female thief," i.e.:
the ruling concerning them. So the muḍāf, namely «حكم» (ruling), was omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi, namely «السارق والسارقة», was put in its place; and the khabar, which is the preposition and its genitive noun, was omitted, because the fāʾ after it prevents its being accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), as is the rule, since the accusative is preferred before a request «[Translator's note: the sentence is reproduced as printed]»; and it — i.e. the fāʾ, which came because of its resemblance to a condition — prevents what follows it from being the khabar, because it never enters upon it; so nothing remains but the nominative. This is a chapter which Sībawayh devoted in his Book, and the reader will see its summary in the section on benefits. This is the reading of the majority. Al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad and a group held that the khabar is the imperative clause, namely His saying «فاقطعوا», and that the fāʾ entered the khabar only because it resembles a condition, since the alif and lām in it are relative, in the sense of «الذي» and «التي», and the adjective is its ṣila (relative clause); so it has the force of your saying: "and he who steals and she who steals, cut off…". Al-Zamakhsharī permitted that, though he preferred what Sībawayh held. (السارقة) is conjoined to (السارق); the fāʾ occurs in the answer to the relative «ال»; (اقطعوا) is an imperative verb, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); and (أيديهما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(جَزاءً بِما كَسَبا نَكالًا مِنَ اللَّهِ): (جزاء) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of recompense," the conditions for the accusative being met. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "recompense them a recompense." It may also be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, i.e. "recompensing them with cutting off." In (بما), the bāʾ is a preposition whose meaning is causality, i.e.:
because of their earning; (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar genitive by the bāʾ; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جزاء). (ما) may also be relative, i.e. "because of what they earned through theft, which is done by the hands," the clause being the ṣila. (نكالا) is accusative in the same way as (جزاء), or it is a badal (substitute) from it; and (من الله) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «نكالا».
(وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (عزيز) is a first khabar and (حكيم) a second. A delightful story of one of the Bedouins will come, which the reader will see in the section on benefits.
(فَمَنْ تابَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ظُلْمِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; (تاب) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; (إن) with its noun, and the clause (يتوب) its khabar; and the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar of (من).
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive; (إن) with its noun and its two predicates.

* Benefits:
1- We present below a summary of the delightful section that Sībawayh included in his Book, for its novelty, its benefit and the agility of mind it shows. He said in the chapter entitled:
«The Chapter of Command and Prohibition», after mentioning the places where the accusative is chosen — the summary of which is that whenever the noun is built upon an imperative verb, that is a place where the accusative is chosen. Then he said, as though clarifying how this verse is distinguished from those where he chose the accusative:
"As for the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: «والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا» (the verse), and His saying:
«الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا» (the verse), this is not built upon the verb; rather it comes on the pattern of the saying of the Exalted: «مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون» (the description of the Garden promised to the God-fearing).
Then He said after it: «فيها أنهار» (in it are rivers)." Thus Sībawayh means to distinguish these verses from the places in which he set out the choice of the accusative. The point of the distinction is that in speech where the accusative is chosen, the noun is built upon the verb, whereas in these verses it is not built upon it, so the choice of the accusative is not required. Then he said: "The description (al-mathal) was placed only for the account that follows it; He mentioned reports and stories, so it is as though He said:
'and among the stories is the description of the Garden'; so this is taken as an implied [element], and Allah knows best.
Likewise «الزانية والزاني», as He, majestic is His praise, said: «سورة أنزلناها وفرضناها» (a sūra which We have sent down and made obligatory); [it is as though] He said: among the obligations [are] the female and male fornicator; then came:
«فاجلدوا», after the nominative had already been applied to them." Sībawayh means: the noun was not built upon the verb mentioned afterwards, but upon an omitted preceding [element], and the verb came incidentally. He resumed his words and said: "Just as there came: «وقائلة خولان فانكح فتاتهم» (and many a woman saying: 'Khawlān — so marry their girl'): he brought the verb after the implied [element] had governed it. Likewise His saying:
«والسارق والسارقة»: 'and among what has been prescribed for you [are] the male thief and the female thief'; these nouns entered only after stories and accounts. Some people read:
«والسارقَ والسارقةَ» in the accusative, and in Arabic this has the strength I mentioned to you; but the generality [of readers] insisted on the nominative." Sībawayh means that in the accusative reading the noun is built upon the verb without relying on what precedes, so the accusative is strong relative to the nominative [in a case] where the noun relies on the omitted preceding [element]. For he has shown that this takes it out of the chapter in which the accusative is chosen; so how could it be understood from him that he preferred it over it? The chapter differs between the two readings, and preference occurs only after equality within the chapter. So the accusative is preferable to the nominative where the noun is built upon the verb, and the nominative is required — we do not say [merely preferred] — where the noun is built upon preceding speech. «[Translator's note: this sentence is somewhat garbled in the print; rendered according to its evident sense.]» Then Sībawayh substantiated this implied [element] by [pointing out] that the speech occurs after stories and reports. If it were as al-Zamakhsharī thought, Sībawayh would not have needed an implied element; rather he would have made it nominative as a mubtadaʾ and made the command its khabar, as al-Zamakhsharī parsed it.
We have summarised this section with commentary on it only because some exegetes thought that Sībawayh prefers the accusative reading without this qualification. The summary of all of this: the accusative is on one ground, namely building the noun upon the imperative verb; and the nominative is on two grounds: one weak, namely [taking it as] a mubtadaʾ with the speech built upon the verb; and the other strong, like the ground for the accusative, namely its being nominative as [part of] a nominal sentence whose [other part] is omitted, indicated by the context. Whenever two grounds for the nominative conflict for us, one strong and the other weak, the reading must be taken on the strong one, as Sībawayh parsed it.

Al-Fakhr al-Rāzī responds:
Al-Fakhr al-Rāzī set out to refute Sībawayh and said: «What Sībawayh held is nothing, and several considerations show its unsoundness.» After lengthy discussion he presented five considerations, which this book has no room to include in full.

Abū Ḥayyān responds to al-Rāzī:
Abū Ḥayyān undertook to refute al-Rāzī, and in his tafsīr al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ he refuted at excessive length the five considerations he had presented. At the end of the discussion he said: «It is astonishing, this man and his boldness toward the sciences, to the point that he composed a book on grammar which he called al-Muḥarrar, and in it followed a strange method, far removed from the terminology of the grammarians and from their aims.» Let the reader refer to this discussion, for it is very fine.

A view of Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī:
We have found that Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī gives a delightful explanation for choosing the nominative, which we include here: He, majestic is His praise, says, in meaning: "whoever steals, man or woman, cut off his hand, O people." For this reason «السارق» and «السارقة» are nominative, because they are not specified; had a specific male thief and female thief been meant, the proper form of speech would have been the accusative.
2- «الأيدي» is plural because each thief has one right hand, which is the one exposed to being cut off for theft; and male thieves have hands, and female thieves have hands; it is as though He said: cut off the right hands of the two kinds. The dual of the pronoun is only for the two kinds.
3- It is reported that a Bedouin heard al-Aṣmaʿī reciting this verse, and he recited at its end: «والله غفور رحيم». The Bedouin denied that this was Quran.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I went back to the muṣḥaf, and it was: «والله عزيز حكيم». When I told the Bedouin that, he said: Yes — He is mighty, so He judged and cut off; had He forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut off. This is one of the lofty leaps of the mind.

dervis-irab:40-41.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): resumptive speech introduced to address the Messenger, though everyone is meant by it, [stating] that He alone disposes of the matters of punishment and of forgiveness for whom He wills. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr) of what follows the negation; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; (تعلم) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (أن) and what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (تعلم). (أن) with its noun; (له), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (ملك السموات) is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (الأرض) is conjoined to the muḍāf ilayhi (السموات); and the nominal clause is the khabar of (أن).
(يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the verbal clause is a second khabar of (أن), or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). Punishment was placed first only because the context is one of threat, so it is fitting to put first the deterrents that suit it. (من) is a relative noun, the object of (يعذب); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); (يغفر) is conjoined to (يعذب); (لمن يشاء) is attached to (يغفر); the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير); and (قدير) is the khabar of (الله).
(يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ): resumptive speech introduced to address the Messenger ﷺ, cautioning him against being affected by what the unbelievers do to grieve him. The parsing of (يا أيها الرسول) has been given many times. (لا) is prohibitive; (يحزنك) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا); the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent); the clause (يسارعون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; and (في الكفر), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يسارعون).
(مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: آمَنَّا بِأَفْواهِهِمْ وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; the clause (آمنا) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); (بأفواههم) is attached to (قالوا), i.e. their saying does not go beyond their mouths; the wāw is circumstantial; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (تؤمن) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (قلوبهم) is the agent; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and (من الذين هادوا) is conjoined to (من الذين قالوا), so it is a ḥāl explaining a single thing. It has also been said: the wāw is resumptive, (من الذين) is a fronted khabar and (سماعون) a delayed mubtadaʾ, so the explanation is of two things. On the first view, «سماعون» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم سماعون» (they are eager listeners). (للكذب) is attached to (سماعون); the second «سماعون» is a badal (substitute) of the first «سماعون» or a tawkīd (emphasis) of it; (لقوم) is attached to «سماعون»; and (آخرين) is an adjective.
(لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ): the clause is a second adjective of (قوم); (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; and (يأتوك) is an imperfect verb in the jussive, with its agent and its direct object.
(يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ): the clause is a third adjective. A muḍāf must be supposed omitted, i.e. "the ruling of the words." (من بعد مواضعه) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "while it is after Allah had set the words in their places." Its meaning may also be "they distort the words from their places," so that «بعد» has been put in place of «عن», as one says «جئتك عن فراغي من الشغل», meaning "after my finishing work." Those meant by them are the Jews.
(يَقُولُونَ: إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هذا فَخُذُوهُ): the clause is a fourth adjective. (يقولون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, the wāw being the agent; (إن) is conditional; (أوتيتم) is a passive past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (هذا) is the second object, the first being the tāʾ, which is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause (خذوه) is in the position of jussive as the apodosis — it was not fit to be an apodosis [without the fāʾ] because it is a request; and the conditional clause is in the position of accusative as the object of saying.
(وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فَاحْذَرُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (تؤتوه) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم), and at the same time it is the protasis; the wāw is the deputy agent and the hāʾ the second object. In (فاحذروا) the fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause (احذروا) is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.
(وَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ فَلَنْ تَمْلِكَ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (يرد) is the protasis; (الله) is the agent; (فتنة) is the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; (تملك) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; (له) is attached to (تملك); (من الله) is attached to an omitted ḥāl from «شيئا», because it was originally an adjective and was placed before it; (شيئا) is a direct object or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar of «من».
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to announce how far the hypocrites have gone
in corruption and how deeply they have plunged into misguidance. The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; (الذين) is the khabar; the clause (لم يرد الله) is the ṣila; (أن) and what falls within its scope is in the position of accusative as the object of (يرد); and (قلوبهم) is the direct object of (يطهر).
(لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا خِزْيٌ وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (في الدنيا) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (خزي) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a second khabar of the demonstrative; and (ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم) is conjoined to what precedes.

dervis-irab:70-71.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): resumptive speech, brought to set out other examples of their crimes, which proclaim that faith is not to be expected of them. The lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); أخذنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ميثاق is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and بني إسرائيل is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَأَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْهِمْ رُسُلًا): the wāw is a conjunction; أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا; and رسلا is a mafʿūl bihi. (كُلَّما جاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ بِما لا تَهْوى أَنْفُسُهُمْ): كلما is an adverb of time that includes the meaning of condition, attached to its omitted apodosis, i.e. "they disobeyed him"; جاءهم is a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and رسول is a delayed fāʿil; بما is attached to جاءهم; and the clause لا تهوى أنفسهم is the ṣila (relative clause). (فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُوا وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ): فريقا is a fronted object of كذبوا, and the second فريقا is a fronted object of يقتلون. The clause is resumptive, arising as the answer to a question that arises from the first apodosis, as though it were said: "What did they do with them?" and it was said: "A party of them they denied, without exposing them to harm, and another party of them they killed." (وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; حسبوا is a verb and its fāʿil; أن is a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; لا is negative; تكون is a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and فتنة is the fāʿil; and أن with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of حسبوا. It has also been read with «تكون» in the nominative, in which case «أن» is lightened from the heavy أنّ, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), its implied form being أنه. (فَعَمُوا وَصَمُّوا ثُمَّ تابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; عموا is conjoined to حسبوا, and صموا is conjoined to His saying فعموا; ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; تاب الله is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to His saying فعموا وصموا; and عليهم is attached to تاب. (ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ): ثم عموا وصموا is conjoined to what preceded; كثير is a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in عموا or صموا; منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كثير; the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and بصير its khabar (predicate); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بصير; and the clause يعملون is the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is a kind of eloquent iltifāt (shift) in His saying: «فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون»: a shift from reporting with the past verb to reporting with the imperfect verb. This is among the subtlest of matters, and it is available in usage only to one who knows the secrets of eloquence and rhetoric.
The Noble Qur'an brims with it. He brought the past verb first, establishing something that had happened; then He brought يقتلون as the narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl māḍiya), to present the killing as hideous and to bring that ghastly scene before the mind, so as to wonder at it and draw the lesson from its folds.
Wondrous instances of it will come in the Qur'an. On this pattern came the saying of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
بأنّي قد لقيت الغول تهوي ... بسهب كالصحيفة صحصحان
فأضربها بلا دهش فخرّت ... صريعا لليدين وللجران
(That I met the ghoul swooping over a plain flat as a page, a bare expanse; and I strike her without alarm, and she fell, felled on her hands and her breast.)
He intended to depict for his people the state that had come upon him until he plucked up courage to strike the ghoul, as though he were embodying it for them, to arouse their admiration at his boldness in that terror. Examples of this are too many to be counted. Of this style is what came in the account of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām at the battle of Badr. He said: "I met ʿUbayda ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ on a horse, wearing complete armour, nothing of him visible but his eyes, saying: 'I am Abū Dhāt al-Kuʾūs.' In my hand was a short spear (ʿanaza) — something like half a spear — and I thrust it into his eye, and he fell; and I tread with my foot on his cheek; the ʿanaza came out bent." His saying «فأطعن بها في عينه، وأطأ برجلي» ("and I thrust it into his eye, and I tread with my foot") is turned from the past form to the imperfect, to represent to the hearer the scene in which he did what he did, in his daring and boldness in killing that armoured horseman.

dervis-irab:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ): the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); and the oath clause is resumptive. كفر الذين is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an omitted oath; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; the clause إن الله is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). inna and its noun; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and المسيح the khabar (predicate) of هو; the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ; ابن is a badal (substitute) for المسيح, and مريم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَقالَ الْمَسِيحُ: يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; قال المسيح is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «قالوا»; يا بني إسرائيل is a vocative in genitive construct (munādā muḍāf); the clause اعبدوا الله is in the position of an accusative as the object of al-Masīḥ's saying; ربي is a badal for الله, and ربكم is conjoined to ربي. (إِنَّهُ مَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ): the clause is resumptive. inna and its noun; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يشرك is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يشرك; the fāʾ links the apodosis; the clause فقد حرم is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من»; and the whole conditional clause is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ. حرم الله is a verb and its fāʿil; عليه is attached to حرّم; and الجنة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَمَأْواهُ النَّارُ وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصارٍ): the wāw is resumptive; مأواه is a fronted khabar and النار a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the reverse is also permissible. The wāw is conjunctive; ما is negative; للظالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and أنصار is genitive in form and nominative in position, because it is a delayed mubtadaʾ.

dervis-irab:73-75.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُؤْفَكُونَ): they are turned away.

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثالِثُ ثَلاثَةٍ): the clause is resumptive, and the lām is in answer to an omitted oath. The clause كفر الذين قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; the clause قالوا is the ṣila (relative clause); inna and its noun, and ثالث ثلاثة is its khabar (predicate); and the clause headed by إنّ is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا إِلهٌ واحِدٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; ما is negative; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; إله is genitive in form and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar is omitted, i.e. "existent"; the second إله is a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in it [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun in the omitted khabar]; and إلا is a particle of restriction. This i'rab has passed in detail in the formula of testimony (kalimat al-shahāda). The meaning is: "while the case is that there is no god existing or present except One God". (وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; إن is conditional; لم ينتهوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينتهوا; and the clause يقولون is the ṣila.
