(لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; يمسّن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كفروا is the ṣila; منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and عذاب أليم is the fāʿil (agent). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, the answer to the oath standing in its place, because the implied form is: ولئن لم ينتهوا; the rule is that when a condition and an oath come together, the answer belongs to whichever comes first. We resorted to this only because of the presence of the lām that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam) [Translator's note: so in the source; in the verse as written that lām is not present, and it is the implied form ولئن that contains it]. (أَفَلا يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive, brought to express wonder at their persistence. The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder and disapproval; the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to something implied, i.e. "Do they not desist, and so not repent?"; إلى الله is attached to يتوبون; يستغفرونه is conjoined to يتوبون; the wāw is circumstantial; الله is a mubtadaʾ, and غفور رحيم are two khabars of it; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. (مَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ): resumptive speech, brought to establish the truth. ما is negative, and it does not operate like ليس because the negation is broken by إلا; المسيح is a mubtadaʾ, and ابن مريم is a badal or a naʿt (adjective); إلا is a particle of restriction; رسول is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause قد خلت is a naʿt; من قبله is attached to خلت, i.e. "passed away and perished"; and الرسل is the fāʿil. (وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ كانا يَأْكُلانِ الطَّعامَ): the wāw is conjunctive; أمه is a mubtadaʾ and صديقة the khabar; the clause كانا is explicative with no grammatical position; the alif of the dual is the noun of كان, the clause يأكلان is the khabar of كانا, and الطعام is a mafʿūl bihi. (انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الْآياتِ ثُمَّ انْظُرْ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ): the clause is resumptive; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; the interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of انظر, «كيف» having suspended «انظر» from operating overtly on what follows it. نبين لهم الآيات is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. ثم is a conjunction of sequence and delay; the meaning is that the clarification of these signs was a wonder, and their turning away from them and their aversion to reflecting on them was more wondrous. أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف, in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; and يؤفكون is an imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «كانا يأكلان الطعام» ("they both used to eat food") there is a kināya (metonymy) for the fact that they both, Allah's blessings be upon them, were human beings, because eating food is followed by digestion and evacuation; so He sufficed with mentioning the eating of food for all this, out of refinement and decorum. This is one of the rare metonymies in the Arabic language. We have said much about kināya before, and here attention must be drawn to the fact that kināya — wherever it occurs — is shared by two aspects, the literal (ḥaqīqa) and the figurative (majāz), and it may be taken in both together, as in the saying of the Exalted: «أو لامستم النساء» ("or you have touched women"). It is permissible to take the kināya there literally or figuratively, and the meaning is sound with each without the expression being impaired. Whoever took it literally, like al-Shāfiʿī, considered touching to be the contact of body with body and made ablution obligatory — and that is the literal sense of touching. Whoever took it figuratively, like Abū Ḥanīfa, considered touching to be intercourse — and that is the figurative sense. More on kināya and its delights will come in this book.
2- Repetition in His saying «انظر» first, and then «ثم انظر» second. In this there is evidence of concern for looking and reflecting, even though the two looks differ: the first concerns how Allah makes the signs clear to His creation, and the second concerns their turning away from them and their aversion to reflecting on their aims and purposes.

dervis-irab:76-77.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لا تَغْلُوا): do not exceed the limit. الغلاء is rising high. Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza al-Yashkurī said in his Muʿallaqa:
أو منعتم ما تسألون فمن حدّ ... ثتموه له علينا الغلاء
(Or if you were denied what you ask, then who is it, you tell of, who has the upper hand over us?)
(الأهواء): plural of هوى, which is what the desire of the soul calls to. Abū ʿUbayda said: «We have not found الهوى used except in the place of evil, because one does not say "فلان يهوى" [Translator's note: i.e. of something good]; rather one says: "he loves good".» When the hāʾ and the wāw are the first and second radicals of a word, they denote the meaning of falling and descending to one side. One says: هوى من الجبل, "he fell from the mountain"; هوت الدلو من البئر هويّا, with fatḥa on the hāʾ, "the bucket fell down the well"; طاح في المهواة والهاوية, "he was flung into the chasm", which is what lies between two mountains; تهاووا فيها, "they fell into it one after another"; هذه هوة عميقة, "this is a deep pit"; «وأمه هاوية» ("his mother will be the abyss"); جلست عنده هويا, i.e. "for a good while"; مضى هوي من الليل, "a portion of the night passed"; and «استهوته الشياطين» ("the devils have lured him"). Among figurative usages is their saying of a coward: إنه الهواء, "he is air", i.e. his heart is empty of boldness. Shawqī seized on this linguistic curiosity and said:
فاتقوا الله في قلوب العذارى ... فالعذارى قلوبهنّ هواء
(Fear Allah concerning the hearts of maidens, for maidens — their hearts are air.)
One says: رجل أهوج, a brave man who throws himself into perils and destruction; ناقة هوجاء, a she-camel as though touched with recklessness, which in her speed does not watch where her hooves fall on the ground; ريح هوجاء and رياح هوج, violent wind(s); هاد الرجل وتهوّد, "the man became a Jew", and هوّد ابنه, "he made his son a Jew"; هوّر البناء فتهوّر, i.e. "it collapsed" — to the end of this material.
All this is among the special features of our noble language.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: أَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا نَفْعاً): resumptive speech, brought to command the Prophet ﷺ to silence them and bind them by the argument. قل is an imperative verb; the hamza is a particle of the interrogative of rebuke and wonder; the clause أتعبدون is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ما is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), though some chose that it be a qualified indefinite noun (nakira mawṣūfa); the clause لا يملك is, on the first view, the ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position, or in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective), and perhaps this is preferable. لكم is attached to يملك; ضرا is the mafʿūl bihi of يملك; and ولا نفعا is conjoined to «ضرا». (وَاللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): the wāw is circumstantial, the link between the ḥāl and its owner being the wāw; the coming of the ḥāl after this speech suits what the situation requires. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, or a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; and السميع العليم are two khabars (predicates) of «الله» or of «هو». Its parallels have preceded. (قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ): the clause of saying is resumptive, and what follows it is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying; لا is prohibitive; تغلوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; في دينكم is attached to تغلوا; غير الحق is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "an exceeding other than the truth"; it may properly be a ḥāl of the agent pronoun, the wāw, i.e. "overstepping the truth". It has been said that the accusative is by connected exception, and it has been said: by disconnected exception. (وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا أَهْواءَ قَوْمٍ قَدْ ضَلُّوا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تتبعوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by «لا»; أهواء is a mafʿūl bihi and قوم a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause قد ضلوا is a naʿt of قوم; من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضلوا, and قبل is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because the adverb is cut off from its genitive construct in wording but not in meaning; أضلوا is conjoined to قد ضلوا, and كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَضَلُّوا عَنْ سَواءِ السَّبِيلِ): conjoined to what preceded.

dervis-irab:78-79.t:
* I'rab:
(لُعِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَلى لِسانِ داوُدَ وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ): the speech is resumptive. لعن is a passive past verb and الذين the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); من بني إسرائيل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); على لسان is attached to لعن — on the singular form of لسان there is an engaging discussion which will come in the section on Benefits; داود is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); عيسى is conjoined to داود; ابن is a badal (substitute) or a naʿt (adjective); and مريم is a muḍāf ilayhi. (ذلِكَ بِما عَصَوْا وَكانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "because of their disobedience"; and the clause is resumptive. ما may also be a relative noun; in either case the clause عصوا has no grammatical position. The clause كانوا is conjoined to عصوا and falls under its ruling; the wāw is the noun of كان, and the clause يعتدون is its khabar. (كانُوا لا يَتَناهَوْنَ عَنْ مُنكَرٍ فَعَلُوهُ): the clause has no grammatical position because it explains the disobedience and transgression; كان and its noun; the clause لا يتناهون is its khabar; عن منكر is attached to يتناهون; and the clause فعلوه is a naʿt of منكر. (لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ): the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; ما is a complete indefinite noun in the position of an accusative as a tamyīz (specification), or a relative noun in the position of a nominative as fāʿil (agent), i.e. "that which they did"; the clause كانوا is a naʿt of ما, or has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; and the clause يفعلون is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
The rebuke of the Jews contained a report of two things extremely ugly and repulsive: the first, the evils they used to commit; the second, their aversion to forbidding one another these evils and to not inclining to them in the future. This is indicated by the saying of the Exalted: «فعلوه» ("which they did"); for were it not mentioned, someone might imagine that forbidding evil is only when it deserves to be forbidden and when one is about to engage in it. So its mention comprises both matters together, in an eloquent manner and a lofty style, which is the summit of eloquence. What is meant by التناهي is not that each one of them should forbid the other the evil he commits, as is the immediate and well-known sense of the form tafāʿul; rather what is meant is merely that forbidding should issue from multiple persons, without regard to each one being both forbidder and forbidden. So failure in mutual forbidding, after it had been commanded, was disobedience.

* Benefits:
The rule says: when two single parts of their two owners are put in genitive construct with both of them without separation, three ways are permissible in them:
1- The plural form; you say: قطعت رؤوس الكبشين ("I cut off the heads of the two rams").
2- The dual form; you say: قطعت رأسي الكبشين.
3- The singular form; you say: قطعت رأس الكبشين.
And His saying in the verse, على لسان داود وعيسى, is in the singular, not the dual or the plural.

dervis-irab:80-81.t:
* I'rab:
(تَرى كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): resumptive speech, brought to address the Prophet concerning the Children of Israel who allied themselves with the disbelievers of the people of Makka.
ترى is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "you"; كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا»; the clause يتولون is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing here is visual; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause). (لَبِئْسَ ما قَدَّمَتْ لَهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ أَنْ سَخِطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, its fāʿil a latent pronoun explained by the word «ما», and «ما» is a complete indefinite noun in the position of an accusative as a tamyīz (specification). «ما» may also be a relative noun in the position of a nominative as fāʿil. The clause of blame has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; the clause قدمت is a naʿt on the first view and the ṣila on the second; لهم is attached to قدمت, and أنفسهم is the fāʿil. أن سخط: أن with what is in its scope is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause of the oath [Translator's note: so in the source; what is meant is the clause of blame, بئس ما قدمت], as though it were said: "Evil is their provision for the Hereafter: Allah's anger with them." Some said: the maṣdar is not the specific object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm), because the anger itself, ascribed to the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be said to be the thing specifically blamed; rather it is the cause of the anger; on this basis they parsed it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. (وَفِي الْعَذابِ هُمْ خالِدُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; في العذاب is attached to «خالدون»; هم is a mubtadaʾ and خالدون the khabar. (وَلَوْ كانُوا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالنَّبِيِّ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ): the wāw is resumptive; لو is conditional; كان and its noun, and the clause يؤمنون is its khabar; بالله is attached to يؤمنون; النبي is conjoined to الله, and ما أنزل إليه is also conjoined. (مَا اتَّخَذُوهُمْ أَوْلِياءَ وَلكِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; أولياء is the second object of اتخذ; and لكنّ with its noun and its khabar.

dervis-irab:82-82.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قِسِّيسِينَ): plural of قسّيس, with kasra on the qāf and a doubled sīn with kasra, meaning القسّ, with fatḥa on the qāf and a doubled sīn: one whose rank is between the bishop and the deacon; he is also the priest (الكاهن). It has the plural قسوس; and قسّيس also has the plurals قسّان, with ḍamma on the qāf, أقسّة and قساوسة. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is like مهالبة; the sīns became many, so they changed one of them into a wāw.
Al-Rāghib said: قسيسين is the plural of قسيس, on the pattern فعّيل, a form of intensity like صدّيق; here it is the head of the Christians and their learned man. Its origin is from تقسّس الشيء, when one follows a thing and seeks it out at night; one says تقسّست أصواتهم, i.e. "I tracked their voices at night". Another said: القسّ, with fatḥa on the qāf, is following a thing; from it the learned man of the Christians was called قسيس, because he follows knowledge. One says قسّ الأثر and قصّه, with ṣād too ("he followed the track"). One says قَس and قِس, with fatḥa and kasra on the qāf, and قسيس. As for Quss ibn Sāʿida al-Iyādī, with ḍamma on the qāf, it is a proper name; it may be one of the forms altered by way of becoming a proper name, its origin being قَس or قِس, with fatḥa or kasra on the qāf. He was the most learned of the people of his time.
(رُهْباناً): it may be singular or plural. When it is plural, its singular is راهب, and راهب is then an active participle from the saying: رهب الله فلان, meaning "so-and-so feared Him", يرهبه رهبا with two fatḥas and رهبا with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ. Among the evidence that it may be a plural among the Arabs is the saying of Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
رهبان مدين والذين عهدتهم ... يبكون من حذر العذاب قعودا
لو يسمعون كما سمعت كلامها ... خرّوا لعزّة ركّعا وسجودا
(The monks of Madyan, and those I knew weeping, seated, for fear of the punishment — if they heard her speech as I heard it, they would fall down before ʿAzza bowing and prostrating.)
الرهبان may also be singular; when it is singular, its plural is رهابين, like قربان and قرابين, and it may also be pluralised as رهابنة when it is so. Among the evidence that it may be a plural among the Arabs [Translator's note: so in the source; the context requires "a singular", as the verse shows] is the saying of the rajaz poet:
لو عاينت رهبان دير في القلل ... لانحدر الرهبان يمشي ونزل
(Had a monk of a monastery on the mountain-tops seen her, the monk would have come down, walking, and descended.)

* I'rab:
(لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ عَداوَةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا): resumptive speech, brought to classify the People of the Book with respect to affection for the believers, to repeat the vile deeds of the Jews, and the gentleness of temper of the Christians and their readiness to yield to the truth. The lām is in answer to an omitted oath; تجدن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; أشد الناس is the first object of تجد; عداوة is a tamyīz (specification); للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشد; اليهود is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the reverse is also permissible; الذين is conjoined to اليهود; and the clause أشركوا is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقْرَبَهُمْ مَوَدَّةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّا نَصارى): the wāw is conjunctive, and the clause is conjoined to what preceded; its i'rab has preceded; and the clause إنا نصارى is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ مِنْهُمْ قِسِّيسِينَ وَرُهْباناً): the clause is resumptive and explanatory; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition; أنّ with what is in its scope is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of ذلك; منهم is attached to the omitted, fronted khabar of أنّ; قسيسين is the noun of أنّ; and رهبانا is conjoined to قسيسين. (وَأَنَّهُمْ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ): conjoined to «بأن منهم», and the clause لا يستكبرون is the khabar of أنّ.
[Volume Three]
[Continuation of Sūrat al-Māʾida]

dervis-irab:1-1.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وفى) with a promise: wafāʾ; and أوفى به, īfāʾ: that is, he brought it complete, with nothing lacking. The poet combined the two:
أما ابن طوف فقد أوفى بذمته ... كما وفى بقلاص النجم حاديها
(As for Ibn Ṭawf, he has fulfilled his pledge, as the driver of the she-camels of the star fulfilled [his duty] toward them.)
Of one who does not give full measure it is said: أخسر الكيل ("he shorted the measure"); and of one who does not fulfil the covenant: غدر ("he betrayed") and نقض ("he broke"). And نقض the covenant and the promise are one and the same thing.
(العقود): the plural of عقد (with fatḥa on the first letter), a verbal noun used as a noun and then pluralised. It is the firmly bound covenant, likened to the tying (ʿaqd) of horses and the like. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
قوم إذا عقدوا عقدا لجارهم ... شدّوا العناج وشدّوا فوقها الكربا
(A people who, when they make a pact for their neighbour, tighten the cord and tighten the knots above it.)
In origin it is applied to solid bodies, such as the knot of a rope and the bonding of a building, and then it is borrowed for abstract things, such as the contract of sale, the covenant and the like. The ʿaqd is therefore more specific than the ʿahd (covenant); and what is meant by العقود is what they bind themselves to by contract.
(البهيمة): every four-legged creature on land and sea; and it was said: whatever has no speech, because of the indistinctness (ibhām) in its voice. But by common usage it is restricted to what is other than beasts of prey and birds. So said al-Rāghib. It is reported from al-Zajjāj that the bahīma, among animals, is whatever has no intellect at all. In al-Qāmūs: the bahīma is every creature with four legs even in water, or every living thing that does not discriminate; its plural is bahāʾim.
(الْأَنْعامِ): these are camels, cattle, sheep and goats, and buffaloes. The annexation of بهيمة to الأنعام is for clarification (li-l-bayān), like "the arāk tree" (شجر الأراك); that is: "the eating of the bahīma that is of the livestock has been made lawful for you". Some held that the annexation is in the sense of comparison, that is: "the bahīma that resembles the livestock has been made lawful for you"; it was said: in chewing the cud and in lacking fangs. It is better to say that the point of resemblance that necessitates lawfulness is that they are among the good things (ṭayyibāt), which are the basis of lawfulness. Al-Ḥarīrī said in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ: "Among that is that they suppose الأنعام to mean النَّعَم; yet the Arabs distinguished between them, making النعم a name for camels specifically, or for the herd in which camels are, and making الأنعام a name for the kinds of livestock, so that some even included in it gazelles and wild asses, clinging to the saying of the Exalted: «أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام»." Al-Rāghib said: النعم is specific to camels, and its plural is أنعام. They were so named because they are among the greatest blessings (niʿam) in their eyes. But الأنعام is said of camels, cattle and sheep and goats, and it is not called أنعام unless camels are among its number." Ibn Barrī said: it is a case of predominance (taghlīb), since they gave النعم predominance over the rest; and there is in reality no difference between them, and it is all-inclusive.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to call for fulfilment of what the contract requires. The i'rab of the vocative has already been given. أوفوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; بالعقود is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوفوا.
(أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعامِ) The sentence is explicative, because it is a detailing after a general statement, on the basis that العقود includes all the rulings that Allah the Exalted has legislated and commanded those under obligation to fulfil. أحلت is a passive past verb; ولكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحلت; وبهيمة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and الأنعام is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(إِلَّا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ) إلا is a particle of exception, and ما is the excepted. It was said: it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), because the expression is not of the genus of the bahīma, and the prohibition is due to something that supervenes, such as death and the like. The sentence يتلى عليكم is the ṣila of the relative. غير is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم»; ومحلي is a muḍāf to «غير», and الصيد is a muḍāf ilayhi to «محلي». The sentence وأنتم حرم, of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is a ḥāl from «محلي الصيد», as if it were said: "We have made lawful for you some of the livestock while you refrain from game, being in iḥrām, so that there be no hardship upon you."
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ ما يُرِيدُ) The sentence gives the reason for the ruling. إن and its ism; the sentence يحكم is its khabar. ما may be a maṣdar particle or a relative, and in either case it is accusative by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), that is: "He rules by His will," or "by that which He wills"; and there is no frivolity in His rulings, nor any defect, nor any injustice.

* Benefits:
The scholars and exegetes expounded at length on what is meant by العقود. In our view it is general, comprising all the covenants of Allah that He entrusted to His servants, of acts of worship and dealings, by which the affairs of this world and the next are together ordered. Fine is the saying of al-Rāghib:
"Contracts, with regard to the thing contracted and the contracting party, are of three kinds: a contract between Allah the Exalted and the servant, a contract between the servant and himself, and a contract between the servant and others among mankind."
The jurists and the scholars of legislation have gone into it extensively, composing long works on it and treating the legal rulings relating to it, which are easy to consult in their proper places.

An eloquent sentence:
The foundation on which contracts rest in Islam is this eloquent, concise and meaningful sentence, «أوفوا بالعقود». It indicates, with force and grace, that every believer must fulfil what he has contracted and bound himself to, and that no one may restrict what the Lawgiver has left unrestricted except by a text from Him. Every saying or deed that people count as a contract is a contract that they must fulfil, as Allah the Exalted commanded, provided it does not involve forbidding what is lawful or permitting what is forbidden, of what is established in the Sharia, such as a contract under compulsion, or to burn someone's house or a tree in an orchard, or for an indecency, or to consume some of people's property wrongfully, such as usury, gambling (maysir) and bribery.

Custom and mutual consent:
All worldly matters are ordered under this, such as sale, hire, partnerships and other worldly dealings. The basis in them is people's custom and their mutual consent, so long as it does not contradict a ruling of the Sharia. This is perfectly clear and firm. Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyya composed a book called «Madārik al-Qiyās» on the subject of contracts, in which he covered this subject exhaustively, supported by evidence from the Book, the Sunna and the reports of the righteous predecessors; let whoever wishes consult it.

A report on the philosopher al-Kindī:
They mention that the philosopher al-Kindī was told by his companions: "O sage, make for us the like of this Qur'an." He said: "Yes, I shall make the like of part of it." Then he withdrew for many days, and came out and said: "By Allah, I cannot, and no one can bear it. I opened the Mushaf and Sūrat al-Māʾida came out. I looked, and behold, it speaks of fulfilment, forbids breach of faith, makes lawful with a general permission, then makes an exception, then tells of His power and wisdom, in two lines. No one can produce the like of this except in volumes (ajlād)."
That is, in many large volumes.

dervis-irab:2-2.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الشعائر): the plural of شعيرة, which is the mark or sign. It was then made a sign for the rites of the Hajj and its ceremonies.
(الهدي): what is sent as a gift to the Kaʿba, to be slaughtered there and by which one draws near to Allah. He said:
يقولون: من هذا الغريب بأرضنا ... أما والهدايا إنني لغريب
(They say: "Who is this stranger in our land?" By the sacrificial gifts, I am indeed a stranger.)
(القلائد): the plural of قلادة, which is what is hung on the neck. They used to hang on the necks of the camels of the hady a sandal, or a rope, or the loop of a water-skin, or tree bark and the like, so that it would be recognised and no one would molest it. It is therefore on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, that is: "and the owners of the garlands" (ولأصحاب القلائد).
(آمِّينَ) with shadda on the mīm, which has kasra, that is: "heading for, intending".
(يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ): the imperfect of جرمه الشيء, when he made him bear it and caused him to commit it; that is, to earn it and do it. It runs in the course of «كسب» ("to earn") in taking one object or two.
(الشنآن): intensity of hatred. One says شنئت الرجل أشنؤه, that is, "I hated him". This maṣdar is transmitted (samāʿī) and contrary to the analogical rule in two respects: its verb is transitive and its middle radical is vowelled with kasra, since it is analogical only in intransitive verbs vowelled with fatḥa. It has many maṣdars, which some counted up to thirteen, the best known of which are: شنئا, شنئا, شنئا, شنأة, شنآنا, شنآنا, مشنأ, مشنأة and مشنوءة. [Translator's note: the source prints the first three forms, and the fourth and fifth, identically, because the vowel marks that distinguish them are missing; they are rendered as printed.]

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ) The i'rab of «يا أيها الذين آمنوا» has been given many times. لا is prohibitive, and تحلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive because of it, the wāw being the fāʿil; and شعائر الله is the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرامَ وَلَا الْهَدْيَ وَلَا الْقَلائِدَ وَلَا آمِّينَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرامَ)
ولا الشهر الحرام is conjoined to شعائر, and الحرام is a naʿt of الشهر. It is the month of the Hajj, which is Dhū al-Qaʿda; al-Ṭabarī insisted that it is Rajab. What follows it is also conjoined to it. ولا آمّين: that is, "and do not violate [the sanctity of] a people heading for ..." (ولا تحلوا قوما آمّين); it is thus a naʿt of an omitted modified noun, and the meaning is: "do not make fighting them lawful so long as they are making for the Sacred House." This is a symbol of the peace to which the Qur'an called. And البيت is the mafʿūl of آمّين, because it is an active participle.
(يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرِضْواناً) The sentence is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «آمّين», that is: "while those heading there are seeking bounty". And فضلا is a mafʿūl bihi; ومن ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبتغون, or to an omitted naʿt of «فضلا»; and رضوانا is conjoined to it.
(وَإِذا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطادُوا) The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the sentence حللتم is in the position of the genitive by annexation; the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; and اصطادوا ...
(وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; ويجرمنكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the jussive because of لا, and the kāf is its first object; وشنآن قوم is the fāʿil. أن صدوكم is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, being the reason for the hatred and attached to it; وعن المسجد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to صدوكم. أن تعتدوا is an interpreted maṣdar, the second object of يجرمنكم. The meaning is: "Let not hatred of a people, because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, earn you transgression, nor make you bear it" (ولا يكسبنكم بغض قوم لأنهم صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام الاعتداء ولا يحملنكم عليه).
(وَتَعاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوى) The wāw is a conjunction; وتعاونوا is an imperative verb, the wāw being the fāʿil; وعلى البر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعاونوا; and التقوى is conjoined to البر.
(وَلا تَعاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; وتعاونوا is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been omitted, jussive because of لا, that is: لا تتعاونوا; وعلى الإثم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; and العدوان is conjoined to it.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ) Also a conjunction; and the sentence of إن with its ism and khabar has no grammatical position, because it is a giving of reasons.

* Benefits:
The Arabs were agreed on honouring Dhū al-Qaʿda and Dhū al-Ḥijja, and differed about Rajab, so the Exalted made His command strict. This is the reason for singling it out by mention.
It was also said that الشهر is a singular defined by the generic al-, so that what is meant is all the sacred months, which are Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja, Muḥarram and Rajab.

dervis-irab:3-3.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ): ihlāl is raising the voice with it for other than Allah, which is their saying at the slaughter: "In the name of al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā". One says "so-and-so made ihlāl for the Hajj" (أهلّ فلان بالحج) when he raised his voice in the talbiya; and from it comes "the infant cried out" (استهلّ الصبيّ) when he raises his voice in crying at birth.
(الْمُنْخَنِقَةُ): the author of al-Qāmūs said: خنقه خنقا (like كتف), so he is خنق; and the sheep انخنقت by itself. The rule of the reflexive-passive (muṭāwaʿa) does not apply to this verb; the muṭāwiʿ is rather اختنق. On this basis المنخنقة includes the animal they strangled until it died, or that was strangled by some cause; the details are in the books of fiqh.
(الْمَوْقُوذَةُ): the one they beat severely with a stick or a blunt stone until it died. He said in al-Qāmūs: al-waqdh is severity of beating. And he said in its commentary, Tāj al-ʿArūs: the mawqūdha is the one that is killed with a stick or stones with no edge, until its strength dissolves and it dies. The torment of the animal contained in waqdh is not hidden.
(الْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ): the one that fell from a high place and died.
(النَّطِيحَةُ): the one that another gored and which died from the goring.
An enjoyable discussion of this form will come in the section on Benefits.
(ذَكَّيْتُمْ): that is, you reached its slaughter while it was still convulsing and its jugular veins were gushing.
Dhakāt and tadhkiya in the original language mean the completion of a particular act. One says: ذكت النار تذكو ذكوّا وذكا وذكاء when its kindling is complete; ذكت الشمس when its heat became intense; and ذكى and ذكي (like رمى and رضي) when his sharp-wittedness was complete. He said in al-Lisān: "al-dhakāʾ is the intensity of the blaze of fire. One says ذكيت النار when you completed its kindling and raised it; and al-dhakā is the completion of kindling a fire, shortened (maqṣūr), written with alif." And dhakāʾ in understanding is for the understanding to be complete and quick to accept.
(النُّصُبِ): al-Rāghib said in his Mufradāt: naṣb of a thing is setting it up so that it projects, like setting up a spear, a building or a stone; and al-naṣīb is stones set up over something, its plural being naṣāʾib and nuṣub (with two ḍammas). The Arabs had stones that they worshipped and slaughtered upon. He said: «كأنّهم إلى نصب يوفضون» ("as though they were rushing to a goal"). Its plural is sometimes said to be anṣāb. And he said in al-Lisān: "al-naṣb (with fatḥa), al-nuṣb (with ḍamma) and al-nuṣub (with two ḍammas) mean sickness, affliction and evil, and in the Revelation: «مسّني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب» ("Satan has touched me with hardship and torment"). And al-naṣība and al-nuṣub (with two ḍammas) are everything set up and made into a sign. So al-nuṣub is both singular and plural." Al-Aʿshā said:
وذا النّصب المنصوب لا تعبدنّه ... لعاقبة والله ربّك فاعبدا
(And the erected stone idol, do not worship it for any outcome; but worship Allah, your Lord.)
Its use today for the commemorative monument (al-naṣb al-tadhkārī) is sound and open to no objection.
(الأزلام): the plural of zalam, with two fatḥas, or like ṣurad, that is, with ḍamma then fatḥa: a small arrow-shaft without feathers or head. These were arrows by which they sought a division of fortune in the Jāhiliyya; its plural is azlām. When one of them wished to travel, raid, trade, marry, or undertake an important matter, he struck the shafts, that is, he shook them. There were three, written on one of which: "My Lord has commanded me"; on the second: "My Lord has forbidden me"; and the third was blank, with nothing on it. If the commanding one came out, he went ahead with his purpose (ṭiyya), that is, the intention he had formed; if the forbidding one came out, he did not act and held back; and if the blank came out, he repeated the casting of lots.
(المخمصة): famine.
(مُتَجانِفٍ): deviating, inclining, from al-janaf, which is inclination and injustice.

* I'rab:
(حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ الْخِنْزِيرِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain what He stated in general terms earlier, namely His saying the Exalted: «إلا ما يتلى عليكم».
حرمت is a passive past verb; وعليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حرمت; والميتة is the nāʾib fāʿil; and الدم and لحم الخنزير are conjoined to الميتة.
(وَما أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ) Also a conjunction. ما is a relative noun; أهل is a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil being "he" (هو); the sentence is the ṣila of the relative; ولغير الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أهل; and به is likewise attached to أهلّ.
(وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَالنَّطِيحَةُ وَما أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ) All of these are conjoined, entering into the ruling of the forbidden things.
(إِلَّا ما ذَكَّيْتُمْ) إلا is a particle of exception; ما is a relative noun, the excepted, connected (muttaṣil), accusative; the sentence ذكيتم is the ṣila of the relative; and the sentence of exception is a ḥāl clause.
(وَما ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ) The sentence is conjoined to the forbidden things.
(وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُوا بِالْأَزْلامِ) The interpreted maṣdar is also conjoined, that is: "and seeking division by the divining arrows is forbidden to you" (وحرم عليكم الاستقسام بالأزلام).
(ذلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ) A mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the sentence is resumptive. The demonstrative refers specifically to seeking division by the divining arrows; and it was said: to everything that has preceded.
(الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ دِينِكُمْ) اليوم is an adverb of time attached to يئس, and by it He meant time in the general sense, not one particular day, in line with the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī:
الآن لما ابيضّ مسربتي ... وعضضت من نابي على جذم
حلبت هذا الدهر أشطره ... وأتيت ما آتي على علم
(Now that my chest-hair has turned white, and I have bitten down on a stump where my canine was, I have milked the teats of this age, and I do what I do with knowledge.)
By his word «الآن» he meant the present time. The masraba is the hair of the chest, which is the last part of a person to turn grey; so the whitening of the masraba is a metonymy for his reaching the end of the course in greying and the close of the circuit of life. The meaning of the two verses: it has become my habit to do what I do with knowledge I have from the length of my experience of the events of time. The sentence is resumptive; الذين is a relative noun, the fāʿil; the sentence كفروا is the ṣila; and ومن دينكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يئس, that is: "of nullifying the matter of your religion".
(فَلا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ) The fāʾ is the eloquent one (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); لا is prohibitive; وتخشوهم is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لا; واخشوني is an imperative verb with its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; and the sentence has no grammatical position.
(الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ) اليوم is an adverb of time attached to أكملت; ولكم is likewise attached to it; ودينكم is the mafʿūl bihi of أكملت; and the sentence is resumptive.
(وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي) Conjoined to what has preceded; وعليكم is attached to أتممت; and نعمتي is the mafʿūl bihi of أتممت.
(وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلامَ دِيناً) The wāw is resumptive; رضيت is a verb and fāʿil; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt of «دينا»; and دينا is a mafʿūl bihi or a tamyīz, because the meaning of رضيت is "I made" (جعلت). If it is in the sense of being pleased, then «دينا» is a ḥāl from الإسلام and لكم is attached to رضيت.
(فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ) The fāʾ is resumptive; من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, a mubtadaʾ; اضطر is a passive past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, its nāʾib fāʿil being "he", referring to من; and في مخمصة is attached to اضطر.
(غَيْرَ مُتَجانِفٍ لِإِثْمٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) غير متجانف is accusative as a ḥāl; ولإثم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to متجانف; the fāʾ links the apodosis; and إن with its ism and its two khabars [Translator's note: the source says «وخبراها» ("its two khabars"), meaning غفور and رحيم]; the sentence joined by the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

* Benefits:
When the form faʿīl has the sense of mafʿūl, masculine and feminine are alike in it, and no feminine marker is attached to it. The Arabs say: ʿayn kaḥīl, not kaḥīla ("a kohl-darkened eye"), and kaff khaḍīb, not khaḍība ("a henna-dyed palm"). How, then, was the tāʾ attached to «نطيحة» when it has the sense of manṭūḥa? It has been said in reply that the tāʾ here is for transfer from the adjectival to the nominal, or that faʿīl here has the sense of fāʿil, as if He had said: "and the goring one that dies from goring", that is, it gores another and the other gores it, and it dies. The Kufans said: attaching the tāʾ to faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl is prevented only when it is an adjective of a mentioned modified noun, as in ʿayn kaḥīl; but when the modified noun has not been mentioned before, attaching the tāʾ is not prevented. This is a fine explanation, for "dhabīḥa" and "naṭīḥa" and the like, when no modified noun precedes them, would not be known to be masculine or feminine. For example: "I saw a wounded one" (رأيت جريحة). But when it is known, no: for example, "I saw a wounded woman" (رأيت امرأة جريحا), or "I saw a wounded female cast on the road" (رأيت جريحا ملقاة في الطريق).
